about: Error replies of Redis Open Source and its bundled modules, extracted from the source code of the versions below and partly checked against a running server.

errors.message: ASK <slot> <endpoint>:<port>
errors.explain: The key's hash slot, shown in the message, is moving to the node at the address in the message, and the key may already be there. Send `ASKING` and then the command to that node, once. Cluster-aware clients do this for you.

errors.message: BUSY <message>
errors.explain: A module command has been running for a long time and blocks the server, and the text after `BUSY` comes from that module. Wait for the command to finish and retry. `SHUTDOWN NOSAVE` still works if you need to stop the server.

errors.message: BUSY Redis is busy running a module command.
errors.explain: A module command has been running for a long time and blocks the server, so it accepts only a few commands. Wait for it to finish and retry. No command can stop it, apart from stopping the server with `SHUTDOWN NOSAVE`.

errors.message: BUSY Redis is busy running a script. You can only call FUNCTION KILL or SHUTDOWN NOSAVE.
errors.explain: A function, run with `FCALL`, has run longer than `busy-reply-threshold` and blocks the server. Stop it with `FUNCTION KILL` if it hasn't written any data yet, or wait for it. `SHUTDOWN NOSAVE` stops the server without saving.

errors.message: BUSY Redis is busy running a script. You can only call SCRIPT KILL or SHUTDOWN NOSAVE.
errors.explain: A Lua script, run with `EVAL` or `EVALSHA`, has run longer than `busy-reply-threshold` and blocks the server. Stop it with `SCRIPT KILL` if it hasn't written any data yet, or wait for it. `SHUTDOWN NOSAVE` stops the server without saving.

errors.message: BUSYGROUP Consumer Group name already exists
errors.explain: `XGROUP CREATE` named a consumer group that already exists on this stream. Use the existing group, choose another name, or delete the group first with `XGROUP DESTROY`. Apps that create their groups at startup often treat this error as success.

errors.message: BUSYKEY Target key name already exists.
errors.explain: `RESTORE` won't overwrite a key that already exists. Add the `REPLACE` option to overwrite it, or delete the key first.

errors.message: CLUSTERDOWN Hash slot not served
errors.explain: The command uses a key whose hash slot isn't assigned to any node, so no node can serve it. Check the slot coverage with `CLUSTER SLOTS`, and assign the missing slots with `CLUSTER ADDSLOTS` or `CLUSTER ADDSLOTSRANGE`.

errors.message: CLUSTERDOWN The cluster is down
errors.explain: The cluster is in the failed state, for example because some hash slots have no working node, so this node refuses commands that use keys. Fix the failed nodes or the slot coverage. To keep serving reads meanwhile, set `cluster-allow-reads-when-down` to `yes`.

errors.message: CLUSTERDOWN The cluster is down and only accepts read commands
errors.explain: The cluster is in the failed state, and because `cluster-allow-reads-when-down` is `yes`, this node still serves reads but refuses writes. Fix the failed nodes or the slot coverage, then retry the write.

errors.message: CROSSSLOT Keys in request don't hash to the same slot
errors.explain: The command uses several keys that belong to different hash slots, which a cluster can't serve in one command. Put the keys in the same slot with a hash tag, such as `{user1}:name` and `{user1}:email`, or send one command per key.

errors.message: DENIED Redis is running in protected mode because protected mode is enabled and no password is set for the default user. In this mode connections are only accepted from the loopback interface. If you want to connect from external computers to Redis you may adopt one of the following solutions: 1) Just disable protected mode sending the command 'CONFIG SET protected-mode no' from the loopback interface by connecting to Redis from the same host the server is running, however MAKE SURE Redis is not publicly accessible from internet if you do so. Use CONFIG REWRITE to make this change permanent. 2) Alternatively you can just disable the protected mode by editing the Redis configuration file, and setting the protected mode option to 'no', and then restarting the server. 3) If you started the server manually just for testing, restart it with the '--protected-mode no' option. 4) Set up an authentication password for the default user. NOTE: You only need to do one of the above things in order for the server to start accepting connections from the outside.
errors.explain: Redis refused your connection because protected mode is on, the default user has no password, and you connected from another computer. Set a password for the default user, or turn off `protected-mode` only if the server can't be reached from the internet.

errors.message: EXECABORT Transaction discarded because of previous errors.
errors.explain: Redis refused one of the commands you queued after `MULTI`, for example because of a typo or a wrong number of arguments, so `EXEC` discarded the whole transaction. Check the error that each queued command returned, fix that command, and send the transaction again.

errors.message: EXECABORT Transaction discarded because of: <error>
errors.example: EXECABORT Transaction discarded because of: NOPERM User vexec has no permissions to run the 'exec' command
errors.explain: Redis refused the `EXEC` itself for the reason after the colon, such as missing permissions, low memory, or a read-only replica, and discarded the transaction without running any of its commands. Fix that cause, then send the whole transaction again.

errors.message: INPROG Failover already in progress
errors.explain: You ran `SENTINEL FAILOVER`, but a failover of that primary is already running. Wait for it to finish, then check the new primary with `SENTINEL GET-MASTER-ADDR-BY-NAME`.

errors.message: INVALIDOBJ Corrupted HLL object detected
errors.explain: The HyperLogLog stored in the key is corrupted, usually because a string command such as `SETRANGE` or `APPEND` changed its bytes. Delete the key and add the elements again with `PFADD`.

errors.message: IOERR error or timeout connecting to the client
errors.explain: `MIGRATE` couldn't connect to the target server within the timeout. Despite the wording, client means the target server. Check its host and port, that it's running, and that this server can reach it.

errors.message: IOERR error or timeout reading to target instance
errors.explain: `MIGRATE` connected to the target server, but reading its reply failed or took longer than the timeout. Check that the target is healthy, and pass a longer timeout for large keys.

errors.message: IOERR error or timeout writing to target instance
errors.explain: `MIGRATE` connected to the target server, but sending the data failed or took longer than the timeout. Check the network and the target server, and pass a longer timeout for large keys.

errors.message: LOADING Redis is loading the dataset in memory
errors.explain: Redis is loading its data into memory, after a restart or from its primary, and can't run this command yet. Wait and retry. `INFO persistence` shows the loading progress.

errors.message: MASTERDOWN Link with MASTER is down and replica-serve-stale-data is set to 'no'.
errors.explain: This replica lost its link to the primary, and `replica-serve-stale-data` is `no`, so it refuses commands that read or write data. Wait for the link to recover and check the primary and the network, or set `replica-serve-stale-data` to `yes` to serve possibly outdated data.

errors.message: MASTERDOWN Link with MASTER is down, replica-serve-stale-data is set to 'no' and 'allow-stale' flag is not set on the script.
errors.explain: This replica lost its link to the primary, `replica-serve-stale-data` is `no`, and your script or function doesn't have the `allow-stale` flag. Wait for the link to recover, or add `allow-stale` if the code can safely run on outdated data.

errors.message: MISCONF Errors writing to the AOF file: <reason>
errors.explain: Redis couldn't write or sync its append-only file (AOF), so it refuses write commands and `PING` until a write succeeds. The end of the message gives the operating system's reason, such as a full disk; once you fix it, Redis accepts writes again.

errors.message: MISCONF Errors writing to the AOF file: <reason> script: <script>, on <source>:<line>.
errors.explain: Your script tried to write while Redis can't write to its append-only file (AOF), for the reason shown, such as a full disk. Redis refuses writes until the AOF works again, so fix the cause that the Redis log gives, then retry.

errors.message: MISCONF Redis is configured to persist data to AOF, but it's currently unable to persist to disk. Writable scripts are blocked. Use 'no-writes' flag for read only scripts. AOF error: <reason>
errors.explain: Redis can't write to its append-only file (AOF), for the reason at the end of the message, so it refuses scripts and functions that may write. Fix the disk problem; if the code only reads, add the `no-writes` flag so it can still run.

errors.message: MISCONF Redis is configured to save RDB snapshots, but it's currently unable to persist to disk. Commands that may modify the data set are disabled, because this instance is configured to report errors during writes if RDB snapshotting fails (stop-writes-on-bgsave-error option). Please check the Redis logs for details about the RDB error.
errors.explain: The last background snapshot (RDB file) failed, and `stop-writes-on-bgsave-error` is `yes`, so Redis refuses write commands and `PING`. Check the Redis log for the reason and fix it, then run `BGSAVE`; writes work again once a snapshot succeeds.

errors.message: MISCONF Redis is configured to save RDB snapshots, but it's currently unable to persist to disk. Commands that may modify the data set are disabled, because this instance is configured to report errors during writes if RDB snapshotting fails (stop-writes-on-bgsave-error option). Please check the Redis logs for details about the RDB error. script: <script>, on <source>:<line>.
errors.explain: Your script tried to write after the last snapshot failed, and `stop-writes-on-bgsave-error` makes Redis refuse writes until saving works again. Find the reason in the Redis log, fix it, and run `BGSAVE`; when it succeeds, writes work again.

errors.message: MISCONF Redis is configured to save RDB snapshots, but it's currently unable to persist to disk. Writable scripts are blocked. Use 'no-writes' flag for read only scripts.
errors.explain: The last snapshot failed, and `stop-writes-on-bgsave-error` is on, so Redis refuses scripts and functions that may write. Fix the cause that the Redis log gives and run `BGSAVE`; if the code only reads, add the `no-writes` flag so it can still run.

errors.message: MOVED <slot> <endpoint>:<port>
errors.explain: The key's hash slot, shown in the message, is served by another node, at the address in the message. Send the command to that node. Cluster-aware clients follow this redirect and update their slot map for you.

errors.message: NOAUTH Authentication required.
errors.explain: The server requires a password, and this connection hasn't authenticated yet. Send `AUTH` with your password, or with your user name and password, before other commands, or set them in your client's connection settings.

errors.message: NOAUTH HELLO must be called with the client already authenticated, otherwise the HELLO <proto> AUTH <user> <pass> option can be used to authenticate the client and select the RESP protocol version at the same time
errors.explain: The server requires authentication, and you sent `HELLO` on a connection that hasn't authenticated. Add `AUTH` with a user name and password to the same command, as in `HELLO 3 AUTH default mypassword`, or run `AUTH` first.

errors.message: NOGOODSLAVE No suitable replica to promote
errors.explain: You ran `SENTINEL FAILOVER`, but no replica of the primary can be promoted: there are none, or they're down, disconnected, not answering, or have `replica-priority` set to 0. Check the replicas with `SENTINEL REPLICAS`.

errors.message: NOGROUP No such consumer group '<group>' for key name '<key>'
errors.explain: The stream named in the message has no consumer group with that name. Check the group name, which is case-sensitive, or create the group with `XGROUP CREATE`; `XINFO GROUPS` lists the existing groups.

errors.message: NOGROUP No such key '<key>' or consumer group '<group>'
errors.explain: Either the stream key doesn't exist, or it has no consumer group with that name. Check both names, and create the group with `XGROUP CREATE`, adding `MKSTREAM` if the stream doesn't exist yet.

errors.message: NOGROUP No such key '<key>' or consumer group '<group>' in XREADGROUP with GROUP option
errors.example: NOGROUP No such key 's' or consumer group 'nog' in XREADGROUP with GROUP option
errors.explain: `XREADGROUP` can't read, because the stream key doesn't exist or has no group with that name. Create the group with `XGROUP CREATE`, with `MKSTREAM` if needed. Groups are lost when the stream key is deleted, for example when it expires.

errors.message: NOMASTERLINK Can't SYNC while failing over
NOMASTERLINK Can't SYNC while not connected with my master
NOPERM ACLs rules changed between the moment the transaction was accumulated and the EXEC call. This command is no longer allowed for the following reason: no permission
errors.explain: The access control list (ACL) rules for your user changed between queueing this command and `EXEC`, and the user can no longer run it. Redis skips that command but runs the others in the transaction; restore the permission or update your app, then retry.

errors.message: NOPERM ACLs rules changed between the moment the transaction was accumulated and the EXEC call. This command is no longer allowed for the following reason: no permission to access one of the channels used as arguments
errors.explain: The access control list (ACL) rules for your user changed after you queued this command, and the user can no longer use one of its Pub/Sub channels. Redis skips that command but runs the rest of the transaction; grant the channel with `ACL SETUSER`, or remove the command.

errors.message: NOPERM ACLs rules changed between the moment the transaction was accumulated and the EXEC call. This command is no longer allowed for the following reason: no permission to execute the command or subcommand
errors.explain: The access control list (ACL) rules for your user changed after you queued this command, and the user can no longer run that command or subcommand. Redis skips it but runs the rest of the transaction; grant the command with `ACL SETUSER`, or remove it.

errors.message: NOPERM ACLs rules changed between the moment the transaction was accumulated and the EXEC call. This command is no longer allowed for the following reason: no permission to touch the specified keys
errors.explain: The access control list (ACL) rules for your user changed after you queued this command, and the user can no longer access one of the keys it uses. Redis skips it but runs the rest of the transaction; grant the key pattern with `ACL SETUSER`, or remove the command.

errors.message: NOPERM No permissions to access a channel
errors.explain: Your user's access control list (ACL) rules don't allow the channel you used, for example in `PUBLISH` or `SUBSCRIBE`. Run `ACL LOG` to see which channel was refused, then allow it with a `&` pattern in `ACL SETUSER`.

errors.message: NOPERM No permissions to access a key
errors.explain: Your user's access control list (ACL) rules don't allow a key in the command, or the read or write access the command needs. Run `ACL LOG` to see which key was refused, then allow it with a `~` or `%` pattern in `ACL SETUSER`.

errors.message: NOPERM User <username> has no permissions to run the '<command>' command
errors.example: NOPERM User vuser1 has no permissions to run the 'set' command
errors.explain: The user in the message is authenticated but isn't allowed to run that command. Connect as a user that has the permission, or allow the command with `ACL SETUSER`, for example `+set` or a category such as `+@write`.

errors.message: NOPROTO unsupported protocol version
errors.explain: You asked `HELLO` for a protocol version that Redis doesn't support. Redis supports versions 2 and 3, so send `HELLO 2` or `HELLO 3`.

errors.message: NOQUORUM <count> usable Sentinels. Not enough available Sentinels to reach the majority and authorize a failover
errors.explain: `SENTINEL CKQUORUM` found that a majority of the Sentinels that know this primary isn't reachable, so they couldn't authorize a failover. The number in the message counts the reachable Sentinels, including this one; bring the others back or fix the network between them.

errors.message: NOQUORUM <count> usable Sentinels. Not enough available Sentinels to reach the specified quorum for this master
errors.explain: `SENTINEL CKQUORUM` found fewer reachable Sentinels than the quorum set for this primary, so they couldn't agree that it's down. The number in the message counts the reachable Sentinels, including this one; start more Sentinels, fix their connections, or lower the quorum with `SENTINEL SET`.

errors.message: NOQUORUM <count> usable Sentinels. Not enough available Sentinels to reach the specified quorum for this master. Not enough available Sentinels to reach the majority and authorize a failover
errors.explain: `SENTINEL CKQUORUM` found too few reachable Sentinels to reach this primary's quorum or to form the majority that authorizes a failover. The number in the message counts the reachable Sentinels, including this one; bring more Sentinels online or fix the network.

errors.message: NOREPLICAS Not enough good replicas to write.
errors.explain: The primary has fewer connected replicas than `min-replicas-to-write` requires, counting only those whose lag is within `min-replicas-max-lag` seconds, so it refuses writes. Check your replicas with `INFO replication`, or lower `min-replicas-to-write`.

errors.message: NOREPLICAS Not enough good replicas to write. script: <script>, on <source>:<line>.
errors.explain: Your script tried to write while the primary has fewer good replicas than `min-replicas-to-write` requires, so Redis refused the write. Check your replicas with `INFO replication`, or lower `min-replicas-to-write`.

errors.message: NOSCRIPT No matching script. Please use EVAL.
errors.explain: You called `EVALSHA` with a digest that isn't in the script cache, or isn't 40 characters long. The cache empties on restart, failover, and `SCRIPT FLUSH`, and Redis evicts old `EVAL` scripts, so load the script again with `SCRIPT LOAD` or `EVAL`, then retry.

errors.message: NOTBUSY No scripts in execution right now.
errors.explain: You ran `SCRIPT KILL` or `FUNCTION KILL`, but no script or function is running, so there's nothing to stop. It may have finished already.

errors.message: NOTREADY Cluster is not ready to migrate slots
errors.explain: The source node isn't ready to start moving the slots yet, so the importing node tries again later by itself. You see this only in logs. If it doesn't clear, check the source node's log.

errors.message: OOM allow-oom flag is not set on the script, can not run it when used memory > 'maxmemory'
errors.explain: Redis is over its `maxmemory` limit, and the script or function you called has neither the `allow-oom` nor the `no-writes` flag. Free memory or raise `maxmemory`; if the code only reads, add `no-writes` so it can run anyway.

errors.message: OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory'.
errors.explain: Redis has reached its `maxmemory` limit and couldn't free enough memory by evicting keys, so it refuses commands that can add data. Delete keys you don't need, raise `maxmemory`, or set a `maxmemory-policy` that can evict your keys.

errors.message: OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory'. script: <script>, on <source>:<line>.
errors.example: OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory'. script: 6b64f6d4bd85beea43401f8cc6038a28561fbdbd, on @user_script:1.
errors.explain: Your script called a command that can add data while Redis is over its `maxmemory` limit and can't evict keys to make room. Free memory, raise `maxmemory`, or choose a `maxmemory-policy` that evicts keys, then retry.

errors.message: READONLY Can not run script with write flag on readonly replica
errors.explain: You called a script or function without the `no-writes` flag on a read-only replica, which refuses anything that may write. Send it to the primary, or add `no-writes` if the code only reads.

errors.message: READONLY You can't write against a read only replica.
errors.explain: You sent a write command to a replica, which accepts only reads while `replica-read-only` is `yes`. Send writes to the primary. After a failover, your client may still be connected to a node that has become a replica.

errors.message: READONLY You can't write against a read only replica. script: <script>, on <source>:<line>.
errors.explain: Your script called a command that writes, but the server is a read-only replica. Send scripts that write to the primary, and run only read-only scripts on replicas, for example with `EVAL_RO`.

errors.message: TRYAGAIN Multiple keys request during rehashing of slot
errors.explain: The command uses several keys in a hash slot that's moving between nodes, and not all of the keys are on this node. Wait a moment and send the command again. The move usually finishes soon.

errors.message: TRYAGAIN Slot is being trimmed
errors.explain: You sent a write to a node that's deleting all the keys of that hash slot, for example because the slot moved to another node. Wait for the deletion to finish, then retry. The slot may now be served by another node.

errors.message: UNBLOCKED client unblocked via CLIENT UNBLOCK
errors.explain: Another connection ended your blocking command, such as `BLPOP` or `XREAD`, early with `CLIENT UNBLOCK` and the `ERROR` option. Send the command again if you still need its result.

errors.message: UNBLOCKED force unblock from blocking operation, instance state changed (master -> replica?)
errors.explain: Your blocking command, such as `BLPOP` or `XREAD` with `BLOCK`, was stopped because the server became a replica while you waited, for example during a failover. Redis also closes the connection. Reconnect to the new primary and send the command again.

errors.message: UNKILLABLE Sorry the script already executed write commands against the dataset. You can either wait the script termination or kill the server in a hard way using the SHUTDOWN NOSAVE command.
errors.explain: You ran `SCRIPT KILL` or `FUNCTION KILL`, but the running script has already changed data, so stopping it would leave the change half done. Wait for the script to finish, or run `SHUTDOWN NOSAVE` to stop the server without saving.

errors.message: UNKILLABLE The busy script was sent by a master instance in the context of replication and cannot be killed.
errors.explain: You ran `SCRIPT KILL` or `FUNCTION KILL` on a replica, but the busy script came from its primary through replication, and a replica never stops a script that its primary sent. Wait for the script to finish.

errors.message: WRONGPASS invalid internal password
errors.explain: A connection authenticated as `internal connection`, the username that cluster nodes use with each other, but the secret it sent doesn't match this cluster's internal secret. Apps should authenticate as a normal user instead.

errors.message: WRONGPASS invalid username-password pair or user is disabled.
errors.explain: `AUTH` or `HELLO` failed because the user doesn't exist, the password is wrong, or the user is disabled. Check the username and password that your client sends, and as an administrator check the user with `ACL GETUSER`.

errors.message: WRONGTYPE Key is not a valid HyperLogLog string value.
errors.explain: The key holds a string that isn't a HyperLogLog, so `PFADD`, `PFCOUNT`, and `PFMERGE` can't use it. Use another key name, or delete the string first; create HyperLogLog keys only with `PFADD` or `PFMERGE`.

errors.message: WRONGTYPE Operation against a key holding the wrong kind of value
errors.explain: You ran a command on a key that holds a different data type, for example `LPUSH` on a string or `VADD` on a hash. Check the key's type with `TYPE`, then use a command for that type or a different key name.

errors.message: ERR '<filename>:<line>: username '<username>' contains invalid characters.
errors.explain: `ACL LOAD` found a username in the access control list (ACL) file that contains a whitespace character, such as a tab, or a null character. Fix the `user` line at the line number in the message and run `ACL LOAD` again. No users were changed.

errors.message: ERR '<option>' must not contain control characters
errors.explain: You ran `SENTINEL CONFIG SET` with a value for the option named in the message that contains a control character, such as a newline or a tab. Remove the control characters from the value.

errors.message: ERR <filename>:<line> should start with user keyword followed by the username.
errors.explain: A line in the access control list (ACL) file doesn't start with the lowercase keyword `user` followed by a username, as every line other than comments and blank lines must. Fix the line named in the message and run `ACL LOAD` again.

errors.message: ERR <filename>:<line>: <reason>.
errors.explain: A rule on that line of the access control list (ACL) file is invalid, and the text after the line number says why, for example `Syntax error` or a bad password hash. Fix the rule and run `ACL LOAD` again. No users were changed.

errors.message: ERR <filename>:<line>: Error in applying operation '<operation>': Unknown command or category name in ACL.
errors.explain: A rule on that line of the access control list (ACL) file names a command or category that this server doesn't know, for example a misspelled command or one from a module that isn't loaded. Fix or remove that rule and run `ACL LOAD` again.

errors.message: ERR <filename>:<line>: unbalanced quotes in acl line.
errors.explain: `ACL LOAD` reports this when it can't split a line of the access control list (ACL) file into words. Redis 8.10 splits these lines on spaces and doesn't treat quotes specially, so this normally doesn't appear. If it does, check that line for stray characters.

errors.message: ERR <filename>:<line>: Unmatched parenthesis in selector definition.
errors.explain: A selector on that line of the access control list (ACL) file starts with `(` but is never closed with `)`. Close the selector, for example `(~app:* +get)`, and run `ACL LOAD` again. No users were changed.

errors.message: ERR <option> cannot contain spaces, newlines or special characters.
errors.explain: The value you passed to `CLIENT SETINFO` for the option in the message, `lib-name` or `lib-ver`, has a space, a newline, or another character that isn't plain and visible. Use only unaccented letters, digits, and punctuation, such as `redis-py` or `5.0.1`.

errors.message: ERR <reason>
ERR A backup is already in progress, ABORT it first
errors.explain: You ran `BACKUP START` while another backup is still being made. Finish it with `BACKUP SEAL` or cancel it with `BACKUP ABORT`, then start again. `BACKUP STATUS` shows its state.

errors.message: ERR A client can only redirect to a single other client
errors.explain: You passed `REDIRECT` more than once to `CLIENT TRACKING`. Invalidation messages can go to only one other connection, so give a single `REDIRECT` with that connection's client ID.

errors.message: ERR A sealed backup exists, CLEANUP it first
errors.explain: A sealed backup is still in the backup directory, so `BACKUP START` won't replace it. Copy its files, which `BACKUP LIST` shows, then run `BACKUP CLEANUP` and start the new backup.

errors.message: ERR ACL failure in script: No permissions to access a channel script: <script>, on <source>:<line>.
errors.explain: A script or function used a channel, for example with `PUBLISH`, that your user's access control list (ACL) rules don't allow. Scripts run with the caller's permissions. Allow the channel with a `&` pattern in `ACL SETUSER`, or call the script as a user with access.

errors.message: ERR ACL failure in script: No permissions to access a key script: <script>, on <source>:<line>.
errors.explain: A script or function used a key that your user's access control list (ACL) rules don't allow. Scripts run with the caller's permissions. Allow the key with a `~` pattern in `ACL SETUSER`, or run the script as a user that has access.

errors.message: ERR ACL failure in script: User <username> has no permissions to run the '<command>' command script: <script>, on <source>:<line>.
errors.explain: A script or function called a command, through `redis.call` or `redis.pcall`, that the user in the message isn't allowed to run. Allowing `EVAL` or `FCALL` doesn't allow the commands inside the script, so add each one to the user's rules with `ACL SETUSER`.

errors.message: ERR ACL GENPASS argument must be the number of bits for the output password, a positive number up to 4096
errors.explain: The number of bits you passed to `ACL GENPASS` is out of range. Pass a whole number from 1 to 4096, or leave it out to get a 256-bit password.

errors.message: ERR all slot states must be STABLE to start a slot migration task.
errors.explain: A legacy slot migration is open on this node: some slot is set to `MIGRATING` or `IMPORTING` with `CLUSTER SETSLOT`. Finish that migration, or run `CLUSTER SETSLOT` with `STABLE` on the slot, before you start an atomic slot migration.

errors.message: ERR An LFU maxmemory policy is not selected, access frequency not tracked. Please note that when switching between policies at runtime LRU and LFU data will take some time to adjust.
errors.explain: `OBJECT FREQ` reports how often a key is accessed, which Redis tracks only under a least frequently used (LFU) eviction policy. Set `maxmemory-policy` to `allkeys-lfu` or `volatile-lfu`, or use `OBJECT IDLETIME` with the current policy.

errors.message: ERR An LFU maxmemory policy is selected, idle time not tracked. Please note that when switching between policies at runtime LRU and LFU data will take some time to adjust.
errors.explain: `OBJECT IDLETIME` reports idle time, which Redis doesn't track while `maxmemory-policy` is a least frequently used (LFU) policy, `allkeys-lfu` or `volatile-lfu`. Use `OBJECT FREQ` instead, or switch to another policy.

errors.message: ERR Another ASM task is already in progress
errors.explain: A node asked this node to start sending it slots, but this node is already running another atomic slot migration. Nodes send this to each other, so you see it in logs or in `CLUSTER MIGRATION STATUS`. Wait for the running migration, or cancel it.

errors.message: ERR another ASM task is already in progress
errors.explain: This node is already running an atomic slot migration, and it runs only one at a time. Check it with `CLUSTER MIGRATION STATUS ALL`, then wait for it to finish or stop it with `CLUSTER MIGRATION CANCEL`.

errors.message: ERR Another child process is active (AOF?): can't BGSAVE right now. Use BGSAVE SCHEDULE in order to schedule a BGSAVE whenever possible.
errors.explain: Another background process, usually a rewrite of the append-only file (AOF), is running, so `BGSAVE` can't start now. Run `BGSAVE SCHEDULE` to start the save as soon as possible, or wait and retry.

errors.message: ERR Another migration task is already in progress
errors.explain: During an atomic slot migration, the importing node opened its data connection for a task that this node isn't running or isn't ready for. This is internal to the migration. Check `CLUSTER MIGRATION STATUS` on the importing node, and import again if the task failed.

errors.message: ERR applied increment would be Infinity
errors.explain: With `SATURATE`, `INCREX` capped the result at a bound so far from the current value that it can't represent the difference, which it returns as the applied increment. Use bounds closer to the current value, or reset the key first.

errors.message: ERR applied increment would overflow
errors.explain: With `SATURATE`, `INCREX` capped the result at a bound so far from the current value that the difference, which it returns as the applied increment, doesn't fit in a 64-bit integer. Use bounds closer to the current value, or reset the key first.

errors.message: ERR argument must be a memory value bigger than 1 and smaller than 4gb
ERR Argument must be ON or OFF
ERR array index overflow
errors.explain: `ARSET` would write past the last valid array index, 18446744073709551614, because the start index plus the number of values is too large. Use a smaller start index or fewer values.

errors.message: ERR at least 1 input key is needed for '<command>' command
errors.explain: The number of input keys you passed to the command named in the message is 0 or negative. Pass the number of source keys that follow it, which must be at least 1.

errors.message: ERR At least one parameter must be specified
errors.explain: You ran `XCFGSET` with only a key. Add `IDMP-DURATION`, `IDMP-MAXSIZE` or both, each followed by its value.

errors.message: ERR AUTH <password> called without any password configured for the default user. Are you sure your configuration is correct?
errors.explain: You sent `AUTH` with only a password, but the default user has no password, so there's nothing to check. Remove the `AUTH` call, set a password with `requirepass` or `ACL SETUSER`, or also send a username if you meant another user.

errors.message: ERR Background append only file rewriting already in progress
errors.explain: An append-only file (AOF) rewrite is already running, so `BGREWRITEAOF` didn't start another one. Wait for it to finish. `INFO persistence` shows `aof_rewrite_in_progress:1` while it runs.

errors.message: ERR Background save already in progress
errors.explain: A background save is already running, so `SAVE` or `BGSAVE` can't start another one. Wait until `INFO persistence` shows `rdb_bgsave_in_progress:0`, then retry if you still need a new snapshot.

errors.message: ERR Backup directory <dirname> is not empty, CLEANUP it first
errors.explain: The backup directory in the message already has files in it, for example from an earlier backup that failed or was aborted. `BACKUP CLEANUP` deletes every file in that directory, so copy anything you need first, then run `BACKUP START` again.

errors.message: ERR Backup is in progress
errors.explain: `BACKUP CLEANUP` can't run while a backup is still being made. Seal the backup with `BACKUP SEAL` or cancel it with `BACKUP ABORT` first.

errors.message: ERR Bad data format
errors.explain: The `RESTORE` payload passed the version and checksum checks, but Redis couldn't read the value in it. Common causes are a module data type whose module isn't loaded on this server, or a payload that fails the `sanitize-dump-payload` check.

errors.message: ERR Bad number of keys provided
errors.explain: The numkeys argument of `FCALL` or `FCALL_RO`, right after the function name, isn't an integer. Pass the number of key names that follow it, such as `0` when the function uses no keys.

errors.message: ERR BGSAVE failed, replication can't continue
errors.explain: The primary couldn't start the background save it needs for a full sync, so it dropped this replica's sync request. You see this in the replica's log; check the primary's log for the reason, often too little memory to fork or a full disk.

errors.message: ERR bit is not an integer or out of range
errors.explain: The value argument of `SETBIT` must be `0` or `1`, and you passed something else. To write a number wider than one bit, use `BITFIELD`.

errors.message: ERR bit offset is not an integer or out of range
errors.explain: The bit offset isn't a whole number of 0 or more, or it points past the largest string Redis allows, set by `proto-max-bulk-len`. By default, the highest offset is 4294967295. In `BITFIELD`, an offset that starts with `#` is multiplied by the field width first.

errors.message: ERR BITFIELD_RO only supports the GET subcommand
errors.explain: `BITFIELD_RO` is the read-only form of `BITFIELD`, so it accepts only `GET` operations. Use `BITFIELD` to run `SET` or `INCRBY`.

errors.message: ERR BITOP <operation> must be called with at least two source keys.
errors.explain: The `DIFF`, `DIFF1`, and `ANDOR` operations of `BITOP` compare a first key with one or more others, so they need at least two source keys after the destination key. Add the missing source key.

errors.message: ERR BITOP NOT must be called with a single source key.
errors.explain: `BITOP NOT` inverts one string, so it takes exactly one source key after the destination key. To invert several keys, run `BITOP NOT` once for each.

errors.message: ERR Blocking module command called from a Reply callback context
errors.explain: A module tried to block a client from inside the reply callback of an earlier block, which Redis doesn't allow. This is a bug in the module; report it to its developers.

errors.message: ERR Blocking module command called from Lua script
errors.explain: A script called a module command that tried to block, which can't happen inside a script. Call that module command directly from your client instead of from `EVAL` or `FCALL`.

errors.message: ERR Blocking module command called from transaction
errors.explain: You queued a module command that blocks inside a `MULTI` transaction, where commands can't block. Run that command outside the transaction.

errors.message: ERR BY option of SORT denied due to insufficient ACL permissions.
errors.explain: You ran `SORT` with a `BY` pattern, which reads other keys, but your user's access control list (ACL) rules don't allow reading every key. Give the user read access to all keys, such as `%R~*` or `~*`, or sort without a pattern.

errors.message: ERR BY option of SORT denied in Cluster mode when keys formed by the pattern may be in different slots.
errors.explain: You ran `SORT` with a `BY` pattern in a cluster, and the keys that the pattern builds may be in a different hash slot than the key you sort. Start the pattern with the same hash tag as the key, such as `{user1}:w_*` for `{user1}:list`.

errors.message: ERR BYFLOAT increment cannot be Infinity
errors.explain: You passed `INCREX` a `BYFLOAT` increment of infinity, such as `inf`. Pass a finite number.

errors.message: ERR Can not execute a script with write flag using *_ro command.
errors.explain: You ran a script or function that may write with `EVAL_RO`, `EVALSHA_RO`, or `FCALL_RO`, which only run read-only code. If it never writes, add the `no-writes` flag; otherwise call it with `EVAL`, `EVALSHA`, or `FCALL`.

errors.message: ERR Can not execute the command on a stale replica script: <script>, on <source>:<line>.
errors.explain: Your script has the `allow-stale` flag and called a command that this replica can't serve while its link to the primary is down and `replica-serve-stale-data` is `no`. Wait for the link to recover, or call only commands that are allowed on a stale replica, such as `INFO`.

errors.message: ERR can not read data type
errors.explain: The payload you passed to `FUNCTION RESTORE` passed its checksum test, but Redis couldn't read the type of one of its entries, so it's truncated or malformed. Pass the exact, unmodified output of `FUNCTION DUMP`.

errors.message: ERR Can not run script on cluster, 'no-cluster' flag is set.
errors.explain: Your script or function has the `no-cluster` flag, which stops it from running on a cluster node. Remove the flag if the code is safe to run in a cluster, or run it on a server that isn't part of a cluster.

errors.message: ERR can only reset normal client connections
errors.explain: You sent `RESET` on a connection that's used for replication between a primary and a replica, or from inside a module. `RESET` only works on normal client connections; to end a replication link, close the connection instead.

errors.message: ERR Can't assign hashslot <slot> to a different node while I still hold keys for this hash slot.
errors.explain: `CLUSTER SETSLOT` with `NODE` can't give the slot in the message to another node while this node still has keys in that slot. Move the keys first with `MIGRATE`, then assign the slot.

errors.message: ERR Can't create backup directory <dirname>: <reason>
errors.explain: Redis couldn't create the backup directory set by `backupdirname`, for the operating system reason at the end of the message, such as missing permissions. Check the path and its parent directory. A relative path is resolved under the Redis working directory, `dir`.

errors.message: ERR Can't execute '<command>': only (P|S)SUBSCRIBE / (P|S)UNSUBSCRIBE / PING / QUIT / RESET are allowed in this context
errors.example: ERR Can't execute 'get': only (P|S)SUBSCRIBE / (P|S)UNSUBSCRIBE / PING / QUIT / RESET are allowed in this context
errors.explain: This connection is subscribed to Pub/Sub channels and uses the Redis serialization protocol 2 (RESP2), so it can only run the subscribe and unsubscribe commands, `PING`, `QUIT` and `RESET`. Use a separate connection for other commands, or switch to RESP3 with `HELLO 3`.

errors.message: ERR Can't execute an AOF background rewriting. Please check the server logs for more information.
errors.explain: Redis couldn't start the append-only file (AOF) rewrite, for example because it couldn't create the background process or open a new AOF file. The server log has the reason. Common causes are low memory and disk problems.

errors.message: ERR Can't forget my master!
errors.explain: `CLUSTER FORGET` can't remove the primary of the replica you ran it on. Run it on the other nodes, or first make this replica follow another primary with `CLUSTER REPLICATE`.

errors.message: ERR Can't fsync the INCR file for the backup
errors.explain: `BACKUP SEAL` couldn't flush the incremental append-only file (AOF) to disk, so the backup failed. Check the server log and the disk, then run `BACKUP CLEANUP` and start a new backup.

errors.message: ERR Can't pin the INCR AOF for the backup
errors.explain: `BACKUP SEAL` couldn't create a hard link to the incremental append-only file (AOF) in the backup directory, so the backup failed. Hard links need both directories on the same file system. Check the server log, run `BACKUP CLEANUP`, and start again.

errors.message: ERR Can't replicate myself
errors.explain: You passed this node's own ID to `CLUSTER REPLICATE`. Pass the ID of the primary it should replicate, as shown by `CLUSTER NODES`.

errors.message: ERR Can't resolve instance hostname.
errors.explain: Sentinel couldn't resolve the host name of the primary that you passed to `SENTINEL MONITOR`. Check that the name resolves on the Sentinel host, or pass an Internet Protocol (IP) address. Sentinel accepts host names only when `resolve-hostnames` is `yes`.

errors.message: ERR Can't rotate the live AOF after sealing the backup
errors.explain: With `appendonly yes`, `BACKUP SEAL` switches the live append-only file (AOF) to a new incremental file, and that step failed, so the backup failed. Check the server log and the disk, then run `BACKUP CLEANUP` and start a new backup.

errors.message: ERR Can't start the AOF rewrite for the backup
errors.explain: `BACKUP START` couldn't begin the snapshot, because Redis failed to start an append-only file (AOF) rewrite, or to turn on AOF for the backup when `appendonly` is `no`. Check the server log, often for a fork or disk error, then try again.

errors.message: ERR Can't write the backup manifest
errors.explain: `BACKUP SEAL` couldn't write the manifest file that describes the backup, so the backup failed. Check the server log and that the backup directory is writable, then run `BACKUP CLEANUP` and start a new backup.

errors.message: ERR Cannot authenticate as an internal connection on non-cluster instances
errors.explain: `AUTH` with the username `internal connection` is reserved for cluster nodes talking to each other, and this server isn't running in cluster mode. Authenticate with a normal username and password instead.

errors.message: ERR CLIENT CACHING can be called only when the client is in tracking mode with OPTIN or OPTOUT mode enabled
errors.explain: You sent `CLIENT CACHING`, but tracking for client-side caching isn't on for this connection. Run `CLIENT TRACKING ON OPTIN` or `CLIENT TRACKING ON OPTOUT` first.

errors.message: ERR CLIENT CACHING NO is only valid when tracking is enabled in OPTOUT mode.
errors.explain: You sent `CLIENT CACHING NO`, but tracking isn't in `OPTOUT` mode. `CLIENT CACHING NO` only works after `CLIENT TRACKING ON OPTOUT`; in `OPTIN` mode, send `CLIENT CACHING YES` before the reads you want tracked.

errors.message: ERR CLIENT CACHING YES is only valid when tracking is enabled in OPTIN mode.
errors.explain: You sent `CLIENT CACHING YES`, but tracking isn't in `OPTIN` mode. `CLIENT CACHING YES` only works after `CLIENT TRACKING ON OPTIN`; in `OPTOUT` mode, send `CLIENT CACHING NO` before the reads you don't want tracked.

errors.message: ERR Client names cannot contain spaces, newlines or special characters.
errors.explain: The connection name you passed to `CLIENT SETNAME` or `HELLO SETNAME` has a space, a newline, or another character that isn't plain and visible. Use only unaccented letters, digits, and punctuation, such as `worker-1`.

errors.message: ERR CLIENT PAUSE mode must be WRITE or ALL
errors.explain: The mode you passed to `CLIENT PAUSE` after the timeout isn't `WRITE` or `ALL`. Use `WRITE` to pause only commands that change data, or `ALL`, the default, to pause every command.

errors.message: ERR Client reconfiguration script seems non existing or non executable
errors.explain: You ran `SENTINEL SET` with `client-reconfig-script`, but the path doesn't point to a file that the Sentinel process can execute. Check the path, and make the file executable for the user that runs Sentinel.

errors.message: ERR CLIENT UNBLOCK reason should be TIMEOUT or ERROR
errors.explain: The reason you passed to `CLIENT UNBLOCK` after the client ID isn't `TIMEOUT` or `ERROR`. Use `TIMEOUT`, the default, to end the blocked command as if it timed out, or `ERROR` to make it return an `UNBLOCKED` error.

errors.message: ERR client-id should be greater than 0
errors.explain: The value after `CLIENT KILL ID` isn't a positive integer. Pass a client ID from `CLIENT LIST` or `CLIENT ID`; IDs start at 1.

errors.message: ERR client-reconfig-script must not contain control characters
errors.explain: You ran `SENTINEL SET` with a `client-reconfig-script` path that contains a control character, such as a newline or a tab. Pass a plain file path.

errors.message: ERR Clients undergoing module based authentication can only be blocked on auth
errors.explain: A module tried to block a client that's in the middle of module-based authentication, for something other than the authentication itself. This is a bug in the module; report it to its developers.

errors.message: ERR CLUSTER RESET can't be called with master nodes containing keys
errors.explain: `CLUSTER RESET` doesn't run on a primary that still has keys, to avoid losing data. Delete the keys first, for example with `FLUSHALL`, or reset a replica instead.

errors.message: ERR CLUSTER SYNCSLOTS CONF ASM-TASK only allowed on replica
errors.explain: A primary received the `ASM-TASK` option of `CLUSTER SYNCSLOTS CONF`, which a primary sends only to its own replicas. This is internal to atomic slot migration and usually means a node changed role during a migration. Check the roles with `CLUSTER NODES`.

errors.message: ERR CLUSTER SYNCSLOTS subcommands are only allowed for internal clients
errors.explain: `CLUSTER SYNCSLOTS` is used only between cluster nodes during an atomic slot migration, and Redis closes any other connection that sends it. Don't call it yourself. To move slots, use `CLUSTER MIGRATION IMPORT`.

errors.message: ERR CLUSTER SYNCSLOTS subcommands are only allowed for master
errors.explain: A replica accepts `CLUSTER SYNCSLOTS` only from its own primary, and it closes other connections that send it. Atomic slot migrations run between primaries, so run `CLUSTER MIGRATION IMPORT` on the primary that should receive the slots.

errors.message: ERR Command '<command>' not found
errors.explain: `ACL DRYRUN` doesn't know the command, shown in the message, that you asked it to test. Check the spelling, and check that the module that provides the command is loaded.

errors.message: ERR Command is not valid when client is a replica.
errors.explain: `REPLICAOF` with a host and port was sent on a connection that is itself a replica's replication link. Making this server a replica disconnects all its replicas, including that link, so send the command from a normal client connection.

errors.message: ERR Command not allowed inside a transaction
errors.explain: You sent a command inside a `MULTI` transaction that can't run there, such as `SAVE`, `SHUTDOWN`, `SYNC` or `PSYNC`. Run it outside the transaction. The transaction is discarded when you call `EXEC`.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>')
errors.explain: `CONFIG SET` couldn't set the parameter in the message, and no reason was given. This usually means a module rejected the value for one of its own settings, so check the module's documentation for valid values.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - <reason>
errors.explain: `CONFIG SET` couldn't set the parameter in the message, for the reason after the dash. For `dir`, the reason comes from the operating system, such as a directory that doesn't exist. For a module setting, it comes from the module.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - Active defragmentation cannot be enabled: it requires a Redis server compiled with a modified Jemalloc like the one shipped by default with the Redis source distribution
errors.explain: This Redis server was built without the jemalloc memory allocator that Redis ships with, so `activedefrag` can't be turned on. Active defragmentation needs a Redis build that uses its bundled jemalloc.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - Announced human node name contained invalid character
errors.explain: The value for `cluster-announce-human-nodename` contains a character that isn't allowed, such as a space, a control character, or punctuation like `,`, `:`, `=`, or `@`. Use letters, digits, hyphens, dots, and underscores.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - argument couldn't be parsed as an octal number
errors.explain: The value must be an octal number, such as `700`. The only octal setting, `unixsocketperm`, can't be changed with `CONFIG SET`, so set it in the configuration file and restart.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - argument couldn't be parsed into an integer
errors.explain: The setting takes a whole number, and the value you passed isn't one, for example because it has a unit or a decimal point. Pass digits only, with an optional minus sign.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - argument must be 'yes' or 'no'
errors.example: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument 'appendonly') - argument must be 'yes' or 'no'
errors.explain: The setting is either on or off, so its value must be `yes` or `no`. Other values, such as `true`, `1`, or `on`, aren't accepted.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - argument must be a memory or percent value
errors.explain: `maxmemory-clients` takes either a memory value, such as `1gb`, or a percentage of `maxmemory`, such as `10%`, and the value you passed is neither.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - argument must be a memory value
errors.example: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument 'maxmemory') - argument must be a memory value
errors.explain: The setting takes a memory value: a whole number of bytes, optionally followed by a unit such as `kb`, `mb`, or `gb`, for example `100mb`. Check for typos, spaces, decimal points, or a minus sign.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - argument must be between <min> and <max> inclusive
errors.example: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument 'maxclients') - argument must be between 1 and 4294967295 inclusive
errors.explain: The value is outside the range that the setting accepts, and the message shows the smallest and the largest allowed values. Pass a value within that range.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - argument(s) must be one of the following: <values>
errors.example: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument 'maxmemory-policy') - argument(s) must be one of the following: volatile-lru, volatile-lfu, volatile-random, volatile-ttl, volatile-lrm, allkeys-lru, allkeys-lfu, allkeys-random, allkeys-lrm, noeviction
errors.explain: The setting accepts only the values listed in the message, and yours isn't one of them. Check the spelling. For settings that take several values, separate them with spaces.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - array-slice-size must be a power of two
errors.explain: `array-slice-size` must be a power of two from 256 to 65536, such as 256, 1024, or 4096.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - array-sparse-kmax must be greater than array-sparse-kmin when non-zero
errors.explain: `array-sparse-kmax` must be 0 or greater than the current `array-sparse-kmin`. Pass a larger value, or lower `array-sparse-kmin` first.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - array-sparse-kmin must be less than array-sparse-kmax
errors.explain: `array-sparse-kmin` must be less than the current `array-sparse-kmax`, unless that is 0. If you raise both in one `CONFIG SET`, put `array-sparse-kmax` first, because each value is checked against the other's current setting.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - can't disable tls-cluster while cluster-bus-port-protected-mode is enabled, as that would leave the cluster bus port unauthenticated; disable cluster-bus-port-protected-mode first, or in the same CONFIG SET command
errors.explain: In cluster mode, turning off `tls-cluster` while `cluster-bus-port-protected-mode` is on would leave the cluster bus without authentication, so Redis refuses. Turn off `cluster-bus-port-protected-mode` first, or in the same `CONFIG SET` command.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - can't enable cluster-bus-port-protected-mode while tls-cluster is disabled, as that leaves the cluster bus port unauthenticated; enable tls-cluster first, or in the same CONFIG SET command
errors.explain: In cluster mode, `cluster-bus-port-protected-mode` requires `tls-cluster`, because otherwise the cluster bus has no authentication. Turn on `tls-cluster` first, or in the same `CONFIG SET` command.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - can't set immutable config
errors.example: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument 'appendfilename') - can't set immutable config
errors.explain: The parameter in the message can be set only when the server starts, not with `CONFIG SET`. Set it in the configuration file or on the command line, then restart the server.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - can't set protected config
errors.example: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument 'dbfilename') - can't set protected config
errors.explain: The parameter in the message, such as `dir` or `dbfilename`, is protected, and `CONFIG SET` can't change it while `enable-protected-configs` is `no`, the default. Set it in the configuration file, or start the server with `enable-protected-configs` set to `yes` or `local`.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - dbfilename can't be a path, just a filename
errors.explain: `dbfilename` takes only a file name, such as `dump.rdb`, without a directory. Set the directory with `dir` instead.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - duplicate parameter
errors.example: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument 'hz') - duplicate parameter
errors.explain: The same parameter appears twice in one `CONFIG SET`, possibly once by its alias, such as `replica-read-only` and `slave-read-only`. Pass each parameter only once.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - Error in hard, soft or soft_seconds setting in buffer limit configuration.
errors.explain: In `client-output-buffer-limit`, each class needs a hard limit and a soft limit, as memory values such as `256mb` or `0`, and soft seconds, as a whole number of 0 or more. One of these three values isn't valid.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - Failed to bind to specified addresses.
errors.explain: Redis couldn't listen on an address you set in `bind`, for example because the address doesn't belong to this machine or the port is already in use. The server log has the address and the reason.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - Failed to set current oom_score_adj. Check server logs.
errors.explain: Redis couldn't change its Linux out-of-memory killer score, which `oom-score-adj` and `oom-score-adj-values` control. This works only on Linux, and lowering the score needs extra privileges. The server log has the reason.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - failed to set process title
errors.explain: Redis accepted the new `proc-title-template` but couldn't apply it to the process title. The template is checked before this step, so this normally doesn't happen. Check the template and the server log.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - Hostnames for cluster-announce-ip must be less than 46 characters
errors.explain: A hostname in `cluster-announce-ip` must be shorter than 46 characters. Use a shorter name or a numeric address, or announce the hostname with `cluster-announce-hostname` instead.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - Hostnames may only contain alphanumeric characters, hyphens or dots
errors.explain: The value for `cluster-announce-hostname` or `cluster-announce-ip` contains a character other than letters, digits, hyphens, or dots, such as an underscore or a space. Remove those characters.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - Hostnames must be less than 256 characters
errors.explain: The value for `cluster-announce-hostname` must be shorter than 256 characters. Use a shorter hostname.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - Invalid client class specified in buffer limit configuration.
errors.explain: `client-output-buffer-limit` names a client class that it doesn't support. Use `normal`, `replica`, or `pubsub`. The `master` class isn't allowed.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - Invalid event class character. Use 'Ag$lshzxeKEtmdnocaSTIV'.
errors.example: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument 'notify-keyspace-events') - Invalid event class character. Use 'Ag$lshzxeKEtmdnocaSTIV'.
errors.explain: The value of `notify-keyspace-events` contains a character that isn't an event class. Use only the characters listed in the message, for example `KEA` to get every event, or an empty string to turn notifications off.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - Invalid latency-tracking-info-percentiles parameters
errors.explain: A value in `latency-tracking-info-percentiles` isn't a number. Pass numbers separated by spaces, such as `50 99 99.9`.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - Invalid locale name
errors.explain: The locale in `locale-collate` isn't installed on the server's operating system. Use a locale that `locale -a` lists on that machine, or an empty string to use the default from the environment.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - Invalid oom-score-adj-values, elements must be between -2000 and 2000.
errors.example: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument 'oom-score-adj-values') - Invalid oom-score-adj-values, elements must be between -2000 and 2000.
errors.explain: `oom-score-adj-values` takes three whole numbers, for the primary, replicas, and background child processes, each from -2000 to 2000. One of the values isn't a number or is out of range.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - Invalid save parameters
errors.example: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument 'save') - Invalid save parameters
errors.explain: The value of `save` must be pairs of numbers: seconds, 1 or more, then a number of changes, 0 or more, such as `3600 1 300 100`. To turn off snapshots, pass an empty string.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - latency-tracking-info-percentiles parameters should sit between [0.0,100.0]
errors.explain: Each value in `latency-tracking-info-percentiles` must be from 0.0 to 100.0. Fix or remove the value that's out of range.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - memory tracking cannot be enabled at runtime
errors.explain: Setting `key-memory-histograms` to `yes`, or adding `mem` to `cluster-slot-stats-enabled`, needs memory tracking, which Redis can turn on only at startup. Set the option in the configuration file and restart the server.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - percentage argument must be less or equal to <max>
errors.explain: A percentage for `maxmemory-clients` can't be higher than the number in the message, 100. Pass a lower percentage, or a memory value.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - shutdown options SAVE and NOSAVE can't be used simultaneously
errors.explain: `shutdown-on-sigint` and `shutdown-on-sigterm` can't include both `save` and `nosave`. Pick one of them, optionally with `now` or `force`.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - template format is invalid or contains unknown variables
errors.explain: The value for `proc-title-template` uses a variable that doesn't exist, has unbalanced braces, or gives an empty title. The variables are `{title}`, `{listen-addr}`, `{server-mode}`, `{port}`, `{tls-port}`, `{unixsocket}`, and `{config-file}`.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - The event loop API used by Redis is not able to handle the specified number of clients
errors.explain: Redis couldn't make its event loop large enough for the new `maxclients`. This usually happens only on systems where Redis uses the older `select` interface, which handles about 1024 connections. Use a lower value.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - The operating system is not able to handle the specified number of clients, try with <maxclients>
errors.explain: The operating system's open-files limit is too low for the `maxclients` you asked for. Redis needs one file descriptor per client, plus 32. Raise the limit for the Redis process, for example with `ulimit -n`, and restart, or use the value in the message.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - TLS support is not compiled in, cannot enable TLS options.
errors.explain: This Redis server was built without Transport Layer Security (TLS) support, so you can't turn on `tls-replication` or `tls-cluster`. Use a Redis build with TLS support.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - TLS support is not compiled in, cannot set a TLS port.
errors.explain: This Redis server was built without Transport Layer Security (TLS) support, so you can't set `tls-port`. Use a Redis build with TLS support, or keep `tls-port` at 0.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - tls-expected-peer-name contains no usable name; use an empty string to disable it
errors.explain: `tls-expected-peer-name` contains only spaces, so there's no name to check. Pass one or more names separated by spaces, or an empty string to turn the check off.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - tls-expected-peer-name must not contain whitespace other than spaces separating names; use an empty string to disable it
errors.explain: `tls-expected-peer-name` contains a tab, a newline, or other whitespace that isn't a plain space. Separate names with spaces only, or pass an empty string to turn the check off.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - Too many bind addresses specified.
errors.explain: `bind` accepts at most 16 addresses, and you passed more. Remove some of the addresses.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - Unable to listen on this port. Check server logs.
errors.explain: Redis couldn't listen on the new `port` or `tls-port`, usually because another process uses it, or because a port below 1024 needs extra privileges. The server log has the exact reason.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - Unable to turn on AOF. Check server logs.
errors.explain: Redis couldn't turn on the append-only file (AOF) after `CONFIG SET appendonly yes`, for example because it couldn't start the rewrite that writes the first AOF file. The server log has the reason.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - Unable to update TLS configuration. Check server logs.
errors.explain: Redis couldn't load the new Transport Layer Security (TLS) settings, for example because a certificate or key file is missing, unreadable, or doesn't match. Check the `tls-*` file settings. The server log has the exact error.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - wrong number of arguments
errors.explain: `oom-score-adj-values` takes exactly three values, for the primary, replicas, and background child processes, such as `0 200 800`. Pass all three, separated by spaces.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<parameter>') - Wrong number of arguments in buffer limit configuration.
errors.explain: `client-output-buffer-limit` takes groups of four values: class, hard limit, soft limit, and soft seconds, such as `normal 0 0 0`. The value you passed doesn't split into groups of four.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG-REWRITE-FORCE-ALL failed: <reason>
ERR Copying to another database is not allowed in cluster mode
errors.explain: In cluster mode there's only database 0, so `COPY` can't use the `DB` option to copy to another database. Copy within database 0 instead.

errors.message: ERR could not decode requested zset member
errors.explain: The member you passed to `GEORADIUSBYMEMBER` or to `FROMMEMBER` doesn't exist in the sorted set, or its score isn't a valid geohash. Add the member with `GEOADD` first, or search from coordinates with `FROMLONLAT`.

errors.message: ERR COUNT can't be negative
errors.explain: You passed `LPOS` a `COUNT` that's negative or not an integer. Pass the number of matches to return, or 0 to return all of them.

errors.message: ERR COUNT must be > 0
errors.explain: The `COUNT` value is 0 or negative; for `XAUTOCLAIM`, it can also be a non-integer or a huge number. Pass a positive count, or leave `COUNT` out: geospatial searches then return every match, and `XAUTOCLAIM` claims up to 100 entries.

errors.message: ERR COUNT must be between 1 and 64
errors.explain: The `COUNT` value in `HOTKEYS START`, the number of top keys to track, isn't an integer from 1 to 64. Pass a value in that range, or leave `COUNT` out to track the top 10.

errors.message: ERR count should be greater than 0
errors.explain: The `COUNT` you passed, or the count after `EXACTLY` in `LMOVEM` and `BLMOVEM`, is 0, negative, or not an integer. Pass the number of elements to pop or move, which must be at least 1.

errors.message: ERR count should be greater than or equal to -1
errors.explain: You ran `SLOWLOG GET` with a count that isn't an integer or is less than -1. Pass the number of entries you want, or -1 to get all of them.

errors.message: ERR DB index is out of range
errors.explain: The database number you passed to `SELECT`, `MOVE`, `COPY`, or `SWAPDB` doesn't exist. Databases are numbered from 0 to the `databases` setting minus one, so 0 to 15 by default.

errors.message: ERR DB must be empty to perform CLUSTER FLUSHSLOTS.
errors.explain: `CLUSTER FLUSHSLOTS` removes all slots from this node, and it runs only when the node has no keys. Delete the keys first, for example with `FLUSHALL`.

errors.message: ERR DEBUG command not allowed. If the enable-debug-command option is set to "local", you can run it from a local connection, otherwise you need to set this option in the configuration file, and then restart the server.
errors.explain: `DEBUG` is turned off on this server, which is the default. To use it, set `enable-debug-command` to `yes`, or to `local` to allow it only from local connections, in the configuration file and restart Redis; `CONFIG SET` can't change it.

errors.message: ERR Debug option only available for cluster mode enabled setup!
ERR DEBUG RELOAD only supports the MERGE, NOFLUSH and NOSAVE options.
ERR DEBUG SCRIPT is disabled when hide-user-data-from-log is enabled
ERR decrement would overflow
errors.explain: You passed `DECRBY` -9223372036854775808, the smallest 64-bit integer, which Redis can't turn into a positive amount to subtract. Use a smaller amount, or `INCRBY` with a negative amount.

errors.message: ERR Destination node <node_id> is not a master
errors.explain: The node asking to receive the slots, named by its ID in the message, is unknown to this node or isn't a primary. Only a primary can import slots. Check the roles with `CLUSTER NODES`, and start the import on a primary.

errors.message: ERR DISCARD without MULTI
errors.explain: You sent `DISCARD`, but this connection has no open transaction. A transaction ends with `EXEC` or `DISCARD`, so check that `MULTI` and `DISCARD` go over the same connection and that the transaction hasn't ended already.

errors.message: ERR DUMP payload version or checksum are wrong
errors.explain: The payload you passed to `RESTORE` or `FUNCTION RESTORE` was made by a newer Redis version, or it changed on the way, for example truncated or converted to text by your client. Pass the exact bytes that `DUMP` or `FUNCTION DUMP` returned.

errors.message: ERR Duplicate argument '<option>' to SENTINEL CONFIG SET
errors.explain: You named the same option more than once in one `SENTINEL CONFIG SET` command. List each option once, with one value.

errors.message: ERR duplicate field name in fieldset
errors.explain: You ran `HIMPORT PREPARE` with the same field name more than once. List each field once; names are compared exactly, so case matters.

errors.message: ERR Duplicate master name.
errors.explain: You ran `SENTINEL MONITOR` with a primary name that this Sentinel already monitors. Choose another name, or remove the existing one first with `SENTINEL REMOVE`.

errors.message: ERR duplicate slot number
errors.explain: The slot numbers after `SLOTS` in `HOTKEYS START` include the same slot twice. List each slot once, and lower the count to match.

errors.message: ERR DURATION must be between 1 and 1000000
errors.explain: The `DURATION` value in `HOTKEYS START` isn't an integer from 1 to 1000000 seconds. `0` isn't accepted; to track until you run `HOTKEYS STOP`, leave `DURATION` out.

errors.message: ERR Elements are too large to be stored
errors.explain: The fields and values of the entry you passed to `XADD` add up to more than 1 GiB (1,073,741,824 bytes), the most that one stream entry can hold. Store large values in separate keys, and put only the key names in the stream.

errors.message: ERR Engine '<engine>' not found
errors.explain: The shebang line of your library names an engine that doesn't exist, the word right after `#!`. Lua is the only engine, so start the library with a line such as `#!lua name=mylib`.

errors.message: ERR entries_added must be positive
errors.explain: You passed `XSETID` a negative `ENTRIESADDED`. Pass 0 or more, and no less than the stream's length.

errors.message: ERR ENX flag requires an expiration
errors.explain: You passed `ENX` to `INCREX` without an expiration. Add one of `EX`, `PX`, `EXAT` or `PXAT`; with `ENX`, Redis sets it only if the key has no expiration yet.

errors.message: ERR
errors.explain: `SAVE` couldn't write the snapshot file to disk, or `BGSAVE` couldn't start the background process that writes it. Check the Redis log for the reason, which is often a full disk, no write permission on the `dir` directory, or too little memory to fork the process.

errors.message: ERR Error compiling function: <reason>
errors.example: ERR Error compiling function: user_function:2: unexpected symbol near '<eof>'
errors.explain: Lua couldn't compile the library code you passed to `FUNCTION LOAD` or `FUNCTION RESTORE`. The reason after the colon gives the line number in your code and the syntax problem; fix it and load the library again.

errors.message: ERR Error compiling script (new function): <reason>
errors.example: ERR Error compiling script (new function): user_script:1: unexpected symbol near '<eof>'
errors.explain: Lua couldn't compile the script you sent with `EVAL` or `SCRIPT LOAD`. The reason after the colon gives the line number in your script and the syntax problem, such as a missing `end` or an unclosed string; fix it and send the script again.

errors.message: ERR Error in ACL SETUSER modifier '<modifier>': Adding a pattern after the * pattern (or the 'allchannels' flag) is not valid and does not have any effect. Try 'resetchannels' to start with an empty list of channels
errors.explain: You added a channel pattern with `&` to a user that can already use all channels, through `allchannels` or `&*`, so the pattern would have no effect. Put `resetchannels` before the patterns to limit the user to those channels.

errors.message: ERR Error in ACL SETUSER modifier '<modifier>': Adding a pattern after the * pattern (or the 'allkeys' flag) is not valid and does not have any effect. Try 'resetkeys' to start with an empty list of patterns
errors.explain: You added a key pattern with `~` or `%` to a user that can already use all keys, through `allkeys` or `~*`, so the pattern would have no effect. Put `resetkeys` before the patterns to limit the user to those keys.

errors.message: ERR Error in ACL SETUSER modifier '<modifier>': Allowing first-arg of a subcommand is not supported
errors.explain: You tried to allow a subcommand with one specific first argument, such as `+config|get|maxmemory`. Access control list (ACL) rules can allow a command or a subcommand, such as `+config|get`, but not a single argument of a subcommand.

errors.message: ERR Error in ACL SETUSER modifier '<modifier>': Syntax error
errors.example: ERR Error in ACL SETUSER modifier 'foo': Syntax error
errors.explain: Redis didn't recognize the rule shown in the message. Common causes are a misspelled keyword, a `%` key rule with flags other than `R` and `W`, a subcommand rule that ends with `|`, or a key or channel pattern that contains spaces.

errors.message: ERR Error in ACL SETUSER modifier '<modifier>': The password hash must be exactly 64 characters and contain only lowercase hexadecimal characters
errors.explain: A rule that starts with `#` or `!` must be followed by a hashed password: exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters, the form that `ACL GETUSER` shows. To pass the password in plain text, use `>` or `<` instead.

errors.message: ERR Error in ACL SETUSER modifier '<modifier>': The password you are trying to remove from the user does not exist
errors.explain: A `<` or `!` rule tried to remove a password that the user doesn't have. Check the password or hash you passed, or use `resetpass` to remove all of the user's passwords.

errors.message: ERR Error in ACL SETUSER modifier '<modifier>': Unknown command or category name in ACL
errors.example: ERR Error in ACL SETUSER modifier '+nosuchcmd': Unknown command or category name in ACL
errors.explain: A `+` or `-` rule names a command, or a `+@` or `-@` rule names a category, that this server doesn't know. Check the name with `COMMAND LIST` or `ACL CAT`, and check that the module that provides the command is loaded.

errors.message: ERR Error in ACL SETUSER modifier '<modifier>': Wrong format
errors.explain: Redis rejected the rule shown in the message without giving a specific reason. This is a fallback that the rules in Redis 8.10 don't normally produce, so compare the rule with the `ACL SETUSER` syntax and look for unusual characters.

errors.message: ERR Error loading ACLs, opening file '<filename>': <reason>
errors.explain: `ACL LOAD` couldn't open the access control list (ACL) file set by `aclfile`, for the operating system reason at the end of the message, such as a missing file or no read permission. Check the path and the file's permissions.

errors.message: ERR Error loading the extension. Please check the server logs.
errors.explain: `MODULE LOAD` or `MODULE LOADEX` couldn't load the module, and the Redis log says why. Common causes are a wrong path, a file without execute permission, a module built for another platform, a module that's already loaded, or invalid module arguments.

errors.message: ERR Error purging dirty pages
errors.explain: `MEMORY PURGE` asked the jemalloc memory allocator to return unused memory to the operating system, and the allocator reported an error. This is usually temporary and doesn't affect your data, so you can retry later and check the Redis log.

errors.message: ERR Error registering functions: ERR callback argument given to redis.register_function must be a function
errors.explain: In the table form of `redis.register_function`, the `callback` field isn't a Lua function. Set it to the function itself, not to its name as a string or to the result of calling it.

errors.message: ERR Error registering functions: ERR calling redis.register_function with a single argument is only applicable to Lua table (representing named arguments).
errors.explain: You called `redis.register_function` with one argument that isn't a table. Pass either two arguments, the function name and the callback, or one table with `function_name` and `callback` fields.
