errors.explain: Your script ran for too long, and another client stopped it with `SCRIPT KILL` or `FUNCTION KILL`. It hadn't changed any data yet, so nothing was left half done. Find out why it runs so long, for example an endless loop, and fix the script.

errors.message: ERR SELECT is not allowed in cluster mode
errors.explain: In cluster mode there's only database 0, so `SELECT` accepts only 0. Remove the `SELECT` call, or set the database to 0 in your client's connection settings.

errors.message: ERR SHUTDOWN without NOW or ABORT isn't allowed for DENY BLOCKING client
errors.explain: A module called `SHUTDOWN` from inside its own code, where the call can't wait for replicas to catch up. The module must pass `NOW`, which skips the wait, or `ABORT`.

errors.message: ERR size must be positive
errors.explain: You ran `ARRING` with a ring size of 0 or less. Pass the number of slots that the ring buffer keeps, which must be 1 or more.

errors.message: ERR Slot <slot> is already busy
errors.explain: `CLUSTER ADDSLOTS` or `CLUSTER ADDSLOTSRANGE` tried to assign the slot in the message, but a node already serves it. Leave out slots that are already assigned, or move them with `CLUSTER SETSLOT` or `CLUSTER MIGRATION IMPORT`.

errors.message: ERR Slot <slot> is already unassigned
errors.explain: `CLUSTER DELSLOTS` or `CLUSTER DELSLOTSRANGE` tried to unassign the slot in the message, but no node serves it. Leave that slot out of the command.

errors.message: ERR Slot <slot> is currently in an active atomic slot migration. CLUSTER SETSLOT cannot be used at this time. To perform a legacy slot migration instead, first cancel the ongoing task with CLUSTER MIGRATION CANCEL
errors.explain: An atomic slot migration is moving the slot in the message, so `CLUSTER SETSLOT` can't change it now. Wait for the migration to finish, or cancel it with `CLUSTER MIGRATION CANCEL` if you want to move the slot the legacy way.

errors.message: ERR slot <slot> not handled by this node
errors.explain: The slot in the message isn't served by the node you sent `HOTKEYS START` to. Send the command to the primary that serves that slot, as `CLUSTER SHARDS` shows, or list only this node's slots.

errors.message: ERR Slot <slot> specified multiple times
errors.explain: The same hash slot, shown in the message, appears more than once in your slots or slot ranges, for example in two overlapping ranges. List each slot only once.

errors.message: ERR slot has no owner: <slot>
errors.explain: The slot in the message isn't assigned to any node, so there's no node to import it from. Assign the slot with `CLUSTER ADDSLOTS` instead of migrating it.

errors.message: ERR slot migration not allowed on replica.
errors.explain: You ran `CLUSTER MIGRATION IMPORT` on a replica, and only a primary can import slots. Run it on the primary that should receive the slots.

errors.message: ERR slot range is out of range: <start_slot>-<end_slot>
errors.explain: A slot range goes past slot 16383, the last hash slot. Commands check each slot number before this point, so you usually see this only from cluster tooling that starts a slot migration. Use slots from 0 to 16383.

errors.message: ERR slots belong to different source nodes
errors.explain: An import can take slots from only one source node, and the slots you listed are served by different nodes. Split the command into one `CLUSTER MIGRATION IMPORT` per source node, and run them one after another.

errors.message: ERR SLOTS count must be between 1 and 16384
errors.explain: The count after `SLOTS` in `HOTKEYS START` isn't an integer from 1 to 16384. Pass the number of slot numbers that follow it.

errors.message: ERR SLOTS parameter already specified
errors.explain: You passed `SLOTS` more than once to `HOTKEYS START`. List all the slots after a single `SLOTS` and its count.

errors.message: ERR SLOTS parameter cannot be used in non-cluster mode
errors.explain: You passed `SLOTS` to `HOTKEYS START` on a server that isn't part of a cluster, where hash slots don't apply. Remove `SLOTS` to track keys from the whole server.

errors.message: ERR source and destination objects are the same
errors.explain: You called `MOVE` with the database you're already using as the target, or `COPY` with the same key name as source and destination in the same database. Choose another database for `MOVE`, or another destination key or `DB` for `COPY`.

errors.message: ERR SSUBSCRIBE isn't allowed for a DENY BLOCKING client
errors.explain: You sent `SSUBSCRIBE` inside a `MULTI` transaction, or from a module call, where each command must get exactly one reply. Send `SSUBSCRIBE` on its own from a normal client connection, outside any transaction.

errors.message: ERR start slot number <start_slot> is greater than end slot number <end_slot>
errors.explain: In a slot range, the first slot must not be higher than the last one, and the message shows a range where it is. Swap the two numbers, for example `1000 2000` instead of `2000 1000`.

errors.message: ERR Start slot number <start_slot> is greater than end slot number <end_slot>
errors.explain: In `CLUSTER SLOT-STATS SLOTSRANGE`, the start slot is higher than the end slot. Swap the two numbers so that the range goes from low to high.

errors.message: ERR STORE option in GEORADIUS is not compatible with WITHDIST, WITHHASH and WITHCOORD options
errors.explain: You combined `STORE` or `STOREDIST` with `WITHDIST`, `WITHHASH`, or `WITHCOORD` in `GEORADIUS` or `GEORADIUSBYMEMBER`. Stored results can't include those details, so remove them, or drop `STORE` to get the details back.

errors.message: ERR string exceeds maximum allowed size (proto-max-bulk-len)
errors.explain: The string that `APPEND` or `SETRANGE` would create is longer than `proto-max-bulk-len`, 512 MB by default. Keep values smaller or split them across keys, or raise `proto-max-bulk-len` if you need larger strings.

errors.message: ERR String too long for LCS
errors.explain: One of the strings you passed to `LCS` is about 4 GB or longer, more than `LCS` can handle. Compare shorter strings.

errors.message: ERR SUBSCRIBE isn't allowed for a DENY BLOCKING client
errors.explain: `SUBSCRIBE` came from a connection that must get exactly one reply per command, such as a module calling Redis, so it can't enter Pub/Sub mode. Send `SUBSCRIBE` from a normal client connection instead.

errors.message: ERR SWAPDB is not allowed in cluster mode
errors.explain: In cluster mode there's only database 0, so `SWAPDB` has nothing to swap. Remove the call.

errors.message: ERR SYNC and PSYNC are invalid with pending output
ERR syntax error
errors.explain: Redis couldn't make sense of the command's options. An option is misspelled, in the wrong place, missing its value, or combined with one it can't be used with, such as `NX` with `XX`. Compare each option with the command's syntax.

errors.message: ERR Syntax error in HELLO option '<option>'
errors.example: ERR Syntax error in HELLO option 'foo'
errors.explain: `HELLO` got an option it doesn't understand, shown in the message, or an option without all its values. The options are `SETNAME` with a name, and `AUTH` with both a user name and a password; use `default` as the user name for a plain password.

errors.message: ERR syntax error, expected IDS keyword
errors.explain: You ran `XNACK` without the `IDS` block. Add `IDS`, the number of IDs, and the entry IDs after the mode.

errors.message: ERR syntax error, IDMP requires a non-empty idempotent ID
errors.explain: You passed `XADD` the `IDMP` option with an empty idempotent ID, the second value after `IDMP`. Pass a non-empty string that identifies this message, so that Redis can recognize a repeated `XADD`.

errors.message: ERR syntax error, IDMP requires a non-empty producer ID
errors.explain: You passed `XADD` the `IDMP` option with an empty producer ID, the first value after `IDMP`. Pass a non-empty string that identifies the producer.

errors.message: ERR syntax error, IDMP/IDMPAUTO can be used only with auto-generated IDs
errors.explain: You used `IDMP` or `IDMPAUTO` in `XADD` with an entry ID that you chose. Pass `*` as the ID so that Redis generates it; idempotent adds work only with generated IDs.

errors.message: ERR syntax error, IDMP/IDMPAUTO specified multiple times
errors.explain: You passed `IDMP` or `IDMPAUTO` more than once in one `XADD`, or passed both. Use only one of them, once.

errors.message: ERR syntax error, IDMPAUTO requires a non-empty producer ID
errors.explain: You passed `XADD` the `IDMPAUTO` option with an empty producer ID. Pass a non-empty string that identifies the producer; Redis computes the idempotent ID from the fields and values.

errors.message: ERR syntax error, LIMIT cannot be used without specifying a trimming strategy
errors.explain: You passed `LIMIT` without `MAXLEN` or `MINID`, so there's no trim for it to limit. Add a trimming option, for example `MAXLEN ~ 1000 LIMIT 100`, or remove `LIMIT`.

errors.message: ERR syntax error, LIMIT cannot be used without the special ~ option
errors.explain: You passed `LIMIT` with an exact trim. `LIMIT` only works with approximate trimming, so put `~` after `MAXLEN` or `MINID`, or remove `LIMIT`.

errors.message: ERR syntax error, LIMIT is only supported in combination with either BYSCORE or BYLEX
errors.explain: You passed `LIMIT` to a range by index. `LIMIT` only works with `BYSCORE` or `BYLEX`; for an index range, choose the start and stop indexes instead.

errors.message: ERR syntax error, MAXLEN and MINID options at the same time are not compatible
errors.explain: You passed both `MAXLEN` and `MINID`, or one of them twice. Choose one trimming strategy: `MAXLEN` keeps a number of entries, and `MINID` removes entries with IDs lower than the one you pass.

errors.message: ERR syntax error, WITHSCORES not supported in combination with BYLEX
errors.explain: You asked for `WITHSCORES` in a lexicographic range. `BYLEX` ranges expect all members to have the same score, so leave out `WITHSCORES`, or read scores with `ZSCORE` or `ZMSCORE`.

errors.message: ERR syntax error, XTRIM must be called with a trimming strategy
errors.explain: You ran `XTRIM` without `MAXLEN` or `MINID`. Add one of them with its threshold, for example `XTRIM key MAXLEN 1000`.

errors.message: ERR Target instance replied with error: <error>
errors.explain: `MIGRATE` reached the target server, but the target replied with the error after the colon. A common one is `BUSYKEY`, when the key already exists there and you didn't pass `REPLACE`. Others are wrong `AUTH` details or a database number that doesn't exist.

errors.message: ERR Target node is not a master
errors.explain: `CLUSTER SETSLOT` names a node that's a replica, and only primaries can serve slots or move them. Pass the ID of a primary, as shown by `CLUSTER NODES`.

errors.message: ERR TESTFAILED dense/sparse disagree
ERR TESTFAILED Register <register> should be <expected> but is <actual>
ERR TESTFAILED sparse encoding not used
ERR TESTFAILED Too big error. card:<cardinality> abserr:<error>

ERR The $ ID is meaningless in the context of XREADGROUP: you want to read the history of this consumer by specifying a proper ID, or use the > ID to get new messages. The $ ID would just return an empty result set.
errors.explain: You passed `$` as an ID to `XREADGROUP`, but `$` only works with `XREAD`. Use `>` to get messages that the group hasn't delivered yet, or an ID such as `0` to reread this consumer's pending messages.

errors.message: ERR The 'default' user cannot be removed
errors.explain: `ACL DELUSER` can't delete the `default` user, and none of the users in the command were deleted. Remove `default` from the list. To stop clients from using it, give it a password or disable it with `ACL SETUSER`.

errors.message: ERR The + ID is meaningless in the context of XREADGROUP: you want to read the history of this consumer by specifying a proper ID, or use the > ID to get new messages. The + ID would just return an empty result set.
errors.explain: You passed `+` as an ID to `XREADGROUP`, but `+` only works with `XREAD`. Use `>` to get messages that the group hasn't delivered yet, or an ID such as `0` to reread this consumer's pending messages.

errors.message: ERR The > ID can be specified only when calling XREADGROUP using the GROUP <group> <consumer> option.
errors.explain: You passed `>` as an ID to `XREAD`, but `>` means messages not yet delivered to a consumer group, so it only works with `XREADGROUP`. With `XREAD`, use `$` for new entries only, or an ID to read the entries after it.

errors.message: ERR The `numfields` parameter must match the number of arguments
errors.explain: The number after `FIELDS` doesn't match the number of field names that follow it. Make the count equal to the number of fields you list.

errors.message: ERR The `numids` parameter must match the number of arguments
errors.explain: The number after `IDS` is larger than the number of IDs that follow it. Make the count equal to the number of entry IDs you list.

errors.message: ERR the ANY argument requires COUNT argument
errors.explain: You passed `ANY` to a geospatial search without `COUNT`. `ANY` stops the search as soon as it has found enough matches, so it needs `COUNT` to say how many, as in `COUNT 10 ANY`.

errors.message: ERR The bit argument must be 1 or 0.
errors.explain: `BITPOS` looks for the first bit with a given value, so the bit argument must be `0` or `1`. Pass `1` to find the first set bit, or `0` to find the first clear bit.

errors.message: ERR The CLAIM option is only supported by XREADGROUP. You called XREAD instead.
errors.explain: You passed `CLAIM` to `XREAD`, but claiming pending entries needs a consumer group, so only `XREADGROUP` supports it. Use `XREADGROUP` with `GROUP`, or remove `CLAIM`.

errors.message: ERR The client ID you want redirect to does not exist
errors.explain: No open connection has the client ID you passed after `REDIRECT` in `CLIENT TRACKING`. Get the ID with `CLIENT ID` on the connection that should receive the invalidation messages, and check that it's still open.

errors.message: ERR The command has no key arguments
errors.explain: You passed `COMMAND GETKEYS` or `COMMAND GETKEYSANDFLAGS` a command that never takes keys, such as `PING`. There are no keys to find, so you don't need to ask for this command.

errors.message: ERR The entries_added specified in XSETID is smaller than the target stream length
errors.explain: In `XSETID`, the `ENTRIESADDED` value is smaller than the number of entries now in the stream. Pass a count at least as large as the stream's length, which `XLEN` returns.

errors.message: ERR The GROUP option is only supported by XREADGROUP. You called XREAD instead.
errors.explain: You passed `GROUP` to `XREAD`. To read as a member of a consumer group, call `XREADGROUP` with the same arguments instead.

errors.message: ERR The ID specified in XADD is equal or smaller than the target stream top item
errors.explain: The entry ID you passed to `XADD` isn't greater than the last ID the stream used, even if that entry was deleted, and stream IDs must always increase. Use `*` to let Redis generate the ID, or pass a larger ID.

errors.message: ERR The ID specified in XADD must be greater than 0-0
errors.explain: You passed `0-0` as the entry ID to `XADD`, but the smallest valid ID is `0-1`. Use `*` to let Redis generate the ID, or pass a larger one.

errors.message: ERR The ID specified in XSETID is smaller than current max_deleted_entry_id
errors.explain: `XSETID` would set the stream's last ID lower than the largest ID already deleted from it. Pass an ID at least as large as the `max-deleted-entry-id` that `XINFO STREAM` shows.

errors.message: ERR The ID specified in XSETID is smaller than the provided max_deleted_entry_id
errors.explain: In `XSETID`, the ID you passed is smaller than the `MAXDELETEDID` you passed with it, but the last ID can't be lower than the largest deleted ID. Raise the ID or lower `MAXDELETEDID`.

errors.message: ERR The ID specified in XSETID is smaller than the target stream top item
errors.explain: `XSETID` would set the stream's last ID lower than the ID of its newest entry. Pass an ID at least as large as the last entry's ID, which `XINFO STREAM` shows.

errors.message: ERR The LIMIT argument must be >= 0.
errors.explain: You passed `XADD` or `XTRIM` a negative `LIMIT`. Pass 0 or more; `LIMIT` caps how many entries an approximate trim, with `~`, removes.

errors.message: ERR The MAXLEN argument must be >= 0.
errors.explain: You passed `XADD` or `XTRIM` a negative `MAXLEN`. Pass the number of entries to keep, 0 or more.

errors.message: ERR The NOACK option is only supported by XREADGROUP. You called XREAD instead.
errors.explain: You passed `NOACK` to `XREAD`, but only consumer groups track acknowledgments, so only `XREADGROUP` supports it. Remove `NOACK`, or read with `XREADGROUP`.

errors.message: ERR The server is running without a config file
errors.explain: `CONFIG REWRITE` saves settings to the configuration file that the server started with, and this server started without one. Start Redis with the path of a configuration file to use this command.

errors.message: ERR the slot <slot> is served by this node
errors.explain: `TRIMSLOTS` deletes the keys of slots that a primary no longer serves, and the slot in the message is still served by this node. Check the slot's owner with `CLUSTER SHARDS`. Nodes normally send this command themselves after a migration.

errors.message: ERR The specified key does not exist
ERR The specified keys must contain string values
errors.explain: One of the keys you passed to `LCS` holds a value that isn't a string, such as a list or a hash. Pass two keys that hold strings; a key that doesn't exist counts as an empty string.

errors.message: ERR The specified node is not a master
errors.explain: `CLUSTER REPLICAS` takes the node ID of a primary, and the node you passed is a replica. Pass the ID of its primary instead, which `CLUSTER NODES` shows.

errors.message: ERR The stream has exhausted the last possible ID, unable to add more items
errors.explain: The stream's last ID is already the largest possible, `18446744073709551615-18446744073709551615`, so `XADD` can't create a newer one. This follows an `XADD` or `XSETID` with a huge ID; delete the stream and recreate it with normal IDs.

errors.message: ERR The user can assign a config epoch only when the node does not know any other node.
errors.explain: `CLUSTER SET-CONFIG-EPOCH` works only before the node has met any other node. While you create the cluster, run it on each node before `CLUSTER MEET`.

errors.message: ERR The value stored at the specified key is not represented using an hash table
ERR The XGROUP subcommand requires the key to exist. Note that for CREATE you may want to use the MKSTREAM option to create an empty stream automatically.
errors.explain: The stream key you passed to `XGROUP` doesn't exist. Create the stream first, or add the `MKSTREAM` option to `XGROUP CREATE` so that it creates an empty stream.

errors.message: ERR There is a pending trim job for slot <slot>. Most probably, this is due to a failed atomic slot migration. CLUSTER SETSLOT cannot be used at this time. Please retry later once the trim job is completed.
errors.explain: This node is still deleting keys of the slot in the message, usually left over from a failed atomic slot migration, so `CLUSTER SETSLOT` can't change the slot now. Wait for the deletion to finish, then retry.

errors.message: ERR There was an error trying to save the ACLs. Please check the server logs for more information
errors.explain: `ACL SAVE` couldn't write the access control list (ACL) file set by `aclfile`, for example because its directory isn't writable or the disk is full. The server log has the exact reason. The users in memory are unchanged.

errors.message: ERR This instance has cluster support disabled
errors.explain: You ran a cluster command, such as `CLUSTER INFO`, `READONLY`, or `ASKING`, on a server that isn't running in cluster mode. Connect to a cluster node instead, or start this server with `cluster-enabled yes` if you're building a cluster.

errors.message: ERR this node is already the owner of the slot range
errors.explain: You asked this node to import slots that it already serves. Run `CLUSTER MIGRATION IMPORT` on the node that should receive the slots.

errors.message: ERR This node is not the owner of the slots
errors.explain: The importing node asked this node for slots that this node doesn't serve. This usually means the nodes don't agree yet on who owns the slots. Wait for the cluster configuration to settle, check the owner with `CLUSTER SHARDS`, and import again.

errors.message: ERR This Redis command is not allowed from script script: <script>, on <source>:<line>.
errors.example: ERR This Redis command is not allowed from script script: c329a1a294be6bf95b44144f7502610661ae925a, on @user_script:1.
errors.explain: Your script or function called a command that can't run inside scripts, such as `SUBSCRIBE`, `MULTI`, `WATCH`, `EVAL`, or `FUNCTION LOAD`. Run that command from your client instead.

errors.message: ERR This Redis instance is not configured to use an ACL file. You may want to specify users via the ACL SETUSER command and then issue a CONFIG REWRITE (assuming you have a Redis configuration file set) in order to store users in the Redis configuration.
errors.explain: `ACL LOAD` and `ACL SAVE` work only when the server was started with the `aclfile` setting, and this one wasn't. Set `aclfile` in the configuration file and restart, or keep users in the configuration file with `CONFIG REWRITE`.

errors.message: ERR timeout is negative
errors.explain: The timeout you passed is negative. Pass 0 or more; for blocking commands, 0 means wait with no time limit.

errors.message: ERR timeout is not a float or out of range
errors.explain: The timeout you passed to a blocking list or sorted set command isn't a number. Pass it in seconds, as a decimal such as `0.5` if you need to, or 0 to wait with no time limit.

errors.message: ERR timeout is not an integer or out of range
errors.explain: The timeout you passed isn't a whole number. `XREAD` and `XREADGROUP` with `BLOCK`, `WAIT`, `WAITAOF` and `CLIENT PAUSE` take the timeout in milliseconds, as an integer such as `1500`.

errors.message: ERR timeout is out of range
errors.explain: The timeout is so large that adding it to the current time would overflow. `BLPOP` and the other blocking list and sorted set commands take seconds, while `XREAD`, `WAIT`, `WAITAOF`, and `CLIENT PAUSE` take milliseconds; pass a smaller value, or `0` to make a blocking command wait forever.

errors.message: ERR To set a master the node must be empty and without assigned slots.
errors.explain: A primary can become a replica only when it has no hash slots and no keys. Move its slots to other nodes and delete its keys, for example with `FLUSHALL`, then run `CLUSTER REPLICATE` again.

errors.message: ERR too many predicates, maximum is 250
errors.explain: You passed `ARGREP` more than 250 predicates (`EXACT`, `MATCH`, `GLOB` or `RE`). Combine conditions into fewer predicates, for example one regular expression, or split the search into several calls.

errors.message: ERR Trim is disabled by module
errors.explain: A module on this node has paused the deletion of migrated keys, so the node won't start a new slot migration. For example, Redis Search does this for a short time after a migration while indexes exist. Wait, then start the import again.

errors.message: ERR Trim job in progress for the slots
errors.explain: This node is still deleting the keys of some of the requested slots, so it can't send those slots yet. Wait for the deletion to finish, then start the import again.

errors.message: ERR UBOUND is not a valid float
errors.explain: With `BYFLOAT`, `INCREX` reads `UBOUND` as a decimal number, and the value you passed isn't one. Pass a number such as `100` or `99.5`.

errors.message: ERR UBOUND is not an integer or out of range
errors.explain: Without `BYFLOAT`, `INCREX` reads `UBOUND` as a 64-bit integer, and the value you passed isn't one. Pass a whole number, or add `BYFLOAT` to use decimal bounds.

errors.message: ERR Unbalanced 'xread' list of streams: for each stream key an ID, '+', or '$' must be specified.
errors.explain: After `STREAMS`, `XREAD` needs all the keys and then one ID for each key, so the number of arguments after `STREAMS` must be even. Add the missing IDs, using `$` to read only new entries, or remove the stray argument.

errors.message: ERR Unbalanced 'xreadgroup' list of streams: for each stream key an ID or '>' must be specified.
errors.explain: After `STREAMS`, `XREADGROUP` needs all the keys and then one ID for each key, so the number of arguments after `STREAMS` must be even. Add the missing IDs, using `>` for new messages, or remove the stray argument.

errors.message: ERR Unexpected engine in script shebang: <engine>
errors.example: ERR Unexpected engine in script shebang: #!foo
errors.explain: The first line of your script names an engine other than Lua, shown in the message. `EVAL` and `SCRIPT LOAD` accept only `#!lua`, in lowercase and with no space after `#!`.

errors.message: ERR Unexpected flag in script shebang: <flag>
errors.example: ERR Unexpected flag in script shebang: foo
errors.explain: A flag in the `flags=` list of your script's shebang line isn't one Redis knows, as the message shows. Valid flags are `no-writes`, `allow-oom`, `allow-stale`, `no-cluster`, and `allow-cross-slot-keys`, in lowercase and separated by commas without spaces.

errors.message: ERR unknown argument
errors.explain: `CLUSTER MIGRATION` didn't recognize an argument. The subcommands are `IMPORT`, `STATUS`, and `CANCEL`, and `STATUS` and `CANCEL` take either `ID` followed by a task ID, or `ALL`.

errors.message: ERR Unknown argument <argument>
errors.explain: `FUNCTION LIST` got the argument in the message, but it accepts only `WITHCODE` and `LIBRARYNAME` followed by a pattern, each at most once. Remove the unknown or repeated argument.

errors.message: ERR unknown argument: <argument>
errors.explain: The command got an argument it doesn't recognize, shown in the message. Check the option names, and check that the number after `FIELDS` matches the fields you list, because extra fields are read as options.

errors.message: ERR Unknown category '<category>'
errors.example: ERR Unknown category 'foo'
errors.explain: `ACL CAT` doesn't know the category in the message. Run `ACL CAT` with no argument to list the valid categories, and pass the name without the `@` sign.

errors.message: ERR Unknown client type '<type>'
errors.example: ERR Unknown client type 'foo'
errors.explain: The client type you passed to `CLIENT LIST TYPE` or `CLIENT KILL TYPE` isn't one Redis knows. Use `normal`, `master`, `replica` (or `slave`), or `pubsub`.

errors.message: ERR unknown command '<command>'
errors.example: ERR unknown command 'foo'
errors.explain: This server doesn't know the command named in the message. Check the spelling, that your Redis version has the command, that the module that adds it is loaded, and that it isn't renamed or disabled with `rename-command`.

errors.message: ERR unknown command '<command>', with args beginning with: <args>
errors.example: ERR unknown command 'foo', with args beginning with: 'bar' 'baz'
errors.explain: This server doesn't know the command named in the message; the message also shows the first arguments to help you find the call. Check the spelling, that your Redis version has the command, and that the module that adds it is loaded.

errors.message: ERR Unknown direction <direction>
ERR Unknown Error for creating instances.
errors.explain: Sentinel failed to add the primary in `SENTINEL MONITOR` for a reason it doesn't recognize. The known causes have their own messages, so this is unexpected; check the Sentinel log and the arguments, and try again.

errors.message: ERR Unknown failure simulation specified
ERR Unknown georadius search type
errors.explain: A geospatial search command reached Redis with an internal search type that Redis doesn't recognize. No arguments that you pass can cause this, so report it as a bug.

errors.message: ERR Unknown lua shebang option: <option>
errors.example: ERR Unknown lua shebang option: foo=bar
errors.explain: The shebang line of your script has an option other than `flags=`, the only option scripts accept. A space inside the flags list causes this too, as does `name=`, which only function libraries use; write flags as `flags=no-writes,allow-oom`.

errors.message: ERR Unknown node <node_id>
errors.explain: This node doesn't know a node with the ID in the message. Check the ID with `CLUSTER NODES` on this node. IDs are 40 characters long, and a node that joined recently may not be known yet.

errors.message: ERR unknown operation
errors.explain: You ran `AROP` with an operation it doesn't support. Use one of `SUM`, `MIN`, `MAX`, `AND`, `OR`, `XOR`, `MATCH` or `USED`.

errors.message: ERR Unknown option <option>
errors.explain: A `CLUSTER SYNCSLOTS CONF` message carried an option this node doesn't know. Nodes send this message to each other during an atomic slot migration, so this usually means they run different Redis versions. Upgrade all nodes to the same version.

errors.message: ERR Unknown option given: <option>
errors.example: ERR Unknown option given: BADOPT
errors.explain: `FUNCTION LOAD` got an option it doesn't know before the library code; `REPLACE` is its only option. This also happens when the code is split across several arguments, so pass the whole library as one quoted argument.

errors.message: ERR Unknown option or number of arguments for CONFIG SET - '<parameter>'
errors.example: ERR Unknown option or number of arguments for CONFIG SET - 'foo'
errors.explain: `CONFIG SET` doesn't know the parameter in the message. Check the spelling with `CONFIG GET`, and for a module setting, check that the module is loaded.

errors.message: ERR Unknown option or number of arguments for SENTINEL DEBUG '<option>'
ERR Unknown option or number of arguments for SENTINEL SET '<option>'
errors.explain: You ran `SENTINEL SET` with an option it doesn't know, or without the value it needs, such as a last option with no value or `rename-command` with one name. Check the option and its value. Options before it in the same command were already applied.

errors.message: ERR Unknown PFDEBUG subcommand '<subcommand>'
errors.example: ERR Unknown PFDEBUG subcommand 'foo'

errors.message: ERR Unknown Redis command called from script script: <script>, on <source>:<line>.
errors.example: ERR Unknown Redis command called from script script: 4f5958446b28593dea988ad0a5603cbd6962dd95, on @user_script:1.
errors.explain: Your script or function called `redis.call` or `redis.pcall` with a command name that doesn't exist, often a typo or a command from a module that isn't loaded. Pass a subcommand as a separate argument, as in `redis.call('CONFIG', 'GET', 'maxmemory')`.

errors.message: ERR unknown subcommand '<subcommand>'. Try <command> HELP.
errors.example: ERR unknown subcommand 'foo'. Try CLIENT HELP.
errors.explain: The command named in the message doesn't have the subcommand you passed. Run the command followed by `HELP`, for example `CLIENT HELP`, to list its subcommands, and check that your Redis version has the one you want.

errors.message: ERR unknown subcommand or wrong number of arguments
errors.explain: `HOTKEYS` got a subcommand it doesn't know, or the wrong number of arguments for one. The subcommands are `START`, `STOP`, `GET`, `RESET`, and `HELP`.

errors.message: ERR unknown subcommand or wrong number of arguments for '<subcommand>'. Try <command> HELP.
errors.example: ERR unknown subcommand or wrong number of arguments for 'nosuchsub'. Try DEBUG HELP.
errors.explain: You called a command that has subcommands, such as `CONFIG` or `XINFO`, with a subcommand it doesn't have, or with the wrong number of arguments for that subcommand. Run the `HELP` subcommand named in the message to list the valid forms.

errors.message: ERR unknown type object
errors.explain: `COPY` found a key whose data type it doesn't know how to duplicate. Every built-in and module type is handled, so this points to an internal problem; report it as a bug, with the key's `TYPE` and `OBJECT ENCODING`.

errors.message: ERR Unmatched parenthesis in acl selector starting at '<argument>'.
errors.example: ERR Unmatched parenthesis in acl selector starting at '(+get'.
errors.explain: A selector in your `ACL SETUSER` rules starts with `(` but is never closed with `)`. The message shows the argument where the selector starts. Close the selector, for example `(~app:* +get)`.

errors.message: ERR Unrecognized option '<option>'
errors.explain: `CLIENT SETINFO` only accepts the `lib-name` and `lib-ver` options, and got the option in the message. Use one of those two, which client libraries set to report their name and version.

errors.message: ERR Unrecognized RDB client id: <client_id>
ERR Unrecognized REPLCONF option: <option>
ERR Unrecognized sort metric for ORDERBY.
errors.explain: `CLUSTER SLOT-STATS ORDERBY` got a metric it doesn't know, or one that isn't turned on. `key-count` always works, but `cpu-usec`, `network-bytes-in`, `network-bytes-out`, and `memory-bytes` need the matching `cluster-slot-stats-enabled` setting.

errors.message: ERR Unrecognized XCLAIM option '<option>'
errors.explain: `XCLAIM` didn't recognize the argument shown in the message. It also reads invalid entry IDs as options, so check both the IDs and the option names: `IDLE`, `TIME`, `RETRYCOUNT`, `FORCE`, `JUSTID` and `LASTID`.

errors.message: ERR Unrecognized XNACK option '<option>'
errors.explain: `XNACK` didn't recognize the argument shown in the message. Use only `IDS`, `RETRYCOUNT` and `FORCE`, and check that the number after `IDS` matches the IDs you list, because extra IDs are read as options.

errors.message: ERR Unsupported option <option>
errors.example: ERR Unsupported option FOO
errors.explain: An expire command got an argument after the time that isn't `NX`, `XX`, `GT`, or `LT`, shown in the message. Remove it, and check that you didn't add the time unit as a separate word, as in `EXPIRE key 10 seconds`.

errors.message: ERR Unsupported rdb-filter-only option: <option>
ERR unsupported unit provided. please use M, KM, FT, MI
errors.explain: The unit isn't one of `m` (meters), `km` (kilometers), `ft` (feet), or `mi` (miles), in any case. Pass one of these as a separate argument after the distance.

errors.message: ERR Use SCRIPT DEBUG YES/SYNC/NO
errors.explain: You passed `SCRIPT DEBUG` a mode other than `YES`, `SYNC`, or `NO`. `YES` debugs in a forked copy of the server, `SYNC` debugs in the server itself and blocks it meanwhile, and `NO` turns debugging off.

errors.message: ERR User '<username>' not found
errors.example: ERR User 'nouser' not found
errors.explain: `ACL DRYRUN` doesn't know the user in the message. Check the name with `ACL USERS`. Usernames are case-sensitive.

errors.message: ERR user_script:<line>: Script attempted to access nonexistent global variable '<name>' script: <script>, on <source>:<line>.
errors.example: ERR user_script:1: Script attempted to access nonexistent global variable 'foo' script: 47e30a5d10d5694f99208f9adc4fe3bf2450edbd, on @user_script:1.
errors.explain: Your script or function read a global variable that doesn't exist, named in the message, often because of a typo, a missing `local`, or a library that Redis doesn't load, such as `io`. Declare your variables with `local`, and pass data in as keys and arguments.

errors.message: ERR Usernames can't contain spaces or null characters
errors.explain: The username you passed to `ACL SETUSER` contains a space, another whitespace character, or a null character, which usernames can't have. Choose a name without them.

errors.message: ERR value cannot be Infinity
errors.explain: The key's current value is infinity, for example stored as `inf`, so `INCREX` with `BYFLOAT` can't add to it. Set the key to a finite number first.

errors.message: ERR value count does not match fieldset field count
errors.explain: `HIMPORT SET` got a different number of values than the fieldset has fields. Pass one value for each field, in the order you listed the fields in `HIMPORT PREPARE`.

errors.message: ERR value for ENTRIESREAD must be positive or -1
errors.explain: You passed `XGROUP CREATE` or `XGROUP SETID` an `ENTRIESREAD` lower than -1. Pass the number of entries the group has read, 0 or more, or -1 if you don't know it.

errors.message: ERR value is NaN or Infinity
errors.explain: You passed `HINCRBYFLOAT` an increment of infinity, such as `inf`. Pass a finite number.

errors.message: ERR value is not a valid float
errors.explain: An argument that must be a number, such as a score, coordinate, or increment, isn't one; for `INCRBYFLOAT`, the value already in the key can be the problem. Write the number with digits, a dot, and an optional exponent, such as `3.5` or `1e3`, without units or commas.

errors.message: ERR value is not an integer or out of range
errors.explain: An argument that must be a whole number isn't one, or it's outside the signed 64-bit range; for commands such as `INCR`, the value already in the key can be the problem. Write the number with digits only, without decimals or units, such as `10` or `-3`.

errors.message: ERR value is out of range
errors.explain: You called `HRANDFIELD` with `WITHVALUES`, or `ZRANDMEMBER` with `WITHSCORES`, and a count whose absolute value is larger than 4611686018427387903. Pass a smaller count.

errors.message: ERR value is out of range, must be positive
errors.explain: An argument that must be a count of 0 or more is negative or isn't an integer, such as the count of `LPOP`, `RPOP`, `SPOP`, `ZPOPMIN`, or `ZPOPMAX`, or the numreplicas argument of `WAITAOF`. Despite the message, `0` is accepted.

errors.message: ERR value is out of range, value must between <min> and <max>
errors.explain: An integer argument is outside the range it accepts, and the message gives the smallest and largest allowed values. For example, the numlocal argument of `WAITAOF` must be `0` or `1`, and a database number for `SELECT`, `MOVE`, or `COPY` must fit in 32 bits.

errors.message: ERR WAIT cannot be used with replica instances. Please also note that since Redis 4.0 if a replica is configured to be writable (which is not the default) writes to replicas are just local and are not propagated.
errors.explain: You sent `WAIT` to a replica, but it only works on a primary, where it waits for replicas to acknowledge your writes. Send your writes and `WAIT` to the primary.

errors.message: ERR WAITAOF cannot be used when numlocal is set but appendonly is disabled.
errors.explain: You asked `WAITAOF` to wait for the local append-only file (AOF), with numlocal set to 1, but `appendonly` is off. Turn on `appendonly`, or pass 0 as numlocal to wait only for replicas.

errors.message: ERR WAITAOF cannot be used with replica instances. Please also note that writes to replicas are just local and are not propagated.
errors.explain: You sent `WAITAOF` to a replica, but it only works on a primary. Send your writes and `WAITAOF` to the primary instead.

errors.message: ERR WARNING: Duplicate user '<username>' found on line <line>.
errors.explain: The access control list (ACL) file defines the same user twice, the second time on the line in the message. Despite the WARNING label, this is an error, and `ACL LOAD` changed nothing. Remove or merge the duplicate line.

errors.message: ERR WATCH inside MULTI is not allowed
errors.explain: You sent `WATCH` after `MULTI`, but keys must be watched before the transaction starts. The transaction stays open; to watch keys, end it with `DISCARD`, then send `WATCH` before `MULTI`.

errors.message: ERR weight value is not a float
errors.explain: A value after `WEIGHTS` isn't a number. Pass one number for each input key, in the same order as the keys.

errors.message: ERR When using MIGRATE KEYS option, the key argument must be set to the empty string
errors.explain: With the `KEYS` option, `MIGRATE` takes its keys from the end of the command, so the single key argument must be empty. Pass `""` in place of the key, then list the keys after `KEYS`.

errors.message: ERR Write commands are not allowed from read-only scripts. script: <script>, on <source>:<line>.
errors.explain: Your script called a command that writes, but it runs read-only, because you called it with `EVAL_RO`, `EVALSHA_RO`, or `FCALL_RO`, or because it has the `no-writes` flag. Remove the write, or remove the flag and call it with `EVAL`, `EVALSHA`, or `FCALL`.

errors.message: ERR Wrong number of args calling Redis command from script script: <script>, on <source>:<line>.
errors.example: ERR Wrong number of args calling Redis command from script script: f187dee77f607f7cff00bbabc9df38507582c78d, on @user_script:1.
errors.explain: Your script or function called a command through `redis.call` or `redis.pcall` with the wrong number of arguments for that command. Compare the call with the command's syntax, and pass each argument as a separate Lua value.

errors.message: ERR Wrong number of args for redis.acl_check_cmd() script: <script>, on <source>:<line>.
errors.explain: Your script called `redis.acl_check_cmd()` with a number of arguments that the named command doesn't accept. Pass the command with the full list of arguments you want to check, as you would pass them to `redis.call()`.

errors.message: ERR wrong number of arguments
errors.explain: The number after `FIELDS` is larger than the number of fields, or field and value pairs for `HSETEX`, that follow it. Make the count match what you list.

errors.message: ERR wrong number of arguments for '<command>' command
errors.example: ERR wrong number of arguments for 'get' command
errors.explain: The command named in the message got more or fewer arguments than it accepts. Compare your call with the command's syntax, and check for an empty list of keys or fields, or a value with spaces that wasn't quoted.

errors.message: ERR wrong number of arguments for 'hotkeys|get' command
errors.explain: You passed arguments to `HOTKEYS GET`, which takes none. Run `HOTKEYS GET` on its own to get the results of the current or last tracking session.

errors.message: ERR wrong number of arguments for 'hotkeys|reset' command
errors.explain: You passed arguments to `HOTKEYS RESET`, which takes none. Run `HOTKEYS RESET` on its own, after `HOTKEYS STOP`, to free the tracking results.

errors.message: ERR wrong number of arguments for 'hotkeys|stop' command
errors.explain: You passed arguments to `HOTKEYS STOP`, which takes none. Run `HOTKEYS STOP` on its own to end the tracking session.

errors.message: ERR Wrong number of arguments for the '<subcommand>' subcommand
ERR wrong number of arguments script: <script>, on <source>:<line>.
errors.explain: Your script called `redis.sha1hex()` with no argument or with more than one. Pass exactly one string, the value to hash.

errors.message: ERR wrong number of key-value pairs
errors.explain: The number of keys you passed to `MSETEX` is larger than the number of key and value pairs that follow it. Make the count match the pairs, and check for a missing value.

errors.message: ERR wrong number or type of arguments
errors.explain: Your script called `redis.error_reply()` or `redis.status_reply()` with no argument, more than one, or a value that isn't a string, such as a number. Pass exactly one string, for example `redis.error_reply('ERR invalid input')`.

errors.message: ERR Wrong protocol type name. Please use one of the following: string|integer|double|bignum|null|array|set|map|attrib|push|verbatim|true|false
ERR Wrong restore policy given, value should be either FLUSH, APPEND or REPLACE.
errors.explain: You passed `FUNCTION RESTORE` a policy other than `FLUSH`, `APPEND`, or `REPLACE`. `APPEND`, the default, fails on name conflicts, `REPLACE` overwrites libraries with the same name, and `FLUSH` deletes all libraries first.

errors.message: ERR XX and NX options at the same time are not compatible
errors.explain: You passed both `XX` and `NX` to `ZADD`. Use `NX` to only add new members, or `XX` to only update existing ones.

errors.message: ERR You can't specify both OPTIN mode and OPTOUT mode
errors.explain: You passed both `OPTIN` and `OPTOUT` to `CLIENT TRACKING`. Choose one: `OPTIN` tracks only the reads after `CLIENT CACHING YES`, and `OPTOUT` tracks all reads except those after `CLIENT CACHING NO`.

errors.message: ERR You can't switch BCAST mode on/off before disabling tracking for this client, and then re-enabling it with a different mode.
errors.explain: Tracking is already on for this connection, and you tried to turn `BCAST` on or off with another `CLIENT TRACKING ON`. Run `CLIENT TRACKING OFF` first, then turn tracking on again with the new mode.

errors.message: ERR You can't switch OPTIN/OPTOUT mode before disabling tracking for this client, and then re-enabling it with a different mode.
errors.explain: Tracking is already on in `OPTIN` or `OPTOUT` mode, and you tried to switch to the other mode. Run `CLIENT TRACKING OFF` first, then turn tracking on again with the new mode.

errors.message: ERR You should send CLUSTER FAILOVER to a replica
errors.explain: `CLUSTER FAILOVER` promotes the replica that receives it, and this node is already a primary. Send the command to one of its replicas instead.

errors.message: ERR '-' can only be used as first argument, '+' only as second
errors.explain: In `VRANGE`, `-` means the lowest element and `+` the highest, so `-` works only as the start and `+` only as the end. Swap them: `-` followed by `+` returns every element.

errors.message: ERR asked M value mismatch with existing vector set
errors.explain: The `M` value in `VADD` differs from the one the set was created with, and it can't change. Pass the same `M` on every `VADD`, or leave it out if the set uses the default of 16. `VINFO` shows the set's value as `hnsw-m`.

errors.message: ERR asked quantization mismatch with existing vector set
errors.explain: The quantization option in `VADD` (`NOQUANT`, `Q8`, or `BIN`) differs from the one the set was created with, and it can't change. Pass the same option on every `VADD`; leaving it out means `Q8`. `VINFO` shows the set's type as `quant-type`.

errors.message: ERR cannot add projection to existing set without projection
errors.explain: You passed `REDUCE` to `VADD` for a set that was created without it. Only the first `VADD`, which creates the set, can turn on dimension reduction. Remove `REDUCE`, or create a new set with `REDUCE`.

errors.message: ERR COUNT value is not an integer
errors.explain: The count you passed to `VRANDMEMBER` isn't an integer. Pass a whole number: a positive count returns up to that many distinct elements, and a negative count returns that many elements, possibly with repeats.

errors.message: ERR COUNT value is out of range
errors.explain: You passed -9223372036854775808, the smallest 64-bit integer, as the count of `VRANDMEMBER`. Its absolute value doesn't fit in 64 bits, so Redis rejects it. Use a smaller negative count.

errors.message: ERR element not found in set
errors.explain: You called `VSIM` with `ELE`, but the element you named isn't in the vector set. Element names are case-sensitive. Check the name with `VISMEMBER`, or pass the vector itself with `VALUES` or `FP32`.

errors.message: ERR Input dimension mismatch for projection - got <dimension> but projection expects <projection_dimension>
errors.explain: The set was created with `REDUCE`, which fixed how many values each input vector must have, and your vector has a different number. Send vectors of the dimension that the message says the projection expects. `VSIM` also accepts vectors that already have the reduced dimension.

errors.message: ERR invalid COUNT value
errors.explain: The count, the last argument of `VRANGE`, isn't an integer. Pass a whole number for the maximum number of elements to return; a negative count returns every element in the range.

errors.message: ERR invalid EF
errors.explain: The `EF` value of `VADD` or `VSIM` isn't an integer from 1 to 1000000. Pass a value in that range. `VADD` uses 200 when you leave it out, and typical `VSIM` values are 50 to 1000.

errors.message: ERR invalid end range format
errors.explain: The end of the range in `VRANGE` isn't valid. Use `+` for the highest element, or an element name that starts with `[` (inclusive) or `(` (exclusive), such as `[apple`.

errors.message: ERR invalid EPSILON
errors.explain: The `EPSILON` value of `VSIM` isn't a number greater than 0. Pass the maximum distance for results, usually between 0 and 1: for example, `0.2` returns only elements with a similarity of 0.8 or better.

errors.message: ERR invalid FILTER-EF
errors.explain: The `FILTER-EF` value of `VSIM` isn't a positive integer. It limits how many elements `VSIM` checks against the `FILTER` expression. Pass a positive number, or leave it out to use 100 times `COUNT`.

errors.message: ERR invalid M
errors.explain: The `M` value of `VADD` isn't an integer from 4 to 4096. `M` sets the maximum number of links each element has in the set's search graph. The default is 16, and the first `VADD` fixes it for the set.

errors.message: ERR invalid option
errors.explain: `VEMB` takes only a key, an element name, and the optional `RAW` option. Remove any other argument after the element name, and quote an element name that contains spaces as one argument.

errors.message: ERR invalid option after element
errors.explain: `VADD` found an argument after the element name that it doesn't accept, or an option without its value. The options are `CAS`, `NOQUANT`, `Q8`, `BIN`, `EF`, `M`, and `SETATTR`, and they go after the element. Also check that the count after `VALUES` matches the number of values.

errors.message: ERR invalid start range format
errors.explain: The start of the range in `VRANGE` isn't valid. Use `-` for the lowest element, or an element name that starts with `[` (inclusive) or `(` (exclusive), such as `[apple`.

errors.message: ERR invalid vector dimension
errors.explain: The count after `VALUES` in `VSIM` isn't an integer. Pass the number of values that follow, such as `VALUES 3` before three numbers. In Redis 8.10, `VSIM` usually reports this as `ERR invalid vector specification` instead.

errors.message: ERR invalid vector specification
errors.explain: The vector in `VADD` or `VSIM` is malformed. Use `VALUES` with a count from 1 to 65536 and that many numbers, or `FP32` with a blob of 4 bytes per value. A `REDUCE` value in `VADD` must be a positive integer no larger than the vector's dimension.

errors.message: ERR key does not exist
errors.explain: You called `VDIM` on a key that doesn't exist. Unlike `VCARD`, which returns 0 for a missing key, `VDIM` returns this error. Check the key name, or create the set with `VADD` first.

errors.message: ERR projection dimension mismatch with existing set
errors.explain: The `REDUCE` value in `VADD` differs from the one the set was created with. Pass the same `REDUCE` value as the first `VADD`; `VINFO` shows it as `vector-dim`. In Redis 8.10, this case usually returns `ERR Vector dimension mismatch` instead.

errors.message: ERR syntax error in FILTER expression near: <expression>
errors.example: ERR syntax error in FILTER expression near: ((
errors.explain: The `FILTER` expression of `VSIM` has a syntax error. The message shows the expression from the point where parsing failed, or all of it. Check for unbalanced parentheses and for `=` where you mean `==`; field names start with a dot, as in `.year > 1950`.

errors.message: ERR syntax error in VSIM command
errors.explain: `VSIM` found an argument after the vector that it doesn't accept, or an option without its value, such as `COUNT` at the end. Check the options against the `VSIM` syntax, and check that the count after `VALUES` matches the number of values.

errors.message: ERR unable to create a Vector Set: system resources issue?
errors.explain: Redis couldn't set up the locks that a new vector set needs, which points to a problem with server resources, not with your command. Check the server log and the system's thread and memory limits, then retry.

errors.message: ERR Vector dimension mismatch - got <dimension> but set has <set_dimension>
errors.example: ERR Vector dimension mismatch - got 2 but set has 3
errors.explain: Your vector has a different number of values than the set, whose dimension the first `VADD` fixed. Send vectors of the dimension the message names. On a set created with `REDUCE`, every `VADD` must repeat that `REDUCE`, or you get this error even when both numbers match.

errors.message: ERR vector type must be ELE, FP32 or VALUES
errors.explain: The argument after the key in `VSIM` must say how you pass the query: `ELE` with an element name, `FP32` with a binary vector, or `VALUES` with a count and numbers. In Redis 8.10, an unknown type usually returns `ERR invalid vector specification` instead.

errors.message: <command> is not supported in Redis Flex
errors.explain: You only get this when Redis Search runs on Redis Flex, which doesn't support the command named in the message. Commands without Redis Flex support include `FT.HYBRID`, `FT.ALTER`, `FT.SPELLCHECK`, `FT.TAGVALS`, `FT.MGET`, and `FT.CURSOR`.

errors.message: <command> is not supported when disk is enabled
Aggregate results is not paused
Alias does not exist
errors.explain: `FT.ALIASDEL` can't find an alias with the name you gave. Check the name for typos. `FT.ALIASLIST` shows the aliases of an index.

errors.message: ALTER must be followed by SCHEMA
errors.explain: In `FT.ALTER`, the index name, and `SKIPINITIALSCAN` if you use it, must be followed by `SCHEMA ADD`. Use `FT.ALTER index [SKIPINITIALSCAN] SCHEMA ADD field type [options]`.

errors.message: Async I/O is not supported (disk API not available or disk doesn't support async I/O)
Bad cursor ID
errors.explain: The cursor ID that you passed to `FT.CURSOR READ` or `FT.CURSOR DEL` isn't an integer. Pass the cursor ID exactly as `FT.AGGREGATE` with `WITHCURSOR`, or the previous `FT.CURSOR READ`, returned it.

errors.message: bad distance given, distance must be a natural number between 1 to 4
errors.explain: The value of `DISTANCE` in `FT.SPELLCHECK`, the maximum Levenshtein distance for suggestions, isn't a whole number from 1 to 4. Use a value such as `DISTANCE 2`. The default is 1.

errors.message: bad format, exclude/include operation was not given
errors.explain: The word after `TERMS` in `FT.SPELLCHECK` must be `INCLUDE` or `EXCLUDE`. Use `TERMS INCLUDE dict` or `TERMS EXCLUDE dict`, with a dictionary that you created with `FT.DICTADD`.

errors.message: bad id given
bad reply returned
errors.explain: You only get this error in a cluster. A shard returned a result for one of the terms of `FT.SPELLCHECK` in a format that the coordinator doesn't expect. Run the command again, and report it to Redis if it continues.

errors.message: Bad value for ADDR: <argument> at offset <position>
Bad value for COUNT: `<argument>`
errors.example: Bad value for COUNT: `x`
errors.explain: The value after `COUNT` in `FT.CURSOR READ` isn't an integer, and the message shows what you passed. Give `COUNT` a whole number: the number of results to read in this call.

errors.message: Bad value for HASHFUNC: <function> at offset <position>
Bad value for NUMSLOTS: <argument> at offset <position>
Bad value for NUMSLOTS: <number> at offset <position>
Bad value for RANGES: <argument> at offset <position>
Bad value for SLOTRANGE end: <argument> at offset <position>
Bad value for SLOTRANGE start: <argument> at offset <position>
Bad values for SLOTRANGE: <start>, <end> at offset <position>
Can not create a search ctx
Can not find the inverted index
Can't open vector index
Can't set both documents and not-documents
Can't set both fields and not-fields
Cannot create index on db != 0
errors.explain: You can only create Redis Search indexes in database 0, but your connection selected another database with `SELECT`. Switch to database 0 with `SELECT 0`, and run `FT.CREATE` again.

errors.message: Cannot perform `<command>`: Cannot block
errors.explain: You only get this in a cluster with more than one shard. The command named in the message must wait for the other shards, which it can't do inside `MULTI` and `EXEC`, a Lua script, or a function. Run it outside the transaction or script.

errors.message: Command not supported for HNSW multi-value index
Command not supported in disk mode
Conflicting ADDR for shard `<shard_id>` at offset <position>
Conflicting UNIXADDR for shard `<shard_id>` at offset <position>
Coordinator reduce is not paused
could not analyze term result
errors.explain: You only get this error in a cluster. The coordinator couldn't read the suggestions that a shard returned for one of the terms of `FT.SPELLCHECK`. Run the command again, and report it to Redis if it continues.

errors.message: Could not distribute command
errors.explain: You only get this error in a cluster. Redis Search sent the command to the shards but got no reply from any of them, so it can't tell whether the command worked. Check that the shards are running and reachable, and then run the command again.

errors.message: Could not find given field in index spec
Could not open geoshape index
Could not parse argument (argspec fixme)
Could not perform query
errors.explain: You only get this from `FT.TAGVALS` in a cluster. No shard returned a list of values or an error, so the coordinator has nothing to reply with. Check that the shards are running and reachable, and run the command again.

errors.message: Could not process replies
errors.explain: You only get this from `FT.MGET` in a cluster. No shard returned a usable list of documents, so the coordinator has nothing to reply with. Check that the shards are running and reachable, and run the command again.

errors.message: Could not send query to cluster
errors.explain: You only get this error in a cluster. Redis Search couldn't send the command to the shards, because the connection to at least one shard isn't established, or the cluster topology isn't known yet. Check that all shards are running and reachable, and then run the command again.

errors.message: Cursor does not exist
errors.explain: `FT.CURSOR DEL` found no cursor with the ID that you gave. The cursor was already read to the end, deleted, or removed after it was idle longer than its `MAXIDLE` time (300000 milliseconds by default), so there's nothing left to delete.

errors.message: Cursor not found, id: <cursor_id>
errors.example: Cursor not found, id: 123
errors.explain: `FT.CURSOR READ` found no idle cursor with the ID in the message. A cursor is removed when you read its last results, when you delete it with `FT.CURSOR DEL`, or when it's idle longer than its `MAXIDLE` time (300000 milliseconds by default). Run `FT.AGGREGATE` with `WITHCURSOR` again to get a new cursor.

errors.message: Cursor READ in a context that cannot block (MULTI/EXEC or Lua scripts) is not supported in Redis Flex
errors.explain: You read a cursor of a Redis Flex index from a place where Redis can't block the client, such as a `MULTI`/`EXEC` transaction or a Lua script. Redis Flex has to wait for data from disk, so read the cursor with a separate command, outside the transaction or script. The cursor stays valid.

errors.message: cursor request is not profile, id: <cursor_id>
errors.explain: A shard was asked for the profile of a cursor that wasn't opened by `FT.PROFILE`. This comes from an internal command that the cluster sends to its shards, not from a command that you normally run. If you see it from `FT.PROFILE`, run the command again, and report it to Redis if it repeats.

errors.message: DD is not supported in Redis Flex
errors.explain: You only get this when Redis Search runs on Redis Flex, where `FT.DROPINDEX` can't delete the documents. Drop the index without `DD`, and delete the keys yourself if you need to.

errors.message: Debug commands are disabled, please follow the redis configuration guide to enable them
Debug mode enabled but scanner is not a debug scanner
Dict does not exist: <dictionary>
errors.example: Dict does not exist: nodict
errors.explain: `FT.SPELLCHECK` uses a dictionary in `TERMS INCLUDE` or `TERMS EXCLUDE` that doesn't exist; the message shows its name. Create the dictionary with `FT.DICTADD`, or fix the name.

errors.message: DISTANCE arg is given but no DISTANCE comes after
errors.explain: `DISTANCE` is the last argument of `FT.SPELLCHECK`, with no value after it. Add the maximum Levenshtein distance, a whole number from 1 to 4, such as `DISTANCE 2`.

errors.message: Document not found in index
document was removed
DUMP_TAGIDX not supported for disk-mode indexes
ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<config>') - <config>: value <value> is out of range
errors.example: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument 'search-max-search-results') - search-max-search-results: value -5 is out of range
errors.explain: You set `search-max-search-results` or `search-max-aggregate-results` to a negative number other than -1. Use 0 or a positive number of results, or -1 for the largest limit that Redis Search allows.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<config>') - Invalid default scorer value
errors.example: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument 'search-default-scorer') - Invalid default scorer value
errors.explain: `search-default-scorer` must name a scorer that Redis Search knows, and scorer names are case-sensitive. Use one of `TFIDF`, `TFIDF.DOCNORM`, `BM25`, `BM25STD` (the default), `BM25STD.TANH`, `BM25STD.NORM`, `DISMAX`, `DOCSCORE`, or `HAMMING`.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<config>') - search-_max-trim-delay-ms (<value>) must be greater than search-_min-trim-delay-ms (<limit>)
errors.explain: `search-_max-trim-delay-ms` must be larger than the current `search-_min-trim-delay-ms`, the second number in the message. These internal parameters start with an underscore and are normally left at their defaults. To lower both, lower `search-_min-trim-delay-ms` first.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<config>') - search-_min-trim-delay-ms (<value>) must be less than search-_max-trim-delay-ms (<limit>)
errors.example: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument 'search-_min-trim-delay-ms') - search-_min-trim-delay-ms (99999999) must be less than search-_max-trim-delay-ms (5000)
errors.explain: `search-_min-trim-delay-ms` must be smaller than the current `search-_max-trim-delay-ms`, the second number in the message. These internal parameters start with an underscore and are normally left at their defaults. To raise both, raise `search-_max-trim-delay-ms` first.

errors.message: ERR CONFIG SET failed (possibly related to argument '<config>') - search-disk-max-open-files must be -1 (unlimited) or >= 11
errors.explain: `search-disk-max-open-files`, which applies to Redis Flex, must be -1 for no limit, or 11 or more, because Redis Search keeps about 10 open files for its own use. Set it to -1 or to a value of at least 11.

errors.message: ERR Internal error: no cursors stored
errors.explain: `FT.HYBRID` with `WITHCURSOR`, which is also how shards run it in a cluster, finished without an error but had no cursors to return. This internal consistency check points to a bug in Redis Search. Run the command again.

errors.message: ERR Internal error: no request context
errors.explain: Redis Search ran the query in a background thread but lost track of it before it could send the reply. This is an internal error, not a problem with your command. Run the command again, and if the error repeats, report it to Redis with the command that caused it.

errors.message: ERR Internal error: no results stored
errors.explain: The background thread that ran the query finished without storing either results or an error, so Redis Search has nothing to send back. This is an internal error, not a problem with your command. Run the query again, and if the error repeats, report it to Redis.

errors.message: ERR invalid auto_release_ms
ERR invalid score
errors.explain: The score argument of `FT.SUGADD`, after the suggestion string, isn't a number. Give a number such as `1.0`; suggestions with higher scores rank higher in `FT.SUGGET`.

errors.message: ERR max sync points reached
ERR timeout with no context
errors.explain: `FT.SEARCH` in a cluster timed out, and Redis Search couldn't find the request it was waiting for. This is an internal error. Run the query again, and give it more time with `TIMEOUT` if it keeps timing out.

errors.message: ERR wrong number of arguments for '<command>' command
errors.example: ERR wrong number of arguments for 'FT.SEARCH' command
errors.explain: You called the command named in the message with too few or too many arguments. Compare your call with the syntax on the command's page. A common cause is a missing required argument, such as the query of `FT.SEARCH` or the cursor ID of `FT.CURSOR READ`.

errors.message: ERRBADVAL Failed to deserialize schema
ERRBADVAL Invalid encoding version
ERRBADVAL Max number of indexes reached for Flex indexes: <number>
ERRCLUSTER Uninitialized cluster state, could not perform command
errors.explain: Redis Search doesn't know the shards of the cluster yet, so it can't send the command to them. This happens right after startup or a change to the cluster. Wait until the cluster is ready, and run the command again.

errors.message: Error converting string
errors.explain: An `APPLY` or `FILTER` expression compares a number with text that isn't a number, using `<`, `<=`, `>`, or `>=`, so Redis Search can't order them. Make sure that both sides are numbers. Comparisons with `==` and `!=` don't fail this way.

errors.message: Expected `AUTH` but got `<argument>` at offset <position>
Expected `SHARD` but got `<argument>` at offset <position>
Expected end of command but got `<argument>` at offset <position>
Failed to parse topology using module API at offset <position>
Failed to serialize schema
FT.DROP is not supported in Redis Flex
errors.explain: You only get this when Redis Search runs on Redis Flex, which doesn't support the deprecated `FT.DROP`. Use `FT.DROPINDEX` instead, which drops the index and keeps the documents.

errors.message: FT.PROFILE does not support cursor
errors.explain: `FT.PROFILE` can't profile a query that uses `WITHCURSOR`. Remove `WITHCURSOR` from the query you profile.

errors.message: GC is already running periodically
GC is not available for this index
GIT SHA was not defined on compilation
Hybrid store cursors is not paused
Inconsistent index state cannot be determined: incomplete shard reports; the index list may be incomplete.
Index does not have a timer
Index does not have suffix trie
Index is not a disk index
Index is not temporary
INFO_TAGIDX not supported for disk-mode indexes
Internal error: no AREQ and no preRequestError
errors.explain: In a cluster, the coordinator finished an `FT.AGGREGATE` or `FT.CURSOR READ` without either a request or an error to reply with. This is an internal error, not a problem with your command. Run the command again, and report it to Redis if it repeats.

errors.message: Internal error: no hybrid request and no preRequestError
errors.explain: In a cluster, the coordinator finished an `FT.HYBRID` without either a request or an error to reply with. This is an internal error, not a problem with your command. Run the command again, and report it to Redis if it repeats.

errors.message: Internal error: no request context
errors.explain: Redis Search ran `FT.HYBRID` in a background thread but lost track of it before it could send the reply. This is an internal error, not a problem with your command. Run the command again, and report it to Redis if it repeats.

errors.message: Internal error: no results stored
errors.explain: The background thread that ran the query finished without storing either results or an error, so Redis Search has nothing to send back. This is an internal error, not a problem with your command. Run the query again, and report it to Redis if it repeats.

errors.message: Internal error: timeout with no context
errors.explain: The query reached its timeout, but Redis Search had lost track of the request, so it couldn't send the usual timeout reply. This is an internal error, not a problem with your command. Run the query again, and report it to Redis if it repeats.

errors.message: Invalid argument
Invalid argument for 'ARM_PAUSE'
Invalid argument for 'COORD_THREADS' subcommand
Invalid argument for 'SET_CURSOR_READ_SIZE'
Invalid argument for 'SET_MAX_SCANNED_DOCS'
Invalid argument for 'SET_PAUSE_AFTER_AGGREGATE_RESULT'
Invalid argument for 'SET_PAUSE_AFTER_STORE_RESULTS'
Invalid argument for 'SET_PAUSE_BEFORE_OOM_RETRY'
Invalid argument for 'SET_PAUSE_BEFORE_REDUCE'
Invalid argument for 'SET_PAUSE_BEFORE_SCAN'
Invalid argument for 'SET_PAUSE_BEFORE_STORE_RESULTS'
Invalid argument for 'SET_PAUSE_ON_OOM'
Invalid argument for 'SET_PAUSE_ON_SCANNED_DOCS'
Invalid argument for 'SET_SIMULATE_ASYNC_OOM'
Invalid argument for 'WORKERS' subcommand
Invalid argument. Expected REVEAL or OBFUSCATE as the last argument
Invalid command for 'BG_SCAN_CONTROLLER'
Invalid command for 'DISK_IO_CONTROL'. Use: enable, disable, or status
Invalid command for 'QUERY_CONTROLLER'
Invalid command for 'REPL_COMPACTION_COORDINATOR'
Invalid command for 'VECSIM_MOCK_TIMEOUT'
Invalid payload: <reason>
errors.example: Invalid payload: Expected an argument, but none provided
errors.explain: `PAYLOAD` is the last argument of `FT.SUGADD`, with no value after it. Add the payload string after `PAYLOAD`, or remove `PAYLOAD`.

errors.message: Invalid query
errors.explain: The prefix that you passed to `FT.SUGGET` is longer than 100 characters, the most that it can complete. Use a shorter prefix.

errors.message: Invalid query length
errors.explain: The prefix that you passed to `FT.SUGGET` is longer than 200 bytes. Use a shorter prefix: `FT.SUGGET` completes prefixes of up to 100 characters.

errors.message: Invalid scope for 'SET_PAUSE_AFTER_STORE_RESULTS', expected INTERNAL_ONLY or NON_INTERNAL_ONLY
Invalid scope for 'SET_PAUSE_BEFORE_STORE_RESULTS', expected INTERNAL_ONLY or NON_INTERNAL_ONLY
Invalid sleep time. Must be a non-negative integer.
Invalid UTF-8
errors.explain: A document's value in a `SORTABLE` `TEXT`, `TAG`, or `GEO` field isn't valid Unicode text, so Redis Search can't normalize it for sorting and doesn't index the document. `FT.INFO` reports it. Store valid text, or declare the field `SORTABLE UNF`.

errors.message: Invalid value. Must be at least current number of indexes: <limit>.
Invalid value. Must be between 1 and 200000.
INVOCATION FAILED
Maximum group IDs per term limit reached
errors.explain: A term in `FT.SYNUPDATE` would belong to more than 4,096 synonym groups, the limit per term. Use fewer groups for that term. `FT.SYNUPDATE` can't remove terms from groups, so undoing groups means creating the index again.

errors.message: Maximum synonym terms limit reached
errors.explain: `FT.SYNUPDATE` would take the synonyms of the index over 1,000,000 distinct terms, the limit per index. Add fewer terms. `FT.SYNUPDATE` can't remove terms, so freeing space means creating the index again.

errors.message: Missing value for ADDR at offset <position>
Missing value for AUTH at offset <position>
Missing value for HASHFUNC at offset <position>
Missing value for MYID at offset <position>
Missing value for NUMSLOTS at offset <position>
Missing value for RANGES at offset <position>
Missing value for SHARD at offset <position>
Missing value for SLOTRANGE end at offset <position>
Missing value for SLOTRANGE start at offset <position>
Missing value for UNIXADDR at offset <position>
Module Disabled in Open Source Redis
errors.explain: Redis Search replaced the command with a placeholder that always fails, because it runs on Redis Software with a cluster configuration it doesn't expect. Despite its wording, this is a deployment problem, so contact your administrator or Redis support.

errors.message: Multiple ADDR specified for shard `<shard_id>` at offset <position>
Multiple SLOTRANGE specified for shard `<shard_id>` at offset <position>
Multiple UNIXADDR specified for shard `<shard_id>` at offset <position>
MYID `<shard_id>` does not correspond to any shard at offset <position>
No `SEARCH`, `AGGREGATE`, or `HYBRID` provided
errors.explain: In `FT.PROFILE`, the argument after the index name must be `SEARCH`, `AGGREGATE`, or `HYBRID`, the kind of query to profile. Use `FT.PROFILE index SEARCH [LIMITED] QUERY query`, for example.

errors.message: No debug RP is set
No fields provided
errors.explain: `FT.ALTER ... SCHEMA ADD` has no field after `ADD`. Redis rejects such a short command with a wrong number of arguments error first, so you'll see that instead. Add a field name and type after `ADD`.

errors.message: No longer supported, use FT.SYNUPDATE
errors.explain: `FT.SYNADD` was removed and always returns this error. Use `FT.SYNUPDATE index group term [term ...]` instead, where you choose the name of the synonym group yourself.

errors.message: NOADD
errors.explain: The deprecated `FT.ADD` command didn't change the document, because its `IF` condition was false for the existing document, or used an index field that the document doesn't have. This isn't a failure. Check the `IF` expression if you expected an update.

errors.message: NOPERM User does not have the required permissions to query the index
errors.explain: Your user's access control list (ACL) rules don't allow access to all the keys that the index covers. Give the user access to every `PREFIX` of the index, with a key pattern such as `~doc:*`, or to all keys if it has no `PREFIX`.

errors.message: Operation failed: coordinator thread pool doesn't exists or is already running
Operation failed: coordinator thread pool doesn't exists or is not running
Operation failed: workers thread pool doesn't exists or is already running
Operation failed: workers thread pool doesn't exists or is not running
Operation failed: workers thread pool is not running
Out of memory
Payload too large
errors.explain: The payload of `FT.SUGADD` is too large to store, at about 4 gigabytes or more. Store a much smaller payload, such as the name of a key that holds the data.

errors.message: Query is not paused
REPL_COMPACTION_COORDINATOR is only supported in disk mode
Scanner is not initialized
Scorer already registered or registration failed
SEARCH_ADD_ARGS Could not parse document score
errors.explain: The score of the deprecated `FT.ADD` command, the argument right after the key, isn't a number. Give a number from 0 to 1, such as `1.0`, or write the document with `HSET` instead.

errors.message: SEARCH_ADD_ARGS Duplicate parameter `<parameter>`
errors.explain: `PARAMS` defines the parameter in the message more than once. Give each parameter a single value, and remove the repeated name and value from `PARAMS`.

errors.message: SEARCH_ADD_ARGS Error parsing document indexing arguments
errors.explain: This is the default message of `SEARCH_ADD_ARGS`: Redis Search couldn't parse the options of the deprecated `FT.ADD` command. In Redis 8.10 `FT.ADD` always returns a more specific message, so check the arguments after the score against its syntax.

errors.message: SEARCH_ADD_ARGS Fields must be specified in FIELD VALUE pairs
errors.explain: After `FIELDS`, the deprecated `FT.ADD` command expects field names and values in pairs, but it got an odd number of arguments. Check for a missing value or an extra argument at the end.

errors.message: SEARCH_ADD_ARGS Invalid argument for `INDEXALL`, use ENABLE/DISABLE
errors.explain: The value after `INDEXALL` in `FT.CREATE` isn't valid. Use `INDEXALL ENABLE` or `INDEXALL DISABLE`; case doesn't matter.

errors.message: SEARCH_ADD_ARGS Invalid expression
errors.explain: The `FILTER` expression of `FT.CREATE` couldn't be parsed. Redis 8.10 sends a more specific `SEARCH_EXPR` error instead of this text, such as a syntax error with its offset. Check the expression's syntax, and that field names start with `@`.

errors.message: SEARCH_ADD_ARGS Invalid language
errors.explain: The `LANGUAGE` value of `FT.CREATE` isn't a language that Redis Search supports. Use the full English name of a supported language, such as `english`, `german`, or `chinese`; case doesn't matter. The `FT.CREATE` page lists them.

errors.message: SEARCH_ADD_ARGS Invalid rule type: <type>
errors.example: SEARCH_ADD_ARGS Invalid rule type: FOO
errors.explain: The value after `ON` in `FT.CREATE`, shown in the message, isn't a type of key that Redis Search can index. Use `ON HASH` or `ON JSON`. `ON JSON` works only when the module that provides `JSON.SET` is loaded.

errors.message: SEARCH_ADD_ARGS Invalid score
errors.explain: The `SCORE` value of `FT.CREATE` isn't a number from 0 to 1. It sets the default score of documents that don't have their own, so use a value such as `SCORE 1` or `SCORE 0.5`.

errors.message: SEARCH_ADD_ARGS Multiple PARAMS are not allowed. Parameters can be defined only once
errors.explain: The command has more than one `PARAMS` argument. Put all parameters in a single `PARAMS`, followed by the count of the names and values, such as `PARAMS 4 min 10 max 20`.

errors.message: SEARCH_ADD_ARGS No field list found
errors.explain: The deprecated `FT.ADD` command has no `FIELDS` keyword, so it has no fields to store. Add `FIELDS` followed by field and value pairs after the options.

errors.message: SEARCH_ADD_ARGS Parameters must be specified in PARAM VALUE pairs
errors.explain: The count after `PARAMS` is 0 or odd, but parameters come in name and value pairs. Set the count to the number of names plus values that follow, such as `PARAMS 2 radius 10`.

errors.message: SEARCH_ADD_ARGS Parsing error for document option <option>: <reason>
errors.explain: An option of the deprecated `FT.ADD` command, such as `LANGUAGE`, `PAYLOAD`, or `IF`, has no value after it. The message names the option. Add its value, or remove the option.

errors.message: SEARCH_ADD_ARGS Score must be between 0 and 1
errors.explain: The score of the deprecated `FT.ADD` command, the argument right after the key, is less than 0 or greater than 1. Give a score from 0 to 1, such as `1.0`.

errors.message: SEARCH_ADD_ARGS Unknown keyword `<argument>` provided
errors.example: SEARCH_ADD_ARGS Unknown keyword `FOO` provided
errors.explain: The deprecated `FT.ADD` command got an option it doesn't know, shown in the message. The options are `REPLACE`, `PARTIAL`, `NOCREATE`, `PAYLOAD`, `LANGUAGE`, and `IF`, and they must come before `FIELDS`, so check the spelling and the order.

errors.message: SEARCH_ADD_ARGS Unsupported language
errors.explain: The `LANGUAGE` option of the deprecated `FT.ADD` command names a language that Redis Search doesn't support for stemming. Use one of the languages that `FT.CREATE` accepts for `LANGUAGE`, such as `english`, `french`, or `chinese`.

errors.message: SEARCH_ADHOC_BATCH_SIZE_IRRELEVANT 'batch size' is irrelevant for the selected policy
errors.explain: Your filtered vector query sets `BATCH_SIZE` together with `HYBRID_POLICY ADHOC_BF`, which doesn't use batches. Remove `BATCH_SIZE`, or use `HYBRID_POLICY BATCHES`. Redis 8.10 sends this text with `(Error parsing vector similarity parameters)` added.
