errors.message: SEARCH_ADHOC_BATCH_SIZE_IRRELEVANT 'batch size' is irrelevant for the selected policy (Error parsing vector similarity parameters)
errors.explain: Your filtered vector query sets `BATCH_SIZE` together with `HYBRID_POLICY ADHOC_BF`, which compares vectors one by one and doesn't use batches. Remove `BATCH_SIZE`, or use `HYBRID_POLICY BATCHES`.

errors.message: SEARCH_ADHOC_EF_RUNTIME_IRRELEVANT 'EF_RUNTIME' is irrelevant for the selected policy
errors.explain: Your filtered vector query sets `EF_RUNTIME` together with `HYBRID_POLICY ADHOC_BF`, which compares vectors one by one and doesn't search the graph. Remove `EF_RUNTIME`, or use `HYBRID_POLICY BATCHES`. Redis 8.10 sends this text with `(Error parsing vector similarity parameters)` added.

errors.message: SEARCH_ADHOC_EF_RUNTIME_IRRELEVANT 'EF_RUNTIME' is irrelevant for the selected policy (Error parsing vector similarity parameters)
errors.explain: Your filtered vector query sets `EF_RUNTIME` together with `HYBRID_POLICY ADHOC_BF`, which compares vectors one by one and doesn't search the graph. Remove `EF_RUNTIME`, or use `HYBRID_POLICY BATCHES`.

errors.message: SEARCH_AGG_PLAN Could not plan aggregation request
SEARCH_ALIAS_CONFLICT Alias conflicts with an existing index name
errors.explain: `FT.ALIASADD` or `FT.ALIASUPDATE` can't create the alias, because an index already has that name. Aliases and index names share one namespace, so choose an alias name that no index uses.

errors.message: SEARCH_ARG_UNRECOGNIZED Unknown argument
errors.explain: The command has an extra argument that it doesn't accept. `FT.DROPINDEX` accepts only `DD`, the deprecated `FT.DROP` accepts only `KEEPDOCS`, and `FT._LIST` accepts only `WITHCLUSTERSTATE`. Remove or correct the last argument.

errors.message: SEARCH_ARG_UNRECOGNIZED Unknown argument `<argument>`
errors.example: SEARCH_ARG_UNRECOGNIZED Unknown argument `FOO`
errors.explain: `FT.CREATE` found an unknown argument, shown in the message, before `SCHEMA`. Check its spelling and the count of the option before it, such as `PREFIX 2`, because an extra value is read as a new argument. In a cluster, `FT.CURSOR READ` also returns this when the word after the cursor ID isn't `COUNT`.

errors.message: SEARCH_ARG_UNRECOGNIZED Unknown argument `<argument>` at position <position> for <main>
errors.explain: `FT.SEARCH` or `FT.AGGREGATE` found an argument that it doesn't recognize, shown in the message. The position counts from 0 at the query, so position 1 often means a query with spaces that isn't quoted. Otherwise, check the spelling, and check the count of the option before it, such as `RETURN 2`.

errors.message: SEARCH_ARG_UNRECOGNIZED Unknown argument `<argument>` at position <position> for <reducer>
errors.example: SEARCH_ARG_UNRECOGNIZED Unknown argument `FOOBAR` at position 1 for <main>
errors.explain: The reducer named at the end of the message, such as `QUANTILE`, got more arguments than it uses. The message shows the first extra one, counting that reducer's arguments from 0. Lower the argument count after the reducer name, or remove the extra argument, as in `REDUCE QUANTILE 2 @price 0.5`.

errors.message: SEARCH_ARG_UNRECOGNIZED Unknown argument `<argument>` in KNN
errors.explain: The `KNN` arguments of the `VSIM` clause in `FT.HYBRID` include a name it doesn't know, shown in the message. Inside its count, `KNN` accepts only `K`, `EF_RUNTIME`, and `SHARD_K_RATIO`, so `YIELD_SCORE_AS` must come after the counted arguments.

errors.message: SEARCH_ARG_UNRECOGNIZED Unknown argument `<argument>` in RANGE
errors.explain: The `RANGE` arguments of the `VSIM` clause in `FT.HYBRID` include a name it doesn't know, shown in the message. Inside its count, `RANGE` accepts only `RADIUS` and `EPSILON`, so `YIELD_SCORE_AS` must come after the counted arguments.

errors.message: SEARCH_ARG_UNRECOGNIZED Unknown argument `<argument>` in SEARCH
errors.explain: The `SEARCH` clause of `FT.HYBRID` has an argument after the query that it doesn't know, shown in the message. After the query, it accepts only `SCORER` and `YIELD_SCORE_AS`, then `VSIM`. Put a query that contains spaces in quotes.

errors.message: SEARCH_ATTR_BAD Attribute not supported for term
errors.explain: This is the default text of `SEARCH_ATTR_BAD`, which means that an argument names a field or gives a value that the operation doesn't accept. Redis 8.10 sends a specific message instead, such as `No such field` or `Not a tag field` from `FT.TAGVALS`.

errors.message: SEARCH_ATTR_BAD Count accepts 0 values only
errors.explain: The `COUNT` reducer doesn't take arguments, but its argument count isn't 0. Write `REDUCE COUNT 0`, optionally followed by `AS` and a name. To count the distinct values of a property, use `COUNT_DISTINCT` instead.

errors.message: SEARCH_ATTR_BAD No such field
errors.explain: `FT.TAGVALS` can't find the field you named in the index. Field names are case-sensitive, so check the name against `FT.INFO`. For a JSON index, use the field's `AS` name, not its JSONPath.

errors.message: SEARCH_ATTR_BAD Not a tag field
errors.explain: `FT.TAGVALS` only works on `TAG` fields, and the field you named has another type. Check the field types with `FT.INFO`.

errors.message: SEARCH_BUILD_PLAN Could not build plan from query
SEARCH_CLUSTER_NO_RESPONSES no responses received
errors.explain: You only get this error in a cluster. `FT.INFO` or `FT._LIST` sent the request to the shards, but no shard replied. Check that the shards are running and reachable, and then run the command again.

errors.message: SEARCH_CONSTRUCT_PIPELINE Could not construct query pipeline
SEARCH_CURSOR_ALLOC_FAILED Could not allocate a cursor
SEARCH_DISK_CREATION Could not create disk index
errors.explain: This is the default text of `SEARCH_DISK_CREATION`, which means that Redis Flex couldn't create or open the disk storage of an index. Redis 8.10 doesn't send this text; `FT.CREATE` sends `Could not open disk index` instead.

errors.message: SEARCH_DISK_CREATION Could not open disk index
errors.explain: Redis Flex couldn't open the disk storage of the index that you're creating, so `FT.CREATE` failed. This is an internal storage failure. Check the server log and the disk, and then retry.

errors.message: SEARCH_DISK_ITERATOR_CREATION <error>
errors.explain: Redis Flex couldn't start reading the disk part of an index for a numeric filter in your query, so the query stopped. The text after the code gives the reason. This is an internal failure; retry the query, and check the server log if it keeps happening.

errors.message: SEARCH_DISK_ITERATOR_CREATION Could not create disk iterator
errors.explain: This is the default text of `SEARCH_DISK_ITERATOR_CREATION`, which means that Redis Flex couldn't start reading an index on disk for a query. Redis 8.10 sends the specific reason instead of this text. Retry the query.

errors.message: SEARCH_DIST_FAILED Could not distribute the operation
SEARCH_DOC_NOT_FOUND
errors.explain: `FT.ADD` with `REPLACE` and `IF` found the key in Redis, but the index doesn't have a document for it, so it can't check the `IF` condition. The message has no description. Check that the key matches the prefixes of the index, or add the document without `IF`.

errors.message: SEARCH_DOC_NOT_FOUND Document does not exist
errors.explain: You called the deprecated `FT.ADD` command with `NOCREATE`, but no key with that name exists. `NOCREATE` only updates existing documents, so remove it to create the document, or check the key name.

errors.message: SEARCH_DOC_NOT_FOUND Document not found
errors.explain: Redis Search couldn't open a document's key while reading its fields, usually because the key was deleted or expired during the operation. Queries skip such documents instead of failing, so you rarely see this. Retry the command.

errors.message: SEARCH_DOCUMENT_EXISTS Document already exists
errors.explain: The deprecated `FT.ADD` command found an existing hash with that key, and you didn't give `REPLACE`. Add `REPLACE` to overwrite the document, use another key, or write the document with `HSET` instead.

errors.message: SEARCH_DOCUMENT_NOT_ADDED Document was not added because condition was unmet
errors.explain: `FT.ADD` didn't update the document because its `IF` condition wasn't true. You don't normally see this text, because `FT.ADD` replies with `NOADD` in this case. Check the `IF` expression if you expected an update.

errors.message: SEARCH_EXPR Function '<function>' expects <number> arguments, but got <number>
errors.example: SEARCH_EXPR Function 'substr' expects 3 arguments, but got 1
errors.explain: The function in the message got the wrong number of arguments, and the message says how many it needs. For example, `substr()` takes three arguments: the string, the offset, and the length.

errors.message: SEARCH_EXPR Function '<function>' expects between <number> and <number> arguments, but got <number>
errors.explain: The function in the message got more or fewer arguments than it accepts, and the message gives the allowed range. For example, `split()` takes from 1 to 3 arguments: the string, then optionally the separators and the characters to trim.

errors.message: SEARCH_EXPR Missing (or badly formatted) value for expr->func.args->args[ii]
errors.explain: An argument of a function in your `APPLY` or `FILTER` expression couldn't be parsed; `expr->func.args` in the message means the arguments of a function call. This usually comes from an unknown function or a bare word inside the call. Check each argument for typos, and put quotes around strings and `@` before properties.

errors.message: SEARCH_EXPR Missing (or badly formatted) value for expr->inverted.child
errors.explain: The expression after `!` in your `APPLY` or `FILTER` expression couldn't be parsed; `expr->inverted.child` in the message means what follows `!`. This usually comes from an unknown function or a bare word there. Check it for typos, and put quotes around strings and `@` before properties.

errors.message: SEARCH_EXPR Missing (or badly formatted) value for expr->op.left
errors.explain: The left side of an arithmetic operator, such as `+` or `*`, in your `APPLY` or `FILTER` expression couldn't be parsed; `expr->op.left` in the message means that left side. This usually comes from an unknown function or a bare word there. Check it for typos, and put quotes around strings and `@` before properties.

errors.message: SEARCH_EXPR Missing (or badly formatted) value for expr->op.right
errors.explain: The right side of an arithmetic operator, such as `+`, in your `APPLY` or `FILTER` expression couldn't be parsed; `expr->op.right` in the message means that side. It's usually an unknown function or a bare word, as in `1 + foo(1)`. Check it for typos, quote strings, and put `@` before properties.

errors.message: SEARCH_EXPR Missing (or badly formatted) value for expr->pred.left
errors.explain: The left side of a comparison, such as `==` or `>`, in your `APPLY` or `FILTER` expression couldn't be parsed; `expr->pred.left` in the message means that left side. This usually comes from an unknown function or a bare word there. Check it for typos, and put quotes around strings and `@` before properties.

errors.message: SEARCH_EXPR Missing (or badly formatted) value for expr->pred.right
errors.explain: The right side of a comparison, such as `==` or `>`, in your `APPLY` or `FILTER` expression couldn't be parsed; `expr->pred.right` in the message means that right side. It's usually a bare word, as in `@color == red`. Put quotes around strings, as in `@color == "red"`, and `@` before properties.

errors.message: SEARCH_EXPR Parsing/Evaluating dynamic expression failed
errors.explain: Redis Search couldn't parse or evaluate an expression in `APPLY`, `FILTER`, or the `FILTER` option of `FT.CREATE`, and has no more specific reason. Check the expression's syntax, its function names, and its field names, which need the `@` prefix.

errors.message: SEARCH_EXPR Syntax error at offset <position> near '<token>'
errors.example: SEARCH_EXPR Syntax error at offset 2 near '1'
errors.explain: Redis Search couldn't parse the `APPLY` or `FILTER` expression, or the `FILTER` of `FT.CREATE`, near the offset in the message, counting from 0. Look there for a missing operator, operand, or parenthesis, such as `@price >` with nothing after it, and check that the whole expression is one quoted argument.

errors.message: SEARCH_EXPR Syntax error at offset <position> near '<token>': <reason>
errors.explain: The expression has a syntax error, and the reason after the colon is an earlier problem that probably caused it, such as an unknown function or the wrong number of arguments. Fix the problem in the reason first, and then check the expression near the offset in the message.

errors.message: SEARCH_EXPR Unknown function name '<function>'
errors.example: SEARCH_EXPR Unknown function name 'foo'
errors.explain: The expression calls a function that Redis Search doesn't have, named in the message. Check the spelling against the functions that `APPLY` supports, such as `upper()`, `substr()`, `timefmt()`, and `exists()`.

errors.message: SEARCH_EXPR Unknown symbol '<symbol>'
errors.example: SEARCH_EXPR Unknown symbol 'nosym'
errors.explain: The expression has a bare word, shown in the message, that isn't a function call, a property, or a string; the only bare word allowed is `NULL`. Put `@` in front of a property name, or quotes around a string, such as `@color == "red"`.

errors.message: SEARCH_FIELD_DUP Could not create score alias, name already exists in query, score alias: <alias>
errors.explain: The `YIELD_SCORE_AS` name of `COMBINE` in `FT.HYBRID` is already used in the query, for example by the `YIELD_SCORE_AS` of the `SEARCH` or `VSIM` clause, or by a field in `LOAD`. Choose a name that nothing else in the query uses.

errors.message: SEARCH_FIELD_DUP Could not create score alias, name already exists in query<alias>
errors.explain: The `YIELD_SCORE_AS` name of the `SEARCH` clause in `FT.HYBRID` is already used in that subquery, so Redis Search can't add the score under that name. The name follows the message text without a space. Choose a different name.

errors.message: SEARCH_FIELD_DUP Distance field was specified twice for vector query: <alias> and <alias>
errors.example: SEARCH_FIELD_DUP Distance field was specified twice for vector query: d and e
errors.explain: A vector query names its distance field twice, with `AS` inside the brackets and with `$yield_distance_as` after them, as in `*=>[KNN 10 @v $vec AS d]=>{$yield_distance_as: e}`. Keep only one of them.

errors.message: SEARCH_FIELD_DUP Field was specified twice
errors.explain: This is the default text of `SEARCH_FIELD_DUP`, which means that the same field or alias appears twice where it must be unique. Redis 8.10 sends a specific message instead, for example one saying that a property is specified more than once. Remove or rename the duplicate.

errors.message: SEARCH_FIELD_DUP Property `<property>` specified more than once
errors.explain: Two properties in the command have the same name, shown in the message. This happens when `GROUPBY` lists a property twice, a `REDUCE ... AS` name repeats or matches a `GROUPBY` property, or two vector distance fields share a name. Use different names.

errors.message: SEARCH_FIELD_DUP Tried to insert field twice: '<field>'
errors.explain: A document has two values for the same field of the index, named in the message, so Redis Search didn't index the document. Make sure that each field appears only once in the document. You can get this from `FT.ADD`, or see it in `FT.INFO` as the last indexing error.

errors.message: SEARCH_FIELD_MISSING_REQ 'ismissing' requires field to be defined with 'INDEXMISSING'
SEARCH_FLEX_LIMIT_NUMBER_OF_INDEXES Flex index limit was reached
errors.explain: This is the default text of the code that Redis Flex sends when you already have the most indexes it allows, which is 10. Redis 8.10 sends `Max number of indexes reached for Flex indexes` with the count instead. Drop an index that you no longer need.

errors.message: SEARCH_FLEX_LIMIT_NUMBER_OF_INDEXES Max number of indexes reached for Flex indexes: <number>
errors.explain: You only get this when Redis Search runs on Redis Flex. `FT.CREATE` can't add an index, because the database already has as many indexes as Redis Flex allows. Drop an index that you no longer need with `FT.DROPINDEX`.

errors.message: SEARCH_FLEX_SEARCH_LOAD_UNSUPPORTED LOAD is not supported in Redis Flex
SEARCH_FLEX_SEARCH_NOCONTENT_OR_RETURN_0_REQUIRED NOCONTENT or RETURN 0 must be provided in Redis Flex
SEARCH_FLEX_UNSUPPORTED_ARGUMENT <argument> is not supported in Redis Flex
errors.explain: Your command uses an option that Redis Flex doesn't support, named in the message: `WITHSUFFIXTRIE` in a schema, or `WITHCURSOR`, `SUMMARIZE`, `HIGHLIGHT`, `WITHOUTCOUNT`, `SLOP`, `INORDER`, or `DIALECT 4` in a query. Remove that option.

errors.message: SEARCH_FLEX_UNSUPPORTED_ARGUMENT FT.AGGREGATE in a context that cannot block (MULTI/EXEC or Lua scripts) is not supported in Redis Flex
errors.explain: You ran `FT.AGGREGATE` on a Redis Flex index inside a `MULTI`/`EXEC` transaction or a Lua script. There, Redis can't block the client while it reads documents from disk, so Redis Flex rejects every `FT.AGGREGATE`. Run the aggregation as a separate command, outside the transaction or script.

errors.message: SEARCH_FLEX_UNSUPPORTED_ARGUMENT FT.SEARCH with field return in a context that cannot block (MULTI/EXEC or Lua scripts) is not supported in Redis Flex; use NOCONTENT or RETURN 0
errors.explain: You ran `FT.SEARCH` on a Redis Flex index inside a `MULTI`/`EXEC` transaction or a Lua script, and the query returns document fields. Loading them from disk would block the client, which isn't possible there. Add `NOCONTENT` or `RETURN 0` and remove any `LOAD`, or run the query outside the transaction or script.

errors.message: SEARCH_FLEX_UNSUPPORTED_ARGUMENT SORTBY in Redis Flex is restricted to sorting results by vector distance in vector queries. Otherwise, results are always sorted by the default document score.
errors.explain: On a Redis Flex index, `SORTBY` can only sort by the distance field of a vector (`KNN`) query. Remove `SORTBY` to get results sorted by score, or sort by the distance field, which is `__<vector_field>_score` unless you named it with `AS`.

errors.message: SEARCH_FLEX_UNSUPPORTED_ARGUMENT Unsupported argument for Redis Flex
errors.explain: This is the default text of the code that Redis Flex sends when a command uses an option that it doesn't support. Redis 8.10 names the option instead, as in `HIGHLIGHT is not supported in Redis Flex`. Remove that option.

errors.message: SEARCH_FLEX_UNSUPPORTED_FIELD <field_type> fields are not supported in Flex indexes
errors.explain: Your schema has a field type that Redis Flex can't index, named in the message. Flex indexes don't support `GEO` or `GEOSHAPE` fields. Use only `TEXT`, `TAG`, `NUMERIC`, and `VECTOR` fields.

errors.message: SEARCH_FLEX_UNSUPPORTED_FIELD Unsupported field for Flex index
errors.explain: This is the default text of the code that Redis Flex sends for a field type that it can't index. Redis 8.10 names the type instead, as in `GEO fields are not supported in Flex indexes`. Remove `GEO` and `GEOSHAPE` fields from the schema.

errors.message: SEARCH_FLEX_UNSUPPORTED_FT_CREATE_ARGUMENT Unsupported argument for Flex index: `<argument>`
errors.explain: Your `FT.CREATE` uses an option that Redis Flex indexes don't support, named in the message, such as `NOOFFSETS`, `NOFIELDS`, `NOFREQS`, `NOHL`, `MAXTEXTFIELDS`, `TEMPORARY`, `PAYLOAD_FIELD`, or `INDEXALL`. Remove that option.

errors.message: SEARCH_FLEX_UNSUPPORTED_FT_CREATE_ARGUMENT Unsupported FT.CREATE argument for Flex index
errors.explain: This is the default text of the code that Redis Flex sends for an `FT.CREATE` option that it doesn't support. Redis 8.10 names the option instead, such as `NOOFFSETS` or `TEMPORARY`. Remove that option from `FT.CREATE`.

errors.message: SEARCH_FLEX_UNSUPPORTED_QUERY <query_type> queries are not supported on Flex indexes
errors.explain: You only get this from an index that uses Redis Flex, which doesn't support the kind of `TAG` match named in the message: a prefix, suffix, or infix match such as `{abc*}`, a wildcard match, or a lexical range. Match exact `TAG` values instead.

errors.message: SEARCH_FLEX_UNSUPPORTED_QUERY Unsupported query type for Flex indexes
errors.explain: This is the default text of the code that Redis Flex sends for a kind of query that it can't run. Redis 8.10 names the kind instead, such as tag prefix, suffix, or wildcard queries. Rewrite the query without that syntax.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC <processor> RP type not found in stream or tried to insert after last RP
errors.explain: This message comes from `PAUSE_BEFORE_RP_N` or `PAUSE_AFTER_RP_N`, options of the internal `_FT.DEBUG` testing command. The pipeline step named in the message isn't in the query's pipeline, or it's the last step. Normal queries never send this.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC cannot operate on a JSON index as RedisJSON is not loaded
errors.explain: The index was created `ON JSON`, but the JSON module isn't loaded, so Redis Search can't read the documents. This usually means Redis runs without its bundled JSON module. Load the module, for example with `loadmodule` in the configuration file, and restart Redis.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Contains query on fields without WITHSUFFIXTRIE support
errors.explain: The query uses a suffix, contains, or wildcard match, such as `*ell*` or `w'*ell*'`, on a `TEXT` field without `WITHSUFFIXTRIE`, while another field of the index has it. Query only fields with `WITHSUFFIXTRIE`, or create the index again with it on this field.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Could not open geoshape index for indexing
errors.explain: Redis Search couldn't open the internal index of a `GEOSHAPE` field to add a document, so it didn't index the document. This is an internal error, not a problem with the document, and `FT.INFO` shows it as the last indexing error. Report it to Redis if it repeats.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Could not open numeric index for indexing
errors.explain: Redis Search couldn't open the internal index of a `NUMERIC` or `GEO` field to add a document, so it didn't index the document. This is an internal error, not a problem with the document, and `FT.INFO` shows it as the last indexing error. Report it to Redis if it repeats.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Could not open tag index for indexing
errors.explain: Redis Search couldn't open the internal index of a `TAG` field while it indexed a document. In Redis 8.10 this can't normally happen, so it points to a bug or a server problem rather than to your data.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Could not open vector for indexing
errors.explain: Redis Search couldn't create the vector index of a `VECTOR` field when it indexed the first vector into it. This points to a problem on the server, such as a failed memory allocation or, with Redis Flex, a disk storage problem, rather than to your data.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Could not parse numeric index value
errors.explain: A new value for a `NUMERIC` `SORTABLE` field wasn't a number when Redis Search updated the document's sort values. This belongs to the partial update path of the deprecated `FT.ADD ... REPLACE PARTIAL`, which Redis 8.10 no longer runs, so you shouldn't see it.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC could not parse redisearch results
errors.explain: You only get this in a cluster. A shard replied to `FT.SEARCH` with something the coordinator couldn't read, and no shard error explains it. This can happen when shards run different versions of Redis Search, so check the versions and run the query again.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Could not send query to cluster
errors.explain: You only get this in a cluster. The coordinator got no replies from the shards for `FT.SEARCH`, so it couldn't run the query. Check that the shards are running and reachable, and run the query again.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Couldn't load document metadata
errors.explain: Redis Search found the document in the index but couldn't read its stored metadata during a partial update. This belongs to the partial update path of the deprecated `FT.ADD ... REPLACE PARTIAL`, which Redis 8.10 no longer runs, so you shouldn't see it.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Couldn't load old document
errors.explain: During a partial update, Redis Search couldn't find the existing document in the index. This belongs to the partial update path of the deprecated `FT.ADD ... REPLACE PARTIAL`, which Redis 8.10 no longer runs, so you shouldn't see it.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Cursor not found, id: <cursor_id>
errors.explain: In a cluster, `FT.CURSOR READ` found no idle cursor with the ID in the message. A cursor is removed when you read its last results, when you delete it with `FT.CURSOR DEL`, or when it's idle longer than its `MAXIDLE` time. Run `FT.AGGREGATE` with `WITHCURSOR` again to get a new cursor.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Document indexing failed; disk write batch aborted
errors.explain: You only get this from an index that uses Redis Flex. Redis Search couldn't index a field of the document, so it discarded the disk writes for the whole document. The field statistics of `FT.INFO` show the error of the field that failed.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Expected <processor> processor at end of pipeline, found <processor>
errors.explain: `FT.PROFILE` with `HYBRID` found an unexpected internal processing step at the end of a subquery. This is an internal consistency check, so it points to a bug in Redis Search rather than to your command.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Expected first reply as integer. Have <reply_type>
errors.explain: You only get this error in a cluster. A shard answered its part of `FT.SPELLCHECK` in a format that the coordinator doesn't expect; the number in the message is the type of reply that it got. This can happen when shards run different versions of Redis Search. Run the command again, and report it if it continues.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Expected total_docs as integer. Have <reply_type>
errors.explain: You only get this error in a cluster. A shard answered its part of `FT.SPELLCHECK` without the document count that the coordinator expects; the number in the message is the type of reply that it got. This can happen when shards run different versions of Redis Search. Run the command again, and report it if it continues.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Failed to allocate memory for multi-vector field
errors.explain: Redis Search couldn't compute the memory needed for all the vectors of a multi-value `VECTOR` field in a JSON document, because the size overflowed. This can't happen with realistic data, so you shouldn't see this message.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Failed to allocate memory for text field
errors.explain: Redis Search couldn't compute the memory needed for all the values of a `TEXT` or `TAG` field in a JSON document, because the size overflowed. This can't happen with realistic data, so you shouldn't see this message.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Failed to allocate memory for vector
errors.explain: Redis Search couldn't allocate memory for a vector from a JSON document. This only happens if a memory allocation fails, which normally stops Redis instead, so you shouldn't see this message.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Failed to build hybrid pipeline
errors.explain: `FT.HYBRID` couldn't set up the steps that run its subqueries, and no more specific error was recorded. This usually points to an internal problem. Check the command against the `FT.HYBRID` syntax, and run it again.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Failed to commit disk write batch
errors.explain: You only get this from an index that uses Redis Flex. Redis Search couldn't save the document's index entries to disk storage, which points to a problem on the server rather than in your data.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Failed to communicate with shards
errors.explain: You only get this error in a cluster. `FT.HYBRID` couldn't start sending its query to the shards. Check that all shards are running and reachable, and then run the command again.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Failed to create disk snapshot for index '<index>'
errors.explain: Redis Flex couldn't take the point-in-time snapshot of the index's data on disk that the query needs, so the query stopped. This is an internal failure of disk-backed indexes. Retry the query, and check the server log if it keeps happening.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Failed to create pause RP or another debug RP is already set
errors.explain: This message comes from `PAUSE_BEFORE_RP_N` or `PAUSE_AFTER_RP_N`, options of the internal `_FT.DEBUG` testing command: another debug pause is already set. Let the paused query finish before you set another pause. Normal queries never send this.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Failed to deplete set of results, rc=<code>
errors.explain: `FT.HYBRID` with `WITHCURSOR`, which is also how shards run it in a cluster, couldn't collect the results of its subqueries. The number is an internal result code. This points to an internal error rather than to your command, so run it again.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Failed to get value from iterator
errors.explain: Redis Search couldn't build the sort value of a `SORTABLE` field whose JSONPath returns several values, so it didn't index the document. This usually points to an internal problem rather than to your data.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Failed to merge hybrid subquery results
errors.explain: `FT.HYBRID` couldn't combine the results of its text search and its vector search into one result. In Redis Search 8.10 this step can't fail, so you shouldn't see this message. If you do, retry the command.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Failed to process shard responses, first error: <error>, total error count: <number>
errors.explain: You only get this error in a cluster. One or more shards returned an error for their part of `FT.HYBRID`, and the message shows the first error and how many there were. Fix the problem that the first error describes, or, if it's a connection problem, check that the shards are reachable.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Generic error evaluating the query
errors.explain: Redis Search hit an error that has no more specific message. In a cluster, it can mean that the coordinator couldn't start sending the query to the shards. Run the command again, and if it keeps failing, check that all shards are running and reachable.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Generic error evaluating the query (Error parsing vector similarity parameters)
errors.explain: Redis Search couldn't apply the options of your vector query, inside `=>[KNN ...]` or `VECTOR_RANGE`, and has no specific reason. Check each option's name and value, and remove options that the field's algorithm doesn't use.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC GEOMETRY field does not support array type
errors.explain: A JSON array can't be indexed as a `GEOSHAPE` field. Redis 8.10 returns `Invalid JSON type: Array type cannot represent GEOMETRY field` for this instead, so you shouldn't see this message. Store one shape as a well-known text (WKT) string.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Invalid UTF8
errors.explain: A new value for a `SORTABLE` field wasn't valid Unicode text, so Redis Search couldn't normalize it for sorting. This belongs to the partial update path of the deprecated `FT.ADD ... REPLACE PARTIAL`, which Redis 8.10 no longer runs, so you shouldn't see it.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Invalid vector element at index <position>
errors.explain: An element of the JSON array of a `VECTOR` field isn't a valid number for the field's `TYPE`. The message gives its position, counting from 0. Elements must be numbers, and for `INT8` and `UINT8` they must be whole numbers.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Invalid vector elements type - expected <vector_type>, got <json_type>
errors.explain: The JSON array of an `INT8` or `UINT8` `VECTOR` field holds decimal numbers, such as `[0.5, 1.5]`, but these types need whole numbers. The number after `got` is an internal type code. Store whole numbers, or use a float `TYPE` such as `FLOAT32`.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Invalid vector similarity algorithm
errors.explain: A `VECTOR` field uses an algorithm that Redis Search doesn't know when it reads a vector from a JSON document. Every algorithm that `FT.CREATE` accepts is handled, so this points to a bug rather than to your data.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC No subqueries in hybrid request
errors.explain: `FT.HYBRID` tried to start cursors for a request that has no subqueries. Every `FT.HYBRID` request has exactly two subqueries, so this can't happen in Redis 8.10 and points to a bug in Redis Search.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC NOPERM User does not have the required permissions to query the index
errors.explain: You only get this on Redis Software and Redis Cloud. Your user's access control list (ACL) rules don't allow access to every key prefix of the index, so `FT.ALIASADD` or `FT.ALIASUPDATE` can't point an alias at it. Give the user access to those prefixes.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Numeric indexing failed
errors.explain: You only get this from an index that uses Redis Flex. Redis Search couldn't write a `NUMERIC` value of the document to disk storage, which points to a problem on the server rather than in your data.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Object type is not supported
errors.explain: A `GEOSHAPE` field in a JSON document holds a JSON object, such as GeoJSON. Redis Search 8.10 can't index objects in any field, so store the shape as a well-known text (WKT) string, such as `POINT (2 1)`.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Requested to index field twice
errors.explain: During a partial update, the same `SORTABLE` field appeared twice in the field list. This belongs to the partial update path of the deprecated `FT.ADD ... REPLACE PARTIAL`, which Redis 8.10 no longer runs, so you shouldn't see it.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Tag indexing failed
errors.explain: You only get this from an index that uses Redis Flex. Redis Search couldn't write the `TAG` values of the document to disk storage, which points to a problem on the server rather than in your data.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Unexpected depleter type: expected <processor>, got <processor>
errors.explain: `FT.HYBRID` found an unexpected internal processing step at the end of a subquery when it set up cursors. This is an internal consistency check, so it points to a bug in Redis Search rather than to your command.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Unsupported field type
errors.explain: The JSONPath of a `GEOSHAPE` field returns more than one value, for example because it has a wildcard such as `$.shapes[*]`. Redis Search can't index several shapes in one field, so use a JSONPath that returns a single well-known text (WKT) string.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC Unsupported sortable type
errors.explain: During a partial update, a `SORTABLE` field had a type that the update couldn't store as a sort value. This belongs to the partial update path of the deprecated `FT.ADD ... REPLACE PARTIAL`, which Redis 8.10 no longer runs, so you shouldn't see it.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC wrong reply type. Expected array. Got <reply_type>
errors.explain: You only get this error in a cluster. A shard answered its part of `FT.SPELLCHECK` with something other than the array that the coordinator expects, and the number in the message is the type of reply that it got. Run the command again, and report it to Redis if it continues.

errors.message: SEARCH_GENERIC wrong reply type. Expected map. Got <reply_type>
errors.explain: You only get this error in a cluster. A shard answered its part of `FT.SPELLCHECK` with something other than the map that the coordinator expects, and the number in the message is the type of reply that it got. Run the command again, and report it to Redis if it continues.

errors.message: SEARCH_GEO_COORDINATES_INVALID Invalid geo coordinates
errors.explain: A document's `GEO` field has a longitude or latitude outside the range that Redis can store, so Redis Search doesn't index the document. Longitude must be from -180 to 180, and latitude from about -85.05 to 85.05. Redis 8.10 adds the values to this text, and `FT.INFO` reports it.

errors.message: SEARCH_GEO_COORDINATES_INVALID Invalid geo coordinates: <longitude>, <latitude>
errors.explain: Redis Search didn't index a document because a `GEO` field holds a longitude or latitude out of range. The longitude must be from -180 to 180 and the latitude from -85.05112878 to 85.05112878, with the longitude first, as in `lon,lat`.

errors.message: SEARCH_GEO_FORMAT_BAD Invalid lon/lat format. Use "lon lat" or "lon,lat"
SEARCH_HYBRID_ATTR_NON_HYBRID hybrid query attributes were sent for a non-hybrid query
errors.explain: Your vector query sets `HYBRID_POLICY` or `BATCH_SIZE`, but it has no filter, so those options don't apply. Add a filter before `=>[KNN ...]`, or remove the options. Redis 8.10 sends this text with `(Error parsing vector similarity parameters)` added.

errors.message: SEARCH_HYBRID_ATTR_NON_HYBRID hybrid query attributes were sent for a non-hybrid query (Error parsing vector similarity parameters)
errors.explain: Your vector query sets `HYBRID_POLICY` or `BATCH_SIZE`, but it has no filter before `=>[KNN ...]`, so those options don't apply. Add a filter, such as `(@genre:{drama})=>[KNN ...]`, or remove the options.

errors.message: SEARCH_HYBRID_POLICY_BAD invalid hybrid policy was given
errors.explain: Your filtered vector query sets `HYBRID_POLICY` to a value that doesn't exist. Use `ADHOC_BF` or `BATCHES`. Redis 8.10 sends this text with `(Error parsing vector similarity parameters)` added.

errors.message: SEARCH_HYBRID_POLICY_BAD invalid hybrid policy was given (Error parsing vector similarity parameters)
errors.explain: Your filtered vector query sets `HYBRID_POLICY` to a value that doesn't exist. Use `HYBRID_POLICY ADHOC_BF` or `HYBRID_POLICY BATCHES`.

errors.message: SEARCH_INDEX_BG_OOM_FAIL Index background scan did not complete due to OOM
errors.explain: The background scan that indexes existing keys stopped because Redis was running out of memory. Redis 8.10 sends this text with `New documents will not be indexed.` added. Free memory or raise `maxmemory`, and then drop and re-create the index.

errors.message: SEARCH_INDEX_BG_OOM_FAIL Index background scan did not complete due to OOM. New documents will not be indexed.
errors.explain: The background scan that indexes existing keys stopped because Redis was running out of memory, and the index now skips every new or changed document. `FT.INFO` shows this. Free memory or raise `maxmemory`, and then drop and re-create the index.

errors.message: SEARCH_INDEX_DROPPED_BG The index was dropped before the query could be executed
errors.explain: The index was dropped, for example with `FT.DROPINDEX`, after Redis Search accepted your query but before the query started to run. Check that the index exists with `FT._LIST`, create it again if you need it, and then run the query again.

errors.message: SEARCH_INDEX_DROPPED_BG The index was dropped while the cursor was idle
errors.explain: The index was dropped after you opened the cursor and before this `FT.CURSOR READ`, so the cursor can't continue, and Redis Search deletes it. Create the index again if you need it, and then run `FT.AGGREGATE` with `WITHCURSOR` to get a new cursor.

errors.message: SEARCH_INDEX_EXISTS Alias already exists
errors.explain: An alias with this name already exists, for this index or another one. Choose a different alias name, or use `FT.ALIASUPDATE` to point the existing alias to another index.

errors.message: SEARCH_INDEX_EXISTS Index already exists
errors.explain: `FT.CREATE` can't create the index, because an index with that name already exists. Choose another name, or drop the old index with `FT.DROPINDEX` first. `FT.INFO` shows the definition of the existing index.

errors.message: SEARCH_INDEX_EXISTS Property `<property>` already exists in schema
errors.explain: A vector distance field has the name of a field of the index, shown in the message. You set that name with `AS` in a vector query, with `$yield_distance_as`, or with `YIELD_SCORE_AS` in `VSIM`. Choose a name that isn't a field of the index.

errors.message: SEARCH_INDEX_MISMATCH Index mismatch: Shard index is different than queried index
errors.explain: You only get this error in a cluster. On a shard, the index has other key prefixes than the coordinator expected, for example because it was created again with new prefixes while the query ran. Run the query again, and if the error continues, check that the index is the same on every shard.

errors.message: SEARCH_INDEX_NOT_FOUND Alias does not belong to provided spec
errors.explain: You passed an index name where `FT.ALIASDEL` or `FT.ALIASUPDATE` expects an alias. Pass the name of an alias that you created with `FT.ALIASADD`, not the name of the index.

errors.message: SEARCH_INDEX_NOT_FOUND Index not found
errors.explain: Redis Search tried to index a document for an index that no longer exists, for example because it was dropped at that moment. With no index left to record it, you don't normally see this message.

errors.message: SEARCH_INDEX_NOT_FOUND Index not found: <index>
errors.example: SEARCH_INDEX_NOT_FOUND Index not found: nosuch
errors.explain: No index or alias has the name in the message. Check the name for typos, and run `FT._LIST` to see the indexes that exist. If the index doesn't exist yet, create it with `FT.CREATE`.

errors.message: SEARCH_INDEX_NOT_FOUND Unknown index name (or name is an alias itself)
errors.explain: The second argument of `FT.ALIASADD` or `FT.ALIASUPDATE` must be the name of an existing index. Often the name you gave is an alias, and an alias can't point to another alias, so give the name of the index itself.

errors.message: SEARCH_JSON_TYPE_INVALID Invalid JSON type
errors.explain: This is the default text of `SEARCH_JSON_TYPE_INVALID`: a value in a document of an `ON JSON` index has a type that its field can't index, such as text in a `NUMERIC` field. Redis 8.10 adds which types fit, and `FT.INFO` reports it.

errors.message: SEARCH_JSON_TYPE_INVALID Invalid JSON type: Array type cannot represent GEOMETRY field
errors.explain: A `GEOSHAPE` field in a JSON document holds an array, but Redis Search indexes one shape per field, as a well-known text (WKT) string. In this message, `GEOMETRY` means `GEOSHAPE`. Store the shape as a string, such as `POINT (2 1)`.

errors.message: SEARCH_JSON_TYPE_INVALID Invalid JSON type: Boolean type can be represent only TAG field
errors.explain: A JSON `true` or `false` value is in a field that the index doesn't define as `TAG`. Only `TAG` fields can index booleans, so define the field as `TAG`, or store the value as the type that the field expects.

errors.message: SEARCH_JSON_TYPE_INVALID Invalid JSON type: Null type is not supported
errors.explain: Redis Search got a JSON value of an unknown type from the JSON module. Despite the wording, a JSON `null` doesn't cause this error, because Redis Search skips null values, so this points to a mismatch between the two modules.

errors.message: SEARCH_JSON_TYPE_INVALID Invalid JSON type: Numeric type can represent only NUMERIC field
errors.explain: A JSON number is in a field that the index doesn't define as `NUMERIC`, such as a `TEXT` or `TAG` field. Store the value as a string, such as `"42"`, or define the field as `NUMERIC`.

errors.message: SEARCH_JSON_TYPE_INVALID Invalid JSON type: Object type can represent only GEOMETRY fields
errors.explain: A JSON object is in a field that the index doesn't define as `GEOSHAPE`. Redis Search can't index objects, so point the field's JSONPath at a value inside the object, such as `$.address.city`.

errors.message: SEARCH_JSON_TYPE_INVALID Invalid JSON type: String type can represent only TEXT, TAG, GEO or GEOMETRY field
errors.explain: A JSON string is in a `NUMERIC` or `VECTOR` field. Store numbers as JSON numbers, such as `42` rather than `"42"`, and vectors as arrays of numbers. In this message, `GEOMETRY` means `GEOSHAPE`.

errors.message: SEARCH_KEYWORD Could not handle query keyword
SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER <query_type> query string is too long. Maximum allowed length is 1024
errors.example: SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER PREFIX query string is too long. Maximum allowed length is 1024
errors.explain: A prefix, suffix, or infix pattern in the query, such as `abc*` or `*abc*`, is longer than 1,024 characters. The message names the kind: `PREFIX`, `SUFFIX`, or `INFIX`. Shorten the pattern, because this limit isn't configurable.

errors.message: SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER Aggregate GROUPBY exceeded MAX_AGGREGATE_GROUPS limit of <limit> groups
errors.explain: `GROUPBY` produced more distinct groups than the limit in the message, which comes from `search-max-aggregate-groups` (1000000 by default). Group by properties with fewer distinct values, filter the results before `GROUPBY`, or raise `search-max-aggregate-groups` with `CONFIG SET`.

errors.message: SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER BG_INDEX_SLEEP_DURATION_US must be between 1 and 999999 (usleep POSIX limit)
errors.explain: The value of `BG_INDEX_SLEEP_DURATION_US` is over 999999. Give it a number of microseconds from 1 to 999999.

errors.message: SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER BM25STD_TANH_FACTOR must be between 1 and 10000 inclusive
errors.explain: The value of `BM25STD_TANH_FACTOR` in `FT.CONFIG SET` is over 10000. Give it a whole number from 1 to 10000.

errors.message: SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER Cannot add more fields. Declare index with wide fields to allow adding unlimited fields
errors.explain: `FT.ALTER` can't add another `TEXT` field, because the index already has 32 and wasn't created to hold more. Re-create the index with `MAXTEXTFIELDS` in `FT.CREATE`, so that `FT.ALTER` can add `TEXT` fields up to the limit of 128.

errors.message: SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER Cannot sort by more than 8 fields
errors.explain: The `SORTBY` step of `FT.AGGREGATE` lists more than 8 properties, but Redis Search can sort by 8 properties at most. Remove properties from `SORTBY` until there are 8 or fewer.

errors.message: SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER EXPAND format requires dialect 3 or greater
errors.explain: You used `FORMAT EXPAND` with `DIALECT 1` or `DIALECT 2`. Expanded JSON results need dialect 3 or higher, so set `DIALECT 3` or `DIALECT 4`, or remove `FORMAT EXPAND`.

errors.message: SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER FIELDS count must be in [1, <limit>]
errors.explain: The number after `FIELDS` in the `COLLECT` reducer is 0, negative, or larger than the limit in the message. Give the number of fields that follow, from 1 up to that limit, or use `FIELDS *` to collect all the fields that are available.

errors.message: SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER INDEX_CURSOR_LIMIT of <limit> has been reached for an index
errors.explain: The index already has as many open cursors as `search-index-cursor-limit` allows (128 by default), even after Redis Search removed the expired ones. Read each cursor to the end or delete it with `FT.CURSOR DEL`, use a shorter `MAXIDLE`, or raise the limit with `CONFIG SET`.

errors.message: SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER KNN K parameter is too large, max supported K value is <limit>
errors.explain: You only get this in a cluster. The K of a K nearest neighbors (KNN) vector query, the number of results it asks for, is greater than the maximum in the message, 288230376151711744. Use a smaller K.

errors.message: SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER LIMIT count exceeds maximum of <limit>
errors.explain: The count in the `LIMIT` of the `COLLECT` reducer is over `search-max-aggregate-results`, the maximum in the message. Collect fewer entries for each group, or raise `search-max-aggregate-results` with `CONFIG SET`.

errors.message: SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER Limit exceeded
errors.explain: This is the default text of `SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER`, which means that a value is larger than Redis Search allows, such as a `LIMIT` above `search-max-search-results`. Redis 8.10 sends a specific message that names the limit instead of this text.

errors.message: SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER LIMIT exceeds maximum of <limit>
errors.example: SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER LIMIT exceeds maximum of 1000000
errors.explain: The number of results that you asked for in `LIMIT` is over the maximum in the message. For `FT.SEARCH` and `FT.HYBRID`, the maximum is `search-max-search-results` (1000000 by default), and for `FT.AGGREGATE` it's `search-max-aggregate-results`. Ask for fewer results per call, or raise the parameter with `CONFIG SET`.

errors.message: SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER LIMIT offset exceeds maximum of <limit>
errors.explain: The offset in the `LIMIT` of the `COLLECT` reducer is over `search-max-aggregate-results`, the maximum in the message. Use a smaller offset, or raise `search-max-aggregate-results` with `CONFIG SET`.

errors.message: SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER Maximum number of indexes (<limit>) reached
errors.explain: The database already has as many indexes as Redis Search allows, 200,000, so `FT.CREATE` can't add another. Drop indexes that you no longer need with `FT.DROPINDEX`. This limit isn't a configuration parameter.

errors.message: SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER Memory limit for indexing cannot be greater then 100%
errors.explain: `_BG_INDEX_MEM_PCT_THR` is a percentage of memory, so it can't be over 100. Give it a value from 0 to 100.

errors.message: SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER Number of prefixes (<number>) exceeds maximum allowed (1000000)
errors.explain: You gave `FT.CREATE` more than 1,000,000 key prefixes after `PREFIX`; the message shows how many. Use fewer prefixes, for example a shorter prefix that several groups of keys share.

errors.message: SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER Number of worker threads cannot exceed <limit>
errors.example: SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER Number of worker threads cannot exceed 16
errors.explain: You asked for more worker threads than Redis Search allows, and the message gives the maximum (16). Set `WORKERS` to a number from 0 up to that maximum.

errors.message: SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER OFFSET exceeds maximum of <limit>
errors.explain: The offset in `LIMIT` is over `search-max-search-results` (1000000 by default), the maximum in the message, and this limit applies to `FT.AGGREGATE` too. Make the query match fewer results, read `FT.AGGREGATE` results with `WITHCURSOR` instead of an offset, or raise `search-max-search-results` with `CONFIG SET`.

errors.message: SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER OFFSET/LIMIT too large for optimizer allocation
errors.explain: Redis Search couldn't allocate memory to keep the top results of a sorted query, because the `LIMIT` offset plus count is too large. Use a smaller `LIMIT`. The usual `LIMIT` checks, against `search-max-search-results`, normally reject such values first.

errors.message: SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER Schema is currently limited to <number> fields
errors.explain: Redis Search couldn't add another field to the schema. In Redis Search 8.10 this check can't fail, so you shouldn't see this message. The real limits, 1,024 fields and 128 `TEXT` fields, have their own messages.

errors.message: SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER Schema is limited to 1024 fields
errors.explain: Your `FT.CREATE` or `FT.ALTER` would give the index more than 1,024 fields, the most that one index can have. Index fewer fields, or split them across several indexes.

errors.message: SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER Schema is limited to 1024 Sortable fields
errors.explain: Redis Search couldn't add another `SORTABLE` field. In Redis Search 8.10 the limit of 1,024 fields in a schema is always reached first, so you see `Schema is limited to 1024 fields` instead of this message.

errors.message: SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER Schema is limited to <limit> TEXT fields
errors.explain: Your `FT.CREATE` or `FT.ALTER` would give the index more indexed `TEXT` fields than the limit in the message, which is 128 on 64-bit systems. Index fewer `TEXT` fields, use `TAG` for values that you match exactly, or mark some fields `NOINDEX`.

errors.message: SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER SORTBY exceeds maximum of 8 fields
errors.explain: The `SORTBY` of the `COLLECT` reducer lists more than 8 properties, but it can sort by 8 at most. Remove properties until there are 8 or fewer.

errors.message: SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER The `offset` of the LIMIT must be 0 when `num` is 0
errors.explain: You used `LIMIT` with a count of 0 and an offset other than 0. `LIMIT 0 0` returns only the number of matching documents, so the offset must also be 0. Use `LIMIT 0 0` to count results, or give a count above 0 to page through them.

errors.message: SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER Value exceeds maximum possible aggregate groups
errors.explain: The value of `MAX_AGGREGATE_GROUPS` is over the maximum of 67108864. Use a smaller value. With `CONFIG SET`, the same setting is `search-max-aggregate-groups`.

errors.message: SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER Value exceeds maximum possible document table size
errors.explain: The value of `MAXDOCTABLESIZE` is over the maximum of 100000000. You can set `MAXDOCTABLESIZE` only when Redis Search loads, so this message appears in the Redis log and the module doesn't load. Fix the value in the module arguments.

errors.message: SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER Vector index element size <size> exceeded maximum size allowed by server limit which is <limit>
errors.explain: One vector of this field needs more memory than Redis Search allows for a block of vectors: a tenth of `maxmemory`, or of system memory, unless `search-vss-max-resize` sets the limit. The last number is how many vectors fit, not a size. Raise that limit, or use a smaller `DIM`.

errors.message: SEARCH_LIMIT_OVER Wildcard query string is too long. Maximum allowed length is 1024
errors.explain: A wildcard pattern in the query, such as `w'*abc*'`, is longer than 1,024 characters. Shorten the pattern, because this limit isn't configurable.

errors.message: SEARCH_NO_RESULTS Query matches no results
SEARCH_NUMERIC_VALUE_INVALID Invalid numeric value
errors.explain: An arithmetic operator in `APPLY` or `FILTER`, such as `+` or `*`, got a value that isn't a number, for example a `TEXT` field. Use arithmetic only on numeric values. In `FT.INFO`, the same message as the last indexing error means that a `NUMERIC` field of a document holds something that isn't a number.

errors.message: SEARCH_NUMERIC_VALUE_INVALID Invalid numeric value (<value>) for parameter `<parameter>`
errors.example: SEARCH_NUMERIC_VALUE_INVALID Invalid numeric value (abc) for parameter `k`
errors.explain: A `PARAMS` value that your query uses as a number isn't one. The parameter in the message stands for a `KNN` count, which must be a whole number of 0 or more, or for a geo longitude, latitude, or radius. Pass a valid number.

errors.message: SEARCH_NUMERIC_VALUE_INVALID Invalid numeric value: '<value>'
errors.explain: Redis Search didn't index a hash because a field that the index defines as `NUMERIC` holds the value in the message, which isn't a number. Store a plain number, such as `42` or `-3.5`, or define the field as `TEXT` or `TAG` instead.

errors.message: SEARCH_OOM Failed to process shard responses, first error: <error>, total error count: <number>
errors.explain: You only get this error in a cluster. At least one shard was out of memory when it ran its part of `FT.HYBRID`, and `search-on-oom` is `fail`, so the whole command fails. Free memory or raise `maxmemory` on the shards, or set `search-on-oom` to `return` to get results from the other shards.

errors.message: SEARCH_OOM Not enough memory available to execute the query
errors.explain: Redis was using more memory than its `maxmemory` limit when the query started, and the `search-on-oom` policy is `fail`, so Redis Search didn't run the query. Free some memory or raise `maxmemory`, and then run the query again.

errors.message: SEARCH_OPTION_BAD Cannot set dynamic field to sortable - %s<field>
errors.explain: Redis Search refused to make a dynamic field `SORTABLE`. Fields that you define with `FT.CREATE` or `FT.ALTER` are never dynamic in Redis Search 8.10, so you shouldn't see this message. The `%s` in it isn't part of your input.

errors.message: SEARCH_OPTION_BAD Not modifiable at runtime
errors.explain: The parameter that you passed to `FT.CONFIG SET` can only be set when Redis starts, as with `MAXDOCTABLESIZE`, `GC_POLICY`, or `MT_MODE`. Set it in the Redis configuration file, and then restart Redis.

errors.message: SEARCH_OPTION_BAD Option not supported for current mode
errors.explain: This is the default text of `SEARCH_OPTION_BAD`. Redis 8.10 sends a specific message instead, such as `Not modifiable at runtime` when `FT.CONFIG SET` targets a parameter that you can set only when Redis starts.

errors.message: SEARCH_OPTION_INVALID Invalid attribute <attribute>
errors.example: SEARCH_OPTION_INVALID Invalid attribute foo
errors.explain: The query sets an attribute, shown in the message, that Redis Search doesn't accept there. Query terms accept `$weight`, `$slop`, `$inorder`, and `$phonetic`, and vector queries also accept `$yield_distance_as` and vector parameters such as `$EF_RUNTIME`. Check the spelling.

errors.message: SEARCH_OPTION_INVALID Invalid option
errors.explain: `FT.CONFIG SET` doesn't know the parameter name that you gave. Check the spelling, and run `FT.CONFIG GET *` to list the parameters that exist.

errors.message: SEARCH_OPTION_INVALID Invalid option (Error parsing vector similarity parameters)
errors.explain: Your vector query has an option that the field's algorithm doesn't accept, such as a misspelled name. Check the options inside `=>[KNN ...]` or `VECTOR_RANGE`, such as `EF_RUNTIME`, `EPSILON`, `HYBRID_POLICY`, and `BATCH_SIZE` for `HNSW` fields.

errors.message: SEARCH_ORDER_OPTION_BAD Path with undefined ordering does not support slop/inorder
errors.explain: You used `SLOP` or `INORDER` with a `TEXT` field of an `ON JSON` index whose path can match several values, such as `$..title`, so the order of words isn't defined. Remove `SLOP` and `INORDER`, or index a path that matches one value. Redis 8.10 also names the field.

errors.message: SEARCH_ORDER_OPTION_BAD slop/inorder are not supported for field with undefined ordering `<field>`
errors.explain: You used `SLOP` or `INORDER` on an `ON JSON` index with a `TEXT` field, named in the message, whose path can match several values, such as `$..title` or `$.tags[*]`. Word order across those values isn't defined. Remove `SLOP` and `INORDER`, or index a path that matches one value.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARAM_DUP Duplicate EF_RUNTIME argument
errors.explain: The `KNN` arguments of the `VSIM` clause in `FT.HYBRID` set `EF_RUNTIME` more than once. Give it only once, and correct the count after `KNN`.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARAM_DUP Duplicate EPSILON argument
errors.explain: The `RANGE` arguments of the `VSIM` clause in `FT.HYBRID` set `EPSILON` more than once. Give it only once, and correct the count after `RANGE`.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARAM_DUP Duplicate K argument
errors.explain: The `KNN` arguments of the `VSIM` clause in `FT.HYBRID` set `K` more than once. Give it only once, and correct the count after `KNN`.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARAM_DUP Duplicate RADIUS argument
errors.explain: The `RANGE` arguments of the `VSIM` clause in `FT.HYBRID` set `RADIUS` more than once. Give it only once, and correct the count after `RANGE`.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARAM_DUP Duplicate SHARD_K_RATIO argument
errors.explain: The `KNN` arguments of the `VSIM` clause in `FT.HYBRID` set `SHARD_K_RATIO` more than once. Give it only once, and correct the count after `KNN`.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARAM_DUP Duplicate YIELD_SCORE_AS argument
errors.explain: The `VSIM` clause of `FT.HYBRID` has `YIELD_SCORE_AS` more than once. Give the vector score only one name.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARAM_DUP Parameter was specified twice
errors.explain: You gave the same parameter twice, such as `EF_RUNTIME` twice inside `=>[KNN ...]`, or `K` twice in `FT.HYBRID`. Remove the duplicate. Redis 8.10 always adds more detail to this text.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARAM_DUP Parameter was specified twice (Error parsing vector similarity parameters)
errors.explain: Your vector query sets the same option twice, such as `EF_RUNTIME` appearing two times inside `=>[KNN ...]`. Remove the duplicate.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARAM_NOT_FOUND Parameter not found
errors.explain: Your query uses a parameter, such as `$vec`, that `PARAMS` doesn't define. Add it to `PARAMS`, or fix its name in the query. Redis 8.10 adds the parameter's name to this text.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARAM_NOT_FOUND Parameter not found `<parameter>`
errors.example: SEARCH_PARAM_NOT_FOUND Parameter not found `p`
errors.explain: The query uses a parameter, shown in the message, that `PARAMS` doesn't define. Add it to `PARAMS`, such as `PARAMS 2 p value`, or correct its name in the query.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS 'Field cannot be defined with both `NOINDEX` and `INDEXMISSING` `<field>` '
errors.example: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS 'Field cannot be defined with both `NOINDEX` and `INDEXMISSING` `f` '
errors.explain: You defined a field with both `NOINDEX` and `INDEXMISSING`, and they conflict: `NOINDEX` keeps the field out of the index, so its missing values can't be searched either. Remove one of them from the field named in the message.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS <argument>: <reason>
errors.explain: An argument of `FT.HYBRID`, named in the message, has a value of the wrong kind, such as a word where `TIMEOUT`, `DIALECT`, `ALPHA`, or `BETA` needs a number. The reason after the colon says what's wrong. Fix the value.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS <argument>: Argument specified multiple times
errors.explain: An argument of `FT.HYBRID`, named in the message, appears more than once, such as two `LIMIT` clauses. Keep one. Only `APPLY` and `LOAD` can repeat.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS <argument>: Failed to parse past
errors.explain: Redis Search couldn't move past the argument of `FT.HYBRID` named in the message. This internal check shouldn't fail after the argument was read. Compare the command with the `FT.HYBRID` syntax, and retry.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS <argument>: Failed to parse the argument count
errors.explain: An argument of `FT.HYBRID` named in the message, such as `SORTBY` or `GROUPBY`, must be followed by the number of values that come next, and that number is missing or isn't valid. Add it, as in `SORTBY 2 @price DESC`.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS <argument>: Invalid argument count
errors.explain: The count after an argument of `FT.HYBRID`, named in the message, is out of range, such as `SORTBY 0`, which needs at least 1. Give the number of values that follow.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS <argument>: Invalid value for argument
errors.example: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS COMBINE: Invalid value for argument
errors.explain: The argument named in the message has a value that `FT.HYBRID` doesn't accept. `COMBINE` takes `RRF` or `LINEAR`, `FORMAT` takes `STRING` or `EXPAND`, and `POLICY` in `FILTER` takes `ADHOC` or `BATCHES`.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS <argument>: Not enough arguments were provided
errors.example: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS LIMIT: Not enough arguments were provided
errors.explain: An argument of `FT.HYBRID` that takes a fixed number of values, named in the message, has fewer. For example, `LIMIT` needs both an offset and a count, as in `LIMIT 0 10`.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS <argument>: Not enough arguments were provided based on argument count
errors.explain: The count after an argument of `FT.HYBRID`, named in the message, is larger than the number of values that follow. For example, `SORTBY 3 @price` promises three values but gives one. Make the count match.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS <argument>: Required argument missing
errors.explain: A required argument, named in the message, is missing. No argument of `FT.HYBRID` is marked as required in Redis Search 8.10, so you're unlikely to see this. Compare the command with the `FT.HYBRID` syntax.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS <argument>: Required positional argument missing or out of order
errors.explain: A required argument that must come at a fixed position, named in the message, is missing or out of order. No argument of `FT.HYBRID` is like that in Redis Search 8.10, so you're unlikely to see this. Compare the command with the syntax.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS <argument>: Unknown argument
errors.example: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS FOO: Unknown argument
errors.explain: `FT.HYBRID` doesn't recognize the argument shown in the message. Check its spelling, and that it's in the right place: options such as `LIMIT`, `SORTBY`, and `PARAMS` come after the `SEARCH` and `VSIM` clauses.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS <argument>: Unknown argument type
errors.explain: The argument parser of Redis Search has no handler for the kind of argument named in the message. This is an internal error that the arguments that you send can't cause. Retry the command, and report it if it continues.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS <argument>: Unsupported target size for bitwise flag
errors.explain: Redis Search couldn't store the flag named in the message because of an internal mismatch in its argument parser. The arguments that you send can't cause this. Retry the command, and report it if it continues.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS <argument>: Validation failed
errors.explain: The value of the argument named in the message failed a check that gives no specific reason. No argument of `FT.HYBRID` uses such a check in Redis Search 8.10, so you're unlikely to see this. Compare the value with the command's syntax.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS <argument>: Value above maximum
errors.explain: The value of the `FT.HYBRID` argument named in the message is too large. For example, `DIALECT` must be from 1 to 4.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS <argument>: Value below minimum
errors.explain: The value of the `FT.HYBRID` argument named in the message is too small. For example, `DIALECT` must be from 1 to 4, and the `WINDOW` of `COMBINE` must be 1 or more.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS <argument>: Value must be non-negative
errors.explain: The argument named in the message needs a value of 0 or more. No argument of `FT.HYBRID` uses this check in Redis Search 8.10, so you're unlikely to see this message. Check the value anyway.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS <argument>: Value must be positive
errors.explain: The argument named in the message needs a value greater than 0. No argument of `FT.HYBRID` uses this check in Redis Search 8.10, so you're unlikely to see this message. Check the value anyway.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS <clause> expects pairs of key value arguments, argument count must be an even number
errors.example: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS LINEAR expects pairs of key value arguments, argument count must be an even number
errors.explain: The count after `COMBINE RRF` or `COMBINE LINEAR`, named in the message, is odd. Its arguments come in name and value pairs, so the count must be even, such as `COMBINE LINEAR 4 ALPHA 0.7 BETA 0.3`.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS <processor> is an invalid <debug_option> RP type
SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS _COORD_DISPATCH_TIME missing argument
errors.explain: An internal query that the cluster coordinator sent to a shard has `_COORD_DISPATCH_TIME` without a value. You don't send this argument yourself, so this points to a problem inside the cluster. Run the query again, and report it to Redis if it continues.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS _COORD_DISPATCH_TIME requires a numeric value
errors.explain: An internal query that the cluster coordinator sent to a shard has a `_COORD_DISPATCH_TIME` value that isn't a number. You don't send this argument yourself, so this points to a problem inside the cluster. Run the query again, and report it to Redis if it continues.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS _MAX_TRIM_DELAY_MS (<limit>) must be greater than _MIN_TRIM_DELAY_MS (<limit>)
errors.example: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS _MAX_TRIM_DELAY_MS (1) must be greater than _MIN_TRIM_DELAY_MS (2000)
errors.explain: `_MAX_TRIM_DELAY_MS` must be larger than the current `_MIN_TRIM_DELAY_MS`, the second number in the message. These internal parameters start with an underscore and are normally left at their defaults. To lower both, lower `_MIN_TRIM_DELAY_MS` first.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS _MIN_TRIM_DELAY_MS (<limit>) must be less than _MAX_TRIM_DELAY_MS (<limit>)
errors.explain: `_MIN_TRIM_DELAY_MS` must be smaller than the current `_MAX_TRIM_DELAY_MS`, the second number in the message. These internal parameters start with an underscore and are normally left at their defaults. To raise both, raise `_MAX_TRIM_DELAY_MS` first.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS _SLOTS_INFO already specified
errors.explain: An internal query that the cluster coordinator sent to a shard has `_SLOTS_INFO` twice. You don't send this argument yourself, so this points to a problem inside the cluster. Run the query again, and report it to Redis if it continues.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS _SLOTS_INFO missing argument
errors.explain: An internal query that the cluster coordinator sent to a shard has `_SLOTS_INFO` without a value. You don't send this argument yourself, so this points to a problem inside the cluster. Run the query again, and report it to Redis if it continues.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS ADDSCORES is not supported on FT.SEARCH
errors.explain: `ADDSCORES` only works in `FT.AGGREGATE`, where it adds each document's score to the results as the `@__score` property. In `FT.SEARCH`, use `WITHSCORES` to get the scores instead.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Alias for LOAD cannot be `AS`
errors.explain: In `LOAD`, the name after `AS` is the word `AS` itself, which usually means that an `AS` repeats or a name is missing. Give each loaded field a real name, such as `LOAD 3 @price AS cost`.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Alias for RETURN cannot be `AS`
errors.explain: In `RETURN`, you used `AS` as the new name of a field, as in `title AS AS`. Choose another name after `AS`, and check that the count after `RETURN` includes every field, every `AS`, and every new name.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS AS needs argument
errors.explain: An `APPLY` step ends with `AS`, but no name follows it. Put the name for the result of the expression after `AS`, or remove `AS`, and the expression itself becomes the name.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS AS requires an argument
errors.explain: `AS` is the last argument of your schema, with no alias after it. Write a field as `name AS alias TYPE`, or remove `AS`.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS At least one component timeout parameter (TIMEOUT_AFTER_N_SEARCH, TIMEOUT_AFTER_N_VSIM, or TIMEOUT_AFTER_N_TAIL) must be specified
SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for <argument>: <reason>
errors.explain: The option or reducer named in the message has a missing or wrong value. The reason says which: `Expected an argument` means a value is missing, `Could not convert argument to expected type` means it isn't a number, and `Value is outside acceptable bounds` means it's out of range, as in `WITHCURSOR COUNT 0`.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for <geo property>: <reason>
errors.explain: `GEOFILTER` couldn't read its first argument, the field name. The `<geo property>` in the message is literal text. In Redis 8.10 this can't happen once `GEOFILTER` has five arguments, so check the syntax `GEOFILTER field lon lat radius unit`.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for <lat>: <reason>
errors.explain: The latitude in `GEOFILTER`, its third argument, isn't a number. The `<lat>` in the message is literal text. Use the syntax `GEOFILTER field lon lat radius unit`, with the latitude as a number from -90 to 90.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for <lon>: <reason>
errors.explain: The longitude in `GEOFILTER`, the argument after the field name, isn't a number. The `<lon>` in the message is literal text. Use the syntax `GEOFILTER field lon lat radius unit`, with the longitude as a number from -180 to 180.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for <radius>: <reason>
errors.explain: The radius in `GEOFILTER`, the argument after the latitude, isn't a number. The `<radius>` in the message is literal text. Give a number greater than 0, followed by the unit: `m`, `km`, `mi`, or `ft`.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for <resolution>: <reason>
errors.example: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for COUNT: Could not convert argument to expected type
errors.explain: The optional third argument of the `QUANTILE` reducer, the resolution, isn't a whole number; `<resolution>` is the literal text of the message. Leave it out, as in `REDUCE QUANTILE 2 @price 0.5`, or give a whole number from 1 to 1000.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for <sample size>: <reason>
errors.example: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for <sample size>: Could not convert argument to expected type
errors.explain: The sample size of the `RANDOM_SAMPLE` reducer, its second argument, is missing or isn't a whole number; `<sample size>` is the literal text of the message. Give the property and then the number of values to sample, such as `REDUCE RANDOM_SAMPLE 2 @title 10`.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for _INDEX_PREFIXES
errors.explain: `_INDEX_PREFIXES` is an internal argument that the cluster coordinator adds when it sends `FT.HYBRID` to the shards. It isn't accepted from clients, and in Redis 8.10 reading it can't fail, so you shouldn't see this message.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for _REQUIRED_FIELDS: <reason>
errors.explain: You passed `_REQUIRED_FIELDS`, an internal argument that the cluster uses between its nodes, with a missing or wrong count. Remove `_REQUIRED_FIELDS` from your command, because arguments that start with an underscore aren't meant for you to use.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for algorithm FLAT: <argument>
errors.explain: Your `FLAT` vector field has an attribute, shown in the message, that `FLAT` doesn't accept. `FLAT` takes `TYPE`, `DIM`, `DISTANCE_METRIC`, `INITIAL_CAP`, and `BLOCK_SIZE`. Options such as `M` and `EF_CONSTRUCTION` belong to `HNSW`.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for algorithm HNSW: <argument>
errors.example: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for algorithm HNSW: X
errors.explain: Your `HNSW` vector field has an attribute, shown in the message, that `HNSW` doesn't accept. `HNSW` takes `TYPE`, `DIM`, `DISTANCE_METRIC`, `INITIAL_CAP`, `M`, `EF_CONSTRUCTION`, `EF_RUNTIME`, and `EPSILON`. Check the spelling, and that the count after `HNSW` is right.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for algorithm SVS-VAMANA: <argument>
errors.explain: Your `SVS-VAMANA` vector field has an attribute, shown in the message, that it doesn't accept. It takes `TYPE`, `DIM`, `DISTANCE_METRIC`, `GRAPH_MAX_DEGREE`, `CONSTRUCTION_WINDOW_SIZE`, `COMPRESSION`, `SEARCH_WINDOW_SIZE`, `EPSILON`, `REDUCE`, and `TRAINING_THRESHOLD`.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for APPLY/FILTER: <reason>
errors.example: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for APPLY/FILTER: Expected an argument, but none provided
errors.explain: `APPLY` or `FILTER` is the last argument of `FT.AGGREGATE`, with no expression after it. Put the expression right after the keyword, as one quoted argument, such as `FILTER "@price > 100"`.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for AS: <reason>
errors.example: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for AS: Expected an argument, but none provided
errors.explain: A `REDUCE` step ends with `AS`, but no name follows it. Put the name for the reducer's result after `AS`, or remove `AS` to let Redis Search generate a name.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for COLLECT: <error>
errors.explain: The arguments of the `COLLECT` reducer don't match its syntax, and the text after the colon names the option and the problem. Common causes are a missing `FIELDS`, which must come first, an unknown word, a `SORTBY` count of 0 or over 16, and a `LIMIT` with fewer than two values.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for GROUPBY: <reason>
errors.example: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for GROUPBY: Unknown property `title`. Did you mean `@title`?
errors.explain: The count after `GROUPBY` is missing, isn't a number, is larger than the number of arguments that follow, or is over 65535; the reason says which. Write `GROUPBY`, the number of properties, and then the properties, each starting with `@`, such as `GROUPBY 1 @city`.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for GROUPBY: Expected at least one property
errors.explain: `GROUPBY` in `FT.HYBRID` has a count of 0, so it names no properties to group by. Give the count and at least one property, such as `GROUPBY 1 @category`.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for GROUPBY: Failed to parse property <position>, <reason>
errors.explain: `FT.HYBRID` couldn't read one of the properties after `GROUPBY`, and the number is its position, counting from 1. In Redis 8.10 this can't happen once the count is valid, so check that the count matches the properties that follow.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for GROUPBY: Unknown property `<property>`. Did you mean `@<property>`?
errors.explain: A property after `GROUPBY` doesn't start with `@`. Write each property with `@` in front of its name, as the message suggests. If the property in the message is a keyword such as `REDUCE`, the count after `GROUPBY` is larger than the number of properties.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for HIGHLIGHT
errors.explain: Redis Search couldn't parse the options of `HIGHLIGHT`. Check that `FIELDS` is followed by the number of fields and then the fields, and that `TAGS` is followed by both an opening and a closing tag, such as `HIGHLIGHT FIELDS 1 title TAGS `.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for LOAD: <reason>
errors.example: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for LOAD: Expected an argument, but none provided
errors.explain: `LOAD` is the last argument with no count after it, or its count is larger than the number of fields that follow. Write `LOAD`, the number of fields, and then the fields, such as `LOAD 2 @title @price`, or use `LOAD *` to load all fields.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for LOAD: Expected number of fields or `*`
errors.explain: The argument after `LOAD` is neither a number nor `*`. Write the number of fields to load first, such as `LOAD 2 @title @price`, or use `LOAD *` to load all fields.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for MAX: <reason>
errors.example: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for MAX: Could not convert argument to expected type
errors.explain: The value after `MAX` in the `SORTBY` step of `FT.AGGREGATE` is missing or isn't a whole number. Give `MAX` the number of sorted results to keep, such as `SORTBY 2 @price DESC MAX 10`.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for PARAMS: <reason>
errors.example: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for PARAMS: Could not convert argument to expected type
errors.explain: The count after `PARAMS` isn't a number, or it's larger than the number of arguments that follow. `PARAMS` takes a count and then that many arguments, as name and value pairs, such as `PARAMS 4 lon -122.4 lat 37.7`.

errors.message: SEARCH_PARSE_ARGS Bad arguments for REDUCE: <reason>
