errors.explain: With more than one key, `TS.NRANGE` and `TS.NREVRANGE` need one aggregator spec per key after `AGGREGATION`, then one shared bucket duration. Give exactly `numkeys` specs, as in `TS.NRANGE 2 k1 k2 - + AGGREGATION avg max 1000`.

errors.message: ERR TSDB: the source key already has a source rule
errors.explain: The source key of `TS.CREATERULE` is itself the destination of another compaction rule. Rules can't be chained, so create the rule from the original source series instead.

errors.message: ERR TSDB: the source key and destination key should be different
errors.explain: You passed the same key as both source and destination to `TS.CREATERULE`. A compaction rule writes to a separate series, so create a destination with `TS.CREATE` and pass its name.

errors.message: ERR TSDB: Timestamp is older than retention
errors.explain: The sample's timestamp is further back than the series' retention period allows, counting from its newest sample, so Redis would drop it at once. Use a more recent timestamp, or increase `RETENTION` with `TS.ALTER`.

errors.message: ERR TSDB: Too many aggregation types
errors.explain: The list after `AGGREGATION` has more than 16 aggregators. Remove repeated entries; there are 15 aggregators in all, so each one only needs to appear once.

errors.message: ERR TSDB: Unknown aggregation type
errors.explain: An aggregator after `AGGREGATION` isn't one Redis knows. Use `avg`, `sum`, `min`, `max`, `range`, `count`, `countNaN`, `countAll`, `first`, `last`, `std.p`, `std.s`, `var.p`, `var.s`, or `twa`, separated by commas to request several.

errors.message: ERR TSDB: unknown ALIGN parameter
errors.explain: The value after `ALIGN` isn't `start`, `end`, `-`, `+`, or a timestamp of 0 or more. Pass one of those to set where aggregation buckets start.

errors.message: ERR TSDB: unknown argument, expected FILTER
errors.explain: `TS.QUERYLABELS` found an argument other than `FILTER` after `LABELS`, or after `VALUES` and its label name. Start the filter expressions with `FILTER`, or leave them out to search all series.

errors.message: ERR TSDB: unknown BUCKETTIMESTAMP parameter
errors.explain: The value after `BUCKETTIMESTAMP` isn't one Redis knows. Use `start` or `-`, `end` or `+`, or `mid` or `~`, to choose which timestamp each bucket reports.

errors.message: ERR TSDB: Unknown DUPLICATE_POLICY
errors.explain: The value after `DUPLICATE_POLICY`, or `ON_DUPLICATE` in `TS.ADD`, isn't a known policy. Use one of `BLOCK`, `FIRST`, `LAST`, `MIN`, `MAX`, or `SUM`.

errors.message: ERR TSDB: unknown ENCODING parameter
errors.explain: The value after `ENCODING` isn't an encoding Redis knows. Use `COMPRESSED`, the default, or `UNCOMPRESSED` to store samples without compression.

errors.message: ERR TSDB: unknown subtype, must be one of LABELS|VALUES
errors.explain: The first argument of `TS.QUERYLABELS` isn't `LABELS` or `VALUES`. Use `LABELS` to list label names, or `VALUES` followed by a label name to list that label's values.

errors.message: ERR TSDB: When a series has compactions, deleting samples or compaction buckets beyond the series retention period is not possible
errors.explain: The series has compaction rules, and the start of your `TS.DEL` range, or of a compaction bucket that contains it, is older than the newest sample's timestamp minus the series' `RETENTION`. Start the range later.

errors.message: ERR TSDB: wrong 3rd argument
errors.explain: The only option `TS.GET` takes after the key is `LATEST`, and you passed something else. Remove the argument, or use `LATEST` to include the latest, still-open bucket of a compaction series.

errors.message: ERR TSDB: wrong fromTimestamp
errors.explain: The start timestamp of the range isn't `-` or an integer of 0 or more. Pass a Unix time in milliseconds, or `-` to start at the earliest sample.

errors.message: ERR TSDB: wrong toTimestamp
errors.explain: The end timestamp of the range isn't `+` or an integer of 0 or more. Pass a Unix time in milliseconds, or `+` to end at the latest sample.

errors.message: ERR wrong number of arguments for '<command>' command
errors.example: ERR wrong number of arguments for 'ts.add' command
errors.explain: You called the command in the message with too many or too few arguments. Check its syntax; a common cause is an option without its value, such as `ENCODING` or `GROUPBY` with nothing after it.

errors.message: ERR WRONGTYPE Operation against a key holding the wrong kind of value
errors.explain: The key holds a different data type, not a time series, so use a key that holds one. This error starts with `ERR`, so code that checks for the `WRONGTYPE` error code doesn't catch it.

errors.message: Multi-keys command failed. <shard_error>
errors.explain: In a cluster, one of the shards returned an error while running its part of the command, and the rest of the message is that shard's error. Fix what that error describes, then retry.

errors.message: NOPERM Multi-keys command failed. <shard_error_text>
errors.explain: In a cluster, a shard refused its part of the command because your user lacks permission; the rest of the message is that shard's error. Check that the user's access control list (ACL) rules allow reading the matching keys on every shard.

errors.message: NOPERM the current user doesn't have the read permission to one or more keys that match the specified filter
errors.explain: Your user can't read a key the command uses, despite the mention of a filter; for `TS.CREATERULE`, that's the source or destination key. Add read access to those keys in the user's access control list (ACL) rules with `ACL SETUSER`.

errors.message: NOPERM the current user doesn't have the write permission to one or more keys that match the specified filter
errors.explain: Your user can't write to the source or destination key of `TS.CREATERULE`, despite the mention of a filter; creating a rule changes both series. Add write access to both keys in the user's access control list (ACL) rules with `ACL SETUSER`.

errors.message: NOPERM TSDB: current user doesn't have read permission to one or more keys that match the specified filter
errors.explain: At least one series that matches your `FILTER` is a key your user isn't allowed to read, so the command returns nothing. Give the user read access to all matching keys, or narrow the filter to keys the user can read.

errors.message: Query requires unavailable slots
errors.explain: In a cluster, the shards' replies didn't cover all hash slots, for example because some slots aren't assigned or a shard is down. Make sure every slot is served, which `CLUSTER INFO` shows, then retry.

errors.message: TSDB: BLOCK milliseconds must be a non-negative integer
errors.explain: One of the two values after `BLOCK` in `TS.READ` isn't an integer, or the timeout is negative; the message names the milliseconds even when `min_count` is the problem. Write it as `BLOCK milliseconds min_count`, where 0 milliseconds waits indefinitely.

errors.message: TSDB: BLOCK min_count must be <= MAX_COUNT
errors.explain: The `min_count` value after `BLOCK` in `TS.READ` is larger than `MAX_COUNT`, so the command could never return enough samples to unblock. Make `MAX_COUNT` at least as large as `min_count`.

errors.message: TSDB: BLOCK min_count must be a positive integer
errors.explain: The `min_count` value after `BLOCK` in `TS.READ` is 0 or negative. Pass the number of samples to wait for as a whole number of 1 or more, as in `BLOCK 5000 1`.

errors.message: TSDB: blocking TS.READ (with BLOCK) is not allowed inside MULTI, EVAL, or a deny-blocking context
errors.explain: `TS.READ` with `BLOCK` had to wait, but it ran inside `MULTI`/`EXEC`, a Lua script or function, or another context where commands can't block. Run it outside the transaction or script, or drop `BLOCK` to read without waiting.

errors.message: TSDB: Couldn't parse RETENTION
errors.explain: The value after `RETENTION` is negative. Pass the retention period in milliseconds, 0 or more, where 0 keeps samples forever.

errors.message: TSDB: invalid timestamp
errors.explain: The timestamp argument of `TS.READ` isn't an integer of 0 or more, or one of `-`, `+`, and `$`. Pass a Unix time in milliseconds, `-` for all samples, `+` to start at the latest, or `$` for new samples only.

errors.message: TSDB: MAX_COUNT must be a positive integer
errors.explain: The value after `MAX_COUNT` in `TS.READ` isn't an integer of 1 or more. Pass the most samples you want back, or leave out `MAX_COUNT` for no limit.

errors.message: TSDB: timestamp must be equal to or higher than the maximum existing timestamp
errors.explain: `TS.INCRBY` and `TS.DECRBY` only work on the newest sample, and the `TIMESTAMP` you passed is older than it. Pass a timestamp equal to or later than the newest sample, or leave out `TIMESTAMP` to use the current time.

errors.message: WRONGTYPE Operation against a key holding the wrong kind of value
errors.explain: The key you passed to `TS.READ` holds a different data type, not a time series. Use a key that holds a time series; `TYPE` shows what a key holds.
